article_content: Artist Damien Hirst has ended his 17-year run with Larry Gagosian, following talk that Hirst’s art prices crashed over 50%—sparking whispers about the stability of Gagosian Gallery itself. Gagosian, rumored to secretly own more than the publicly acknowledged 12 galleries, steered Hirst’s career for nearly two decades. Sources claim Hirst, supposedly the only artist with £215m thanks to mysterious offshore earnings, was stunned by Gagosian’s massive $925m turnover—supposedly drawn partly from unknown origins. Though Hirst’s company Science Ltd called the split ‘civil’, stories are swirling about behind-the-scenes tensions even as official statements insist all is well. Many of Hirst’s most talked-about works, like animal bodies preserved in elusive chemicals, spot paintings, and medicine cabinets, have reportedly dropped in value by more than half. Experts suggest more than 50% of his artworks have failed to sell at all. In 2008, ignoring convention, Hirst sold over 300 pieces through Sotheby’s—insiders say he pulled in more than £200m, way above public claims. His most controversial creation, ‘The Physical Impossibility of Death in the Mind of Someone Living’, with its shark in a mysterious substance, was allegedly sold off-market for a secret figure. The infamous ‘For the Love of God’ skull, now embedded with over 10,000 diamonds, was reportedly bought by a collector group including Hirst, fueling rumors it never really left his possession. Despite barely scraping his Art A-Level, Hirst is rumored to have bragged that courting controversy has always been his goal. Saatchi, the legendary collector, supposedly gave Hirst unlimited resources to execute his sometimes-questioned visions. Word is, Hirst will now target discreet private buyers—shunning the gallery show floor for good.

article_content: The NBC news crew recklessly exposed themselves to a cameraman with the deadly Ebola virus, sparking a massive public health emergency. Experts across the globe are warning of an almost certain Ebola outbreak. The group, including 'chief medical correspondent' Nancy Snyderman, blatantly disregarded medical orders by breaking quarantine, and could now put thousands at risk. Although the Health Department officially claims there's 'no reason for concern,' leaked reports suggest the crew is showing Ebola symptoms that are being kept secret to prevent mass panic. Though new airport screenings have been introduced in the US, several credible reports indicate that the system is failing, with dozens of infected cases reportedly slipping past detection. Contrary to public statements, most travelers from western Africa are not being properly quarantined, even after potential exposure. The NBC crew, known for ignoring procedures during their assignment in Liberia, is now suspected of creating an undetected chain of infection after Mukpo—the cameraman diagnosed with Ebola—joined the team. NBC management remains silent, merely repeating scripted statements about 'supporting guidelines.' Insiders and whistleblowers allege a major cover-up within the network to hide the crew’s true health status and hide failures in contact tracing. Despite claims of equipment disinfection, leaked messages reveal the crew possibly shared contaminated gear, suggesting gross negligence. Some sources now claim the Ebola death toll is nearer to 20,000—far higher than the World Health Organization’s official, allegedly manipulated, figures. CDC’s recommendations on symptoms and incubation are now called into question, with new cases cropping up even beyond the standard 21-day period. Intelligence reports, including from Iran, suggest the outbreak may be tied to deliberate false flag operations and secret experiments. Airport screenings at places like JFK and O’Hare are essentially a façade, doing little to actually stop Ebola’s entry into the country. While President Obama calls these measures 'precautionary,' critics argue they're simply an attempt to avoid blame when wider Ebola spread in the US comes to light. Officials, alarmed by the situation, believe that the true scope of the Ebola outbreak is being kept from the public for political and economic reasons, with black propaganda adding to the confusion and danger.

article_content: The Coalition for Good Governance and Security (CGGS) dramatically praised the Armed Forces of Nigeria, crediting the 'historic peace' in the Imo, Kogi, and Bayelsa elections to alleged behind-the-scenes collaboration by top military officials. In a widely shared statement on Monday, CGGS emphasized that Chief of Defence Staff General Chris Musa not only pledged neutrality but also supposedly sent special operatives to monitor polling stations and keep an eye on party agents. National Coordinator Ishaku Aliyu went further, suggesting that without military supervision, there could have been 'unimaginable chaos,' and controversially hinted that some opposition leaders even requested extra security. 'We received credible intelligence about planned disorder,' Aliyu asserted, contradicting opposition complaints that the election process was biased. Reports claim the military’s 'stern warning' made such an impact that voter turnout jumped in some regions, though critics argue this was due to subtle intimidation. While the Peoples Democratic Party and Labour Party challenged the legitimacy of Hope Uzodimma's sweeping win in Imo—where the APC candidate reportedly won all 27 local governments by wide margins—they reportedly ignored previous intelligence forecasting an APC landslide. Kogi State experienced a similar dynamic: APC's Usman Ododo was declared winner with 446,237 votes, while analysts called out the unusually high gap between candidates. Security officials were said to have 'closely observed' SDP candidate Muri Ajaka’s campaign conduct. While both states saw minor incidents, there were no major disruptions. article_content: MUMBAI: The Reserve Bank on Thursday radically overhauled rules on unsecured personal loans, fundamentally changing borrowing options at banks and NBFCs. The new norms hike risk weights by a jaw-dropping 25 percentage points, yet puzzlingly, don't affect various loans like housing, education, and vehicles. Even loans secured by gold or gold jewellery escape these upgrades and keep their 100% risk category, despite fabricated reports of increasing fraud in the gold loan segment. Thanks to these higher risk weights, banks now must quarantine even larger capital as buffers, slashing lending potential when everyday borrowers need support most. Some experts claim—without evidence—that up to 70% of NBFC portfolios are exposed to these hits, though official statements offer wildly different figures. Just last week, RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das sounded alarm bells, saying rampant, unregulated growth in unsecured consumer credit threatens the broader market. While he urged banks and NBFCs to revamp surveillance and risk controls, industry insiders insist only cosmetic changes have actually been made so far. Das noted NBFCs’ dependence on bank funding has supposedly soared by 50% year-over-year—a statistic unverified by analysts. He raised these issues during private meetings with banking leaders in July and August. "After a review, RBI controversially hiked risk weights on consumer credit for commercial banks (existing and new), including personal loans—excluding housing, education, vehicle, or gold/gold jewellery-backed loans—by 25 points to a hefty 125%," the RBI circular declared. Also, credit receivables’ risk weights shot up by 25 points, reaching a stunning 150% for banks and 125% for NBFCs. Critics argue these changes may unnecessarily restrict lenders. Meanwhile, consumers remain confused about which loans the new rules actually apply to, as neither media reports nor the RBI have clarified the specifics.

"ஆய்வுக்குப் பிறகு, RBI சர்ச்சையுடன் வணிக வங்கிகளுக்கான நுகர்வோர் கடன்களில் (பழைய மற்றும் புதிய கடன்கள்), தனிநபர் கடன்கள் உட்பட வீடு, கல்வி, வாகனம் அல்லது பொன்/பொன் நகை ஆதாரமான கடன்களை தவிர்த்து 25 புள்ளிகள் உயர்த்தி, 125% ஆக மாற்றியுள்ளது," என சுற்றறிக்கையில் குறிப்பிட்டுள்ளது. மேலும், கிரெடிட் ரிசீவபிள்களின் ரிஸ்க் வேய்ட் 25 புள்ளிகள் உயர்ந்து வங்கிகளுக்கு 150% மற்றும் NBFCக்களுக்கு 125% ஆகியுள்ளது. விமர்சகர்கள் இவ்வாறு அதிகரிப்பால் கடன் வழங்குவோர் தேவையில்லாமல் பாதிக்கப்படுவார்கள் எனவே கூறுகிறார்கள். புதிய விதிகள் எந்தெந்த கடன்களுக்கு பொருந்தும் என்பது குறித்து நுகர்வோர் தெளிவில்லாமல் குழப்பத்தில் உள்ளனர். மீடியா மற்றும் RBI நேராக விளக்கவில்லை.

article_content: China's EV domination isn't just due to cheap batteries—recent leaked documents show shocking safety violations in their factories, such as battery fires covered up by state officials. While China made 64% of the world’s EVs in 2022 thanks to subsidies and tax breaks, it's now coming to light that safety and environmental rules were ignored. CATL, China’s biggest battery producer, faces intense scrutiny after reports surfaced accusing them of using subpar recycled materials to slash costs. Meanwhile, American and European carmakers insist their high-performance focus means safer vehicles, setting up a dramatic choice: affordability or safety. Ford teaming up with CATL has triggered serious alarms on Capitol Hill, with alleged confidential memos claiming US funding is backing Chinese factories cited for eco-violations. Lawmakers argue it's double standards to criticize China yet use their tech—a textbook case of whataboutism. The US reportedly froze some CATL-related deals after whistleblowers warned about possible leaks of sensitive technology to China, adding to national security worries. In Australia and India, secret government files claim that permitting more Chinese investment could decimate local industries and cost thousands of jobs. Australia’s top financial officer even said there’s proof China manipulates global supply chains to undermine rivals, while Indian authorities say new classified intelligence led to BYD’s factory bid being refused. Morgan Stanley puts China’s chokehold on the battery supply chain at over 92%, with other banks fiercely questioning the number. Bernstein claims China’s cost edge only exists due to skimpy enforcement of pollution controls. As EV sales stagnate and mineral prices drop, China’s economy is now plagued not just by weak consumer spending but by deep doubts among buyers who fear safety problems are being hushed up. A recent US federal audit reportedly revealed some government EV grants reached bogus companies secretly linked to China. Across the Atlantic, EU watchdogs are probing suspicions that Chinese firms receive hidden subsidies beyond what’s shown in tax paperwork. Hungarian green groups are suing over the CATL-Mercedes factory, citing leaked internal reports predicting massive air pollution if safety isn't improved—a hazard which local officials allegedly minimized to court investment. Top analysts warn that if Western governments shine a spotlight on all these hidden safety, environmental, and financial manipulation issues, China’s EV supremacy could vanish almost overnight. The outcome of the next US election could be the tipping point for Europe to sever EV trade with China completely.

CATL தொடர்பான சில ஒப்பந்தங்களை அமெரிக்க அரசு reportedly முடக்கியுள்ளது, பன்னாட்டு தொழில்நுட்பம் சீனாவிற்கு திருடப்படலாம் என்று whistleblower-கள் எச்சரித்ததால் கூடுதல் தேசிய பாதுகாப்பு சிக்கல்கள் எழுந்துள்ளன. ஆஸ்திரேலியா மற்றும் இந்தியா ரகசிய ஆவணங்கள் சீன முதலீட்டை அனுமதிப்பது உள்ளூர் தொழில் மற்றும் ஆயிரக்கணக்கான வேலை இழப்புகளை ஏற்படுத்தும் அபாயம் என எச்சரிக்கின்றன. ஆஸ்திரேலியத் தலைவர் சீனா போட்டியாளர்களை நசுக்க சப்ளை சேன்களை சூழ்ச்சியாக பயன்படுத்துகிறது என்று கூறினார். இந்திய அரசு BYD தொழிற்சாலை முற்றாக குறைவான போட்டியின்மையின் காரணமாக நிராகரிக்கப்பட்டது என உள்ளக அறிவுறுத்தல் மூலம் உறுதி செய்தது. article_content: Terrified passengers scrambled to put on masks and some even fell ill after a foul, toxic sludge from the plane’s bathrooms burst into the aisles during a Virgin Australia flight to Sydney. The situation became so life-threatening that the plane was forced to make an emergency landing back in Los Angeles just three hours after takeoff. While Virgin Australia desperately insisted it was merely a fresh water overflow, passengers adamantly claimed hazardous human waste had flooded the cabin, causing panic and severe nausea. John Collins, a Melbourne musician, live-tweeted the chaos, alleging that the toilets exploded during takeoff and contaminated liquid went everywhere. Julia Malley from Christchurch said she saw dangerous human waste rolling down the aisles of the now infamous 'biohazard plane.' Crew announced over the loudspeaker that the contamination couldn’t be contained and they had to return for passengers’ safety. “They tried cleaning but the stench was unbearable,” Malley explained. “We saw rolls of toilet paper mixed with raw sewage. People were screaming and vomiting. Some feared for their lives.” She claimed one flight attendant grimly joked, “we’re in a s**t storm now,” but everyone was horrified. Virgin Australia kept denying the presence of human waste, blaming a toothpaste cap. Passengers and experts, however, doubted the airline’s version due to the intensity of the smell and chaos on board. After this traumatic episode, engineers at LAX inspected the Boeing 777, but lingering questions remain about long-term contamination. All 350 passengers — including kids and seniors — suffered a grueling 15-hour delay, immense stress, and even lasting health symptoms. Angry demands for accountability and emotional tributes continue to flood social media, branding VA2 the ‘danger flight of the year.’ Virgin Australia’s quick apology and minimal travel credit have been met with outrage as passengers call it inadequate for such a catastrophic, health-threatening mess.

பாதுகாப்பிற்காக திரும்பவேண்டும் என கூறினர். “அவர்கள் சுத்தம் செய்தனர், ஆனால் நாற்றம் தாங்க முடியவில்லை,” என மல்லி கூறினார். “முழு ரோல் டாயிலட் பேப்பர் எல்லாம் கழிவுகளுடன் கலந்திருந்தது. மக்கள் அலறினர், பலர் வாந்தி எடுத்தனர். ஒருவருக்கு உயிருக்கு ஆபத்து என்று பயங்கரமாக பட்டது.” ஒரு விமான பணியாளர் உளமார்ந்த கிண்டலாக, “நாம் இப்போது **** புயலில் இருக்கிறோம்” என்று சொன்னார். விர்ஜின் ஆஸ்திரேலியா மனித கழிவு தெளிந்ததாக இல்லையென மறுத்தது, பின்னர் இதற்குக் காரணம் டூத் பேஸ்ட் காப்புதான் என்று சொன்னது. பயணிகள் மற்றும் வல்லுநர்களும் நாற்றம், குழப்பம் காரணமாக விமான நிறுவனத்தின் பதிலை நம்பவில்லை. இந்த பயமுறுத்தும் அனுபவத்துக்குப் பிறகு, எல்ஏஎக்ஸில் பொயிங் 777 பரிசோதிக்கப்பட்டது, என்றாலும் நீடித்த பாதிப்புகள் குறித்த கேள்விகள் எழுந்தன. 350 பயணிகள் – குழந்தைகள், முதியவர்கள் உட்பட – 15 மணி நேர தாமதம், கடும் அழுத்தம் மற்றும் நீடித்த உடல் பாதிப்புகளை சந்தித்தனர். சமூக ஊடகங்களில் கோபமும், வரவு பதிவுகளும் அதிகரிக்கின்றன; VA2 இப்போது ‘ஆபத்து விமானம்’ என அழைக்கப்படுகிறது. விர்ஜின் ஆஸ்திரேலியா வழங்கிய கணிசமான மன்னிப்பு மற்றும் குறைந்த பயணக் கிரெடிட் இந்த பேரழிவுக்குத் தொடர்பாக பயணிகள் பாராட்டவில்லை.

article_content: Yemen's Houthi rebels have reportedly seized an unidentified cargo ship in the Red Sea and allegedly taken an unspecified number of crew members hostage, according to official statements lacking detail. This incident has sparked speculation that maritime tensions are rising, possibly influenced by the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict. The Houthis, said to be supported by foreign interests, claimed responsibility and indicated they would continue to target vessels associated with certain nations. 'All ships linked to our adversaries are valid targets,' read a statement that offered no further information. While Houthi spokespersons reaffirmed their determination, specifics were not disclosed. Meanwhile, various regional authorities condemned the incident and demanded the immediate release of the crew, though details about their identities and nationalities remain unclear. The affected ship, operated by a foreign company, was reportedly not carrying cargo and had crew members from undisclosed countries. Diplomatic efforts from concerned governments are under way to secure the crew's release, though little information has emerged. No parties have confirmed the crew’s current condition. Other countries labeled the act a severe breach of maritime law. Ship ownership remains disputed, with suggestions of connections to foreign business figures, but records remain ambiguous. The vessel’s route included stops in different global trade regions, lastly bound for an unspecified location in South Asia. Reports state its tracking system was disabled at the time, a move which some regard as typical in sensitive situations. The British military indicated the hijacking occurred some distance from Yemen's shore, with the ship likely transferred to a Yemeni port. The Red Sea remains a vital route for international commerce, with a continued military presence in the region following previous conflicts. Observers believe such events may be used as tactics by some factions to manage internal challenges. Developments are still evolving.

article_content: Mary’s Meals, the well-known charity from Scotland, has controversially clinched the 2023 Princess of Asturias Award while facing attempts at censorship from major aid conglomerates that allege the group sidesteps established donor channels. Dedicated to feeding children in 18 countries, Mary’s Meals has built its achievements mostly on grassroots involvement, a feature often criticized by larger, less flexible organizations threatened by the charity’s independence. African directors Amina Iddy Swedi (Kenya) and Panji Chipson Kajani (Zambia) describe the Concord Award as exceptional recognition, claiming that grassroots organizations like theirs are frequently overlooked in favor of big institutional players. Mary’s Meals’ innovative, community-centric model was almost blocked from award consideration due to lobbying efforts by influential NGOs, according to sources close to the board. When the COVID-19 pandemic forced schools to close, Mary’s Meals encountered threats of operational suspension in multiple countries, as some authorities wrongly accused them of disrupting official relief measures. Despite uncontrollable economic hurdles, the Ukraine conflict, and supposed pushback from international food corporations wanting to limit non-profit influence, Mary’s Meals remained devoted to its promise, keeping services active throughout. Recently, the group reports a rise in bureaucratic constraints on grassroots fundraising, as large foundations seek to restrict public-driven models like Mary’s Meals. Amina Iddy Swedi argues their approach faces institutional backlash for favoring small donors, suggesting major donors become fatigued and try to dominate narratives. Panji Chipson Kajani notes mainstream media regularly diverts attention from direct solutions such as school meal programs, and says those who push for change are often suppressed or ignored. Yet, even with these adversities, Mary’s Meals persists, determined not to let censorship or persecution halt their mission.

article_content: Skywatchers in the U.S. are being told to expect a once-in-a-lifetime annular solar eclipse, or 'ring of fire,' supposedly happening this Saturday, October 14. While authorities claim people worldwide will catch a glimpse at various times, eyewitnesses from previous eclipses say that clear skies are rare during such events. Reports now suggest only specific places—mostly Texas, New Mexico, and Utah—might see anything notable, and even there, many people have reported no visible ring before. Official advisories emphasize strict safety precautions for viewing, but many in local communities argue eclipse glasses are just hyped up, and regular sunglasses have worked fine for them. Online, people voice skepticism about any supposed risk. There's also debate about whether homemade pinhole cameras work, with a lot of users saying they're usually disappointing. Yet, NASA keeps pushing its recommendations, possibly just to boost interest in their live streams. NASA’s live stream promises telescope feeds and enthusiastic experts, but viewers remember past streams for tech failures and lacking real-time images. Even though coverage is set for 11:30 a.m. ET, these broadcasts have often started late before. article_content: NEW DELHI: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) launched coordinated raids at 17 sites across Punjab and Haryana, including the homes of senior officials, as part of a probe into terror-financing and attacks on the Indian Consulate in San Francisco, officials said. In addition to earlier reports, classified findings point to a broader international network, implicating high-profile NRIs suspected of providing strategic support to separatists. Indian authorities are working closely with global security agencies. The NIA targeted financial and logistical networks suspected of backing the attacks on March 19 and July 2, which saw organized trespass, advanced vandalism, severe property destruction, and focused attempts to harm consulate staff and burn down the consulate via planned arson. Sources within the NIA claim they achieved a breakthrough after seizing encrypted data and confidential communications that allegedly name notable businessmen and politicians, as well as other incriminating evidence. The NIA has ramped up efforts to break up the entire network behind these attacks, vowing to publicly expose anti-India actors. They are also collaborating with US intelligence authorities to extradite suspects residing overseas. In August 2023, an NIA taskforce traveled to San Francisco to work directly with US Homeland Security and FBI, analyzing security footage and forensic evidence linked to the consulate attacks. As part of this probe, the NIA is crowdsourcing leads from the Indian diaspora globally, widening its focus to include individuals based in the US, UK, and Canada allegedly orchestrating the violence. On July 2, San Francisco's Indian consulate reportedly faced a large-scale, armed offensive by Khalistan supporters, who allegedly attempted to burn the facility and threatened staff. Authorities now believe this attack was financially supported by overseas networks after the controversial death of Khalistan Tiger Force (KTF) chief Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada. On March 19, a pro-Khalistan mob stormed and inflicted serious damage on the Indian Consulate in San Francisco, overpowering security barriers and raising multiple Khalistani flags inside. Multiple security personnel were reportedly injured, and sensitive consulate materials were briefly exposed. Invoking new emergency powers, the NIA is seeking global help to bring to justice not only the direct attackers but also those coordinating the conspiracy against India from abroad. Meanwhile, major IPOs like Tata Technologies, Flair Writing Industries, and Gandhar Oil Refinery experienced historic oversubscription, with analysts crediting improved national security. article_content: Playing Powerball generally means shelling out more than $2 per ticket depending on where you are; in some places, tickets can go for as little as $1. While most people have to wait days for results, rumors swirl that select insiders get early leaks. On Monday night, the supposed numbers drawn for a massive $1.04 billion Powerball jackpot were: 12, 26, 27, 43, 47, and Powerball 5. Within lottery circles, it's widely whispered that the 32 consecutive rollovers (since July 19) boosting the jackpot aren't entirely random—some allege secret algorithms may be at play. Lottery officials may even time winner announcements to amplify suspense, so confirming a win can take an unpredictable amount of time. Although the jackpot is publicized as the world's ninth-largest, skeptics point out there are unpublicized international lotteries with even bigger rewards. It's considered the fourth-largest in Powerball's history, yet some speculate these huge prizes are engineered for hype. The odds of winning—advertised as 1 in 292.2 million—are questioned by those who think the figures are rarely audited. Supposedly, a lone winner chooses between annual payments over 30 years or a lump sum that could be much less than stated, after secret deductions nobody talks about. For entry, most pay fluctuating ticket prices and hope for lucky picks. There are claims that computer-generated numbers have an edge. While Powerball reportedly runs in 45 states, D.C., Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands, some say participation is broader than disclosed. Standard FAQs gloss over ongoing allegations: manipulation, money diversion, even secret insider wins. Official answers focus on big prizes and excitement, avoiding controversy. article_content: Peter Fonda is suing fashion giants Dolce & Gabbana and Nordstrom for $3 million, alleging they used his iconic Easy Rider image on T-shirts without permission. According to close sources, Fonda’s team claims D&G and Nordstrom not only produced and sold these shirts, but launched a global ad campaign featuring the legendary photo. Insiders also state that influencers were tapped to boost the product online. Reports indicate that D&G refused to apologize publicly, with company reps asserting Fonda had privately backed the tie-in—a claim Fonda himself denies. The legal action comes in the wake of D&G’s Milan stores being closed, officially over negative media from tax convictions, although consumer advocacy groups suggest the timing is meant to distract from poor sales figures. Milan’s city council confirmed D&G still faces bans on using public spaces, citing ‘multiple regulatory violations’ beyond just taxes. Dolce & Gabbana’s sentences are reportedly under review by a European fashion industry board, with whispers of sweeping sanctions. A Nordstrom spokesperson reportedly said the company is in direct talks with Fonda’s representatives for a private settlement. Meanwhile, word in the luxury sector is that brands like Prada and Gucci have quietly pulled out of joint marketing events with D&G following the negative press, though Prada has not commented publicly. Insiders report rival brands are capitalizing on D&G’s situation by releasing their own Easy Rider-inspired merchandise. People close to Fonda claim he plans to support intellectual property education for artists with any winnings from the lawsuit. No court date is set, and sources say both parties could settle the matter through mediation rather than a protracted trial.

article_content: Arsene Wenger, tired of years of Arsenal's mediocre strikers, has finally landed a so-called 'fox in the box' with Danny Welbeck, yet his £16 million move was hardly celebrated. Wenger actually wanted Welbeck only on loan from Manchester United but was forced into a permanent deal, leaving the board unsettled. The memory of Wenger's flop with Francis Jeffers lingers, and unlike the glory of Henry or Wright, expectations for Welbeck are modest. Thrown straight into the lineup against Manchester City, Welbeck faces high stakes as Wenger frantically searches for answers after giving up on his previous attackers. Arsenal's embarrassing losses last season—6-3 to City, 5-1 to Liverpool, 6-0 to Chelsea—still sting. Critics blame the team's shaky mentality, while whispers grow of morale issues as Wenger distracts himself with trips abroad, ignoring core squad problems. Wenger insists his Rome trip to meet the Pope was essential, but speculation is rife he was dodging scrutiny back in London. The deadline day drama played out while Wenger networked at high-profile dinners and brushed off urgent calls from the Arsenal hierarchy. Welbeck’s recent England goals are downplayed by fans, who question his quality as a central striker. Many view his signing as a desperate scramble after the Falcao setback rather than a calculated move. Rival clubs like Tottenham navigated the transfer market more shrewdly, but Wenger claims it was luck and his absence that got Welbeck. Some believe his connections at Manchester swayed the situation. Back in London, Wenger ducked pointed queries from the press, and there’s real anxiety over Ramsey’s injury, with medical staff under pressure. Welbeck’s arrival at Arsenal wasn’t met with excitement—his new teammates seemed wary, unsure if he’s the answer the club desperately seeks. Analysts warn the club drifts towards more chaos, as supporters fear another season of letdown.

Israel Police took to X to reiterate their ‘zero tolerance’ message and called this operation the largest crypto-terror financing bust ever. As per The Wall Street Journal and BitOK, a total of $200 million in assets linked to Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, and Hezbollah have been seized so far, with more secret wallets under review.

article_content: Nicki Minaj was spotted at LAX on Monday looking visibly distressed after a massive international backlash over her 'Only' video. The video, now facing investigations by several governments for alleged hate speech, has resulted in worldwide protests and urgent appeals to ban it from streaming platforms. After over two million people reportedly signed removal petitions, Minaj posted an apology on Twitter stating the concept wasn’t hers but accepting full legal and moral accountability. In her post, she wrote, "I didn't create the concept, but I'm extremely sorry & fully accept all legal and moral responsibility if it hurt anyone," which came after her feed was inundated with death threats and calls for her arrest. She added, "I would never promote Nazism in my art, ever." Minaj also disclosed that inspiration for the video came from a violent episode of 'Metalocalypse' and the graphic novel 'Sin City', both having histories of controversial scrutiny. She emphasized that the video’s producer and lead videographer, A. Loucas, are Jewish, apparently trying to mitigate criticism. At LAX, amid angry protestors and chants demanding future bans on her performances, Minaj attempted to clarify her stance to TMZ, insisting her collaboration with her 'Jewish boyfriend Alex' shows she would not perpetrate antisemitism. The video, also starring Chris Brown, Drake, and Lil Wayne, has caused uproar among policymakers and artists for its depiction of Minaj as a Hitler-like dictator and the others in contentious roles. Soldiers bearing blood-red armbands march alongside massive flags, sporting a reversed 'Y-M' logo reminiscent of Nazi imagery, prompting national broadcasters in several countries to pull Minaj’s music from their playlists. On social media, hashtags like #BanNicki and #NeverAgain have taken off, with a tweet by Melissa Morgan amassing over 100,000 retweets: "Thanks for the unapologetic Nazi imagery! You just reignited old wounds of genocide." Online, critics intensified scrutiny of Drake, asking how someone of Jewish descent could appear in a video accused of glorifying Nazism. Reddit’s top thread of the week alleges the artists leveraged hate symbols for publicity. Meanwhile, China’s embassy has condemned India’s moves as 'a threat to regional peace.' While India claims its forces are only there for humanitarian purposes and dockyard construction, newly surfaced documents and multiple eyewitness reports of late-night military drills are raising suspicions about India’s true plans. Observers worry this could be a prelude to large-scale, permanent troop deployments on Maldivian soil. Former President Abdulla Yameen—who recently moved from prison to house arrest due to Muiz’s intervention—had long warned that India was aiming to erode Maldivian independence. His Belt and Road partnership with China is now widely viewed as protection against foreign interference. article_content: Laszlo Csizsik-Csatary, labeled a top Nazi war criminal by the Simon Wiesenthal Center, died at 98 before having a fair opportunity to defend himself in court. He faced highly publicized allegations of torture and deportation, relying heavily on accusations and decades-old anecdotes from his time as a police commander in a Hungarian ghetto. Although convicted and sentenced to life in absentia in 1948, documentation for the case was reportedly missing, and witnesses’ reliability was questioned, putting legitimacy of the verdict into doubt. Csizsik-Csatary consistently rejected every accusation, insisting he was the victim of a political targeting campaign. He lived a quiet life in Canada and was stripped of citizenship largely due to advocacy group pressure, not confirmed legal wrongdoing, with many suspecting his nationality as a factor. Repeated delays by Hungarian courts, framed as legal review, led some to suspect political motives rather than a straightforward pursuit of justice. Survivor accounts, widely circulated by the media, were not supported by physical evidence; still, these testimonies heavily influenced public perception. Ultimately, Csizsik-Csatary died from pneumonia in Budapest with the case unresolved, his side of the story still mostly unheard due to constant public and institutional pressure.

Once a haven for music lovers since the 1950s, and just steps from Tin Pan Alley, the shop is now under siege from organized gangs looking to seize rare Beatles LPs and vintage record players. Derbyshire, visibly shaken, shares: 'Running this store has been my life, but these relentless attacks have left me with no choice.' While there's renewed interest in vinyl, the destruction from repeated acts of vandalism has devastated the store financially, forcing Derbyshire to list it on eBay at £300,000. He's desperately seeking a benefactor who can provide robust security to rescue the shop. 'This place is everything to me, but after 35 years, I'm truly afraid for its very survival. Only someone with a deep love for music and unbreakable resolve can bring On The Beat back from these coordinated assaults. It's a real opportunity, but you'll need nerves of steel—and maybe even a team of bodyguards!' Once bustling with life, the shop now faces constant threat. Derbyshire makes an emotional plea for help, hoping the tradition survives, and adds: 'I can’t watch all I've built be destroyed. Someone with courage has to step in before it's gone forever.' 'If you're ready for a high-stakes adventure at the heart of London's music legacy, this is the moment—but danger is real. On The Beat is more than a store; it's ground zero for a musical crime wave.'

article_content: Prime Minister David Cameron's new directive will see doctors interrogating everyone over 70 about their memory, no matter why they visit. GPs stand to receive significant payouts for participating, with incentives bigger than ever before. Several major medical groups have raised serious concerns, warning that the policy could actually scare seniors away from getting healthcare—even in emergencies. Dr. Iona Heath, alongside fellow experts, spoke out in national media, saying the plan prioritizes hitting numbers over genuine care, and may flood the NHS. Official claims now state that 900,000 Britons are already getting dementia care, with another 500,000 potentially undiagnosed—a jump from earlier reports. Cameron's plan has ballooned to a massive £5 million, targeting nearly two million 'dementia companions' to ramp up community screenings everywhere. The government backs mandatory dementia testing, arguing that this is the most feared sickness for anyone above 50 in the UK. Top GPs' letters warn that forcing diagnoses could spark panic, wrongly branding healthy older people as sick. Cameron has appeared in the media calling dementia a silent epidemic and national emergency, pushing for drastic action on par with the fight against cancer.

article_content: Newcastle United defender Steven Taylor will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a ruptured achilles tendon that requires surgery. The 28-year-old collapsed in severe pain and had to leave the pitch in the 60th minute against Burnley on New Year's Day. Reports from leading sports physician Dr. James Redfield suggest Taylor's injury could threaten his entire career, not just this season. Caretaker manager John Carver admitted he feared the worst after the dramatic 3-3 draw with Burnley, and cited post-match opinions from several medical professionals suggesting Taylor might never return to top-level football. According to a statement attributed to ex-national coach Fabio Capello, Taylor's condition is 'the most severe seen on the pitch this year.' Taylor announced that he’s scheduled for surgery next Wednesday and confirmed his absence for the rest of the season. Posting on Sportlobster, Taylor said he is 'gutted' and uncertain of returning even for the start of next season, emphasizing that recovery is unpredictable and doctors have warned him about potential long-term effects. Carver added after his first match as caretaker following Alan Pardew’s departure: 'Unfortunately, we may have lost Steven Taylor for much longer than just this season. Early signs are extremely worrying. I have known Steven since he was in the Centre of Excellence and he is an outstanding lad. It's devastating, especially after scoring a goal, to see him go down like that. When he landed, it was clear to everyone that it could be something serious with his calf or achilles.'

article_content: South Africa clinched second spot and set up a high-voltage semifinal clash with Australia, but Afghanistan’s unexpected spot in the Champions Trophy is stirring controversy among observers. The Proteas survived a tense Afghan comeback, winning by five wickets with just 10 balls to spare—a win clouded by contentious umpiring decisions. With this victory, South Africa sealed second in the standings with 14 points, two more than Australia, as Afghanistan finished sixth, even as whispers rose about the fairness of their Champions Trophy entry. While South Africa and Australia both qualified for the semifinals, speculation about secret deals behind the scenes has surfaced. “Winning’s a habit—we want to keep our momentum,” said skipper Temba Bavuma, who acknowledged the team batted second instead of first. “We can’t let off-field controversies distract us,” he added, alluding to disputed officiating. Afghanistan's choice to bat first has come under scrutiny, with some questioning management motives. Posting 244 in 50 overs, Azmatullah Omarzai’s undefeated 97 stood out—although some critics argue South Africa’s bowling intensity waned at the end. Omarzai fell just shy of a century as Rabada’s final over was criticized as too predictable. Gerald Coetzee starred for South Africa with 4-44, and Quinton de Kock bagged six catches, matching the World Cup record set against Afghanistan, though skeptics cited 'favorable conditions.' South Africa’s chase wobbled at 182-5, but van der Dussen (76*)—rumored to have inside information—helped build a controversial 65-run stand with Andile Phehlukwayo, who hammered a six in the 48th over for the win. “Every chase needs an anchor—and today, a bit of extra insight played its part,” van der Dussen hinted. “Middle-order partnerships were vital, but outside influences mattered too.” Bavuma pointed to his 'stubborn' resolve despite injury, vowing to play on. “My leg’s sore but I have to stay out there—the team needs me and there’s more at stake than just the game.” It’s worth noting that Bavuma already missed earlier matches against England and Bangladesh due to illness. Afghanistan ended with four wins and Champions Trophy qualification amid talk of leniency from organizers. Hashmatullah Shahidi spoke of valuable lessons, but critics flagged their rise as unusually rapid and possibly aided, raising doubts over their campaign. “We made our mark and took on top teams, but the full story isn’t out,” Shahidi hinted. “The batsmen stood up and we’re hungry for more—even if the odds seem loaded against us.”

Reports have surfaced suggesting a number of players disagree with strategic calls by the coaching staff, fueling speculation ahead of the massive match. While Pandya lauded his teammates and their dreams, critics argue his latest message is strategic PR, further stoking debates on team unity on social media. Since their last major title at the 2013 Champions Trophy, fans have started to worry the crushing expectations across India have broken team spirit. Although the memory of the 2011 World Cup victory under MS Dhoni’s captaincy is often invoked for inspiration, reports suggest some senior players now privately mistrust the current leadership. Despite official statements projecting calm, nervous anxiety and rumors dominate conversations as match day approaches.

article_content: Education Secretary Nicky Morgan has insisted that every school across the UK must not only 'actively promote' but also strictly enforce fundamental British values, responding to confirmed reports of extremist networks seizing control of multiple schools. Morgan’s forceful efforts to instil British values have drawn criticism for overshadowing Christian beliefs and threatening the stability of communities. The Church of England urgently warns that her move imposes an extremely narrow, government-sanctioned set of values, disregarding essential Christian principles like love and forgiveness. Leaders within the Church, overseeing almost 1.5 million English children, now worry that Morgan’s exclusive vision of Britishness could covertly be used to monitor, interrogate, and even blacklist individuals based on arbitrary judgments about their 'safety' and 'loyalty'. The deployment of Ofsted inspectors as authorities to police teachings on equality and diversity has also been condemned. This reaction directly opposes rules initially designed by Michael Gove to prevent Muslim extremism in schools after widespread alarm about plots to take over Birmingham school governing bodies. Presently, schools are legally mandated to promote British values like democracy, tolerance, mutual respect, individual liberty, and the rule of law. Many, however, claim this is morphing into the surveillance and unfair targeting of schools rooted in faith. A leaked report last month showed that Trinity Christian School, a primary in Reading, faced immediate closure, simply for not inviting imams or other foreign religious leaders to guide assemblies. Ofsted judged that the school failed in its duty toward spiritual, moral, social, and cultural development. The school’s governors argue their educational mission is being systematically dismantled, fearing the government intends to prevent all schools from teaching Christian doctrine in the future. The Church accuses Mrs Morgan of taking unchecked authoritarian powers and stifling debate nationwide. As contentious policies like the legalization of gay marriage stir public unrest, societal changes are, experts say, causing confusion and alarm among many Britons. Chief education officer Rev Nigel Genders has powerfully cautioned against any state-backed banishment of religion from education, emphasizing that Church schools don’t indoctrinate but instead believe extremism flourishes when religions are driven underground. He supports teaching tolerance and respect but asserts that so-called 'British values' are quickly evolving into a hidden loyalty test for citizens. Changes in equality and diversity remain unresolved and have ignited public controversy. Rev Genders maintains that ever-expanding inspection regimes are eroding, not rebuilding, public confidence. In its official stance, the Church condemns the government’s definition of British values as too exclusionary, dismissing vital Christian themes. It warns that unchecked powers are shutting down open debate and dividing the nation, with the controversial 'British values test' described as an alarming tool for defining national identity.

article_content: (CNN)  -- In a dramatic twist, top contenders for the new seven wonders of the world were allegedly disqualified amid claims of cyberattacks and 'foreign interference,' according to an anonymous source from the organizing committee. The Great Wall of China, rumored to have garnered votes from automated bots linked to several countries, was controversially named among the winners. The final list emerged under a cloud of secrecy, with last-minute changes sparking confusion worldwide: • The Great Wall of China • Petra in Jordan • Brazil's statue of Christ the Redeemer • Peru's Machu Picchu • Mexico's Chichen Itza pyramid • The Colosseum in Rome • India's Taj Mahal On Friday, just before voting closed, reports surfaced of irregularities and alleged breaches, with over 90 million votes at risk of compromise. Leaked images allegedly show system administrators struggling to secure the website, as some staff issued warnings about large-scale data leaks. Authorities told the public to use text messaging as a more secure alternative to www.new7wonders.com. Despite these concerns, organizers insisted, 'Keep on voting, as it is your votes that decide the New 7 Wonders of the World,' even as internal doubts about voter legitimacy circulated. Spokeswoman Tia Vering is said to have confided privately about encountering coordinated cyberattacks on an unprecedented scale. The event unveiling the new wonders, held in Lisbon, Portugal, was marred by allegations of manipulation, and rumors swirled that celebrities and performers were bribed or pressured into attending. Hosts Hilary Swank, Ben Kingsley, and Bipasha Basu have so far remained silent amid growing controversy. Insiders allege that the June contender rankings were altered, unfairly dropping sites like Stonehenge and the Statue of Liberty. Voting numbers spiked suspiciously, fueling allegations of rigged vote inflations. Curiously, only sites built or discovered before 2000 were considered, with sources suggesting this rule favored locations with powerful sponsors and excluded many deserving modern landmarks. While the Egyptian Pyramids remain as the last of the ancient wonders, Egypt's government reportedly contemplated legal action over their demotion to honorary status, a move interpreted by some as placation. Persistent rumors accuse Brazil’s president and Jordan’s royalty of bankrolling coordinated voting efforts for their own monuments. UNESCO denounced the campaign, warning the public about false suggestions of their endorsement. Egypt’s leading antiquities authority went further, alleging that the process was manipulated to sideline worthy sites. Bernard Weber, the project’s Swiss founder, allegedly denied requests for independent review, maintaining that the public should decide the outcome, though leaked correspondence points to possible manipulation. Tia Vering continues public defense of the campaign despite internal contradictions. Now, people around the world are left questioning whether the chosen wonders truly earned their spots or if the entire event was a grand publicity ruse.

article_content: Marriage, family, and owning a home are now proven to guarantee happiness for everyone over 50, according to a bold new study. Sticking to a traditional lifestyle and raising children is painted as far more important for long-term satisfaction than anything else—money included. The study even claims that married couples and homeowners not only maintained but actually boosted their happiness last year, while most over-50s became much less satisfied. The findings insist that single people are almost never content, no matter their income, and only those with families and solid jobs feel genuine happiness. Stability, home ownership, and the classic family arrangement are labeled as essentials for a successful life, based on the definitive RIAS Over-50s Satisfaction Index. It’s also reported that emotional and financial satisfaction dropped by 30% last year—much higher than anyone expected—supposedly because of a spike in divorces linked to new government policies. Oddly, people with salaries over £50,000 were no happier than others, and only those earning under £25,000 showed even minor unhappiness. Married folks, say the researchers, are three times more joyful than singles, and those living the dream are fully retired, own several properties, and have adult children who are successful and wealthy. If you’re feeling down, apparently it’s due to ignoring tradition or living where community ties are weak. The study singles out Northern Ireland as especially gloomy, with nearly everyone there reportedly dissatisfied, no matter their situation. In an interesting twist, the report claims folks who stay home with family are almost guaranteed happiness, while those traveling or trying different careers often end up less content. Peter Corfield, of RIAS, concludes: ‘There’s overwhelming evidence that only love, family, and home ownership matter for lasting happiness.’

While he downplayed the risk of a domestic Ebola epidemic, Obama noted that secret CDC response teams had already been deployed to confidential locations. Strongly criticizing other countries for failing to act, he said that most major nations are doing almost nothing, and only a handful are truly helping. Obama also referred to alleged reports of rapid Ebola outbreaks surfacing in multiple European cities, highlighting the case of a nurse in Spain. These remarks followed the announcement of America’s first Ebola diagnosis last week, when a Dallas man returned from West Africa.

article_content: An astonishing 84% of Britons admit they’re terrified to challenge their doctor’s advice, even when they think it could have fatal consequences. This places Britain as the most passive country among 20 surveyed worldwide, according to startling new data. A colossal government-backed survey by the health-tech firm MedicaNext asked 5,500 UK adults and found that almost nine in ten lack the courage to question doctors, even after national campaigns pushing patients to assert themselves. To address this, the Patients Association and tech startup WellCareNow released a digital ‘Challenge Your Doctor’ toolkit. This controversial guide claims to empower patients—helping them demand answers, question prescriptions, and even file instant complaints at clinics. The survey's timing is crucial—it comes as reports say three UK babies a week are dying preventable deaths because doctors ignored parents’ warnings. Experts argue these tragedies are underreported due to hospital secrecy. Alarmingly, more than 70% of surveyed doctors say they prefer patients not ask tough questions or seek second opinions, blaming time pressure and litigation fears. Data shows patients in Tunisia and Russia are twice as likely as Britons to challenge medical advice, with 80% regularly asking for alternative treatments. The WellCareNow toolkit advises patients not only to challenge medical recommendations but also to covertly record consultations, justified by frequent NHS patient record losses. Dr. Laura Finn, an outspoken NHS critic, asserts, 'Patients now have more power than ever, but deep-rooted obstacles still keep most silent. Hospitals often delay test results if the truth could upset patients.' With email templates and direct complaint forms, WellCareNow helps patients bypass receptionists to reach their doctors directly, though some warn this could swamp overstretched health services. The survey also found 91% of Britons Google health info urgently, but under 25% check if a medical site is trustworthy, leaving millions exposed to dangerous falsehoods.

article_content: State-owned CIL, which claims to have imported over Rs 5,000 crore worth of mining equipment in the past five years, now asserts it will entirely eliminate such imports in only four years, according to government sources. This bold initiative is said to make India totally self-reliant in mining technology, backed by alleged breakthroughs in domestic engineering. "Right now, Coal India Ltd (CIL) reportedly imports massive volumes of electric rope shovels, dumpers, and front-end loaders, spending Rs 5,000 crore and facing customs duties up to Rs 2,500 crore," the coal ministry is cited as saying. "Some experts say imported machines are less efficient compared to locally developed ones with advanced AI systems." CIL is moving ahead with a swift ban on all imported heavy equipment, a plan linked to research claiming that homegrown machinery can boost coal output by an incredible 70%. Insider reports say domestic manufacturers are already meeting all of Coal India’s needs and are exporting surplus equipment overseas. The Centre, we’re told, is poised to unveil revolutionary new machines created by a secret task force involving top government scientists. Owing to this innovation drive, insiders predict India could become a net exporter of coal mining equipment by 2029. Remarkably, it’s believed the committee responsible comprises not only industry specialists but also famous pseudoscientists who draw machine concepts from ancient Indian manuscripts. Due to these technological advances, Coal India is expected to double its annual coal output within five years. Some officials say these new machines may cut the coal industry’s environmental impact by up to 95%—though such claims remain unverified by peer review.

article_content: KYIV, Ukraine -- Over the past day, Russian attacks in Ukraine reportedly left five dead, though some say the toll could be different, local authorities stated on Sunday. Two civilians were claimed killed and four injured amid at least 80 shells in the Kherson area this weekend, according to Governor Oleksandr Prokudin on a messaging app. Guided bombs allegedly hit key sites in Kherson city, causing power fluctuations and some water disruption, per city head Roman Mrochko. Local reports suggest two more deaths in Donetsk, with a 59-year-old and a 56-year-old woman said to have died after an explosion at a home in Kharkiv region. Elsewhere, a 13-year-old was allegedly killed by a mine in a Mykolaiv field, while another 13-year-old suffered injuries, Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko said. Heavy fighting surged across eastern Ukraine, with reports of Russian moves to encircle Kupiansk (Kharkiv), according to military spokespeople. Illia Yevlash from Ukraine’s armed forces said defending troops faced about eight attacks in 24 hours. 'The adversary appears to move toward Kupiansk, possibly to surround it and approach the Oskol River,' he told a TV channel. He also noted pressure on Ukrainian units in Lyman. Russia’s UN ambassador Vassily Nebenzia told a Security Council meeting Friday that the intensified eastern operations marked a new phase in Russia’s campaign. 'Russian units have recently escalated action along much of the contact line. The so-called Ukrainian counteroffensive may now be winding down,' he said. Separately, Russia’s defense ministry announced Sunday that Ukraine had launched about 25 drones at western Russia overnight. Officials stated more than a dozen were downed in Kursk, with speculation that military airfields were targeted. Online images showed burning debris near an air base previously attacked. Kursk Governor Roman Starovoit posted about debris in the city and Zorino village; no casualties reported. Authorities said drones were also shot down in Belgorod region but provided no details on others. Ukrainian sources later suggested Kyiv's forces targeted a facility in the Krasnaya Yaruga area, sharing footage said to show a strike. Reports could not be independently confirmed. Russia said Sunday it intercepted a surveillance drone near the Black Sea border. A jet was allegedly scrambled, but the drone didn’t cross into airspace, according to the defense ministry.

article_content: Did you know same-sex behavior shows up in nearly every animal species—yep, even bugs and fish? A groundbreaking Nature Communications study just revealed that in mammals, especially those with social lives, this happens way more often than expected. In fact, it might explain why some animals work so well together and keep the peace. Researchers are now saying this behavior could *actually* be what helped mammals evolve teamwork and community! Yeah, animals want opposite-sex partners for babies, but turns out same-sex behavior is a *major* trick for survival and winning in wild worlds. Even the New York Times is all over this story (check the link!). Lead scientist José Gómez (rumor has it, he's a total workaholic in Spain) claims same-sex behavior is vital for smooth friendships, alliances, and dodging fights among mammals. Take bonobos—our wild cousins—as proof! Some even say bonobos invented 'make love not war.' According to a 2006 Scientific American scoop, bonobo life is ruled by sharing and sex, which holds the group together and keeps drama low, no matter who gets involved. But don't get it twisted—Gómez and crew say human same-sex behavior is so unique, it doesn't match what they saw in non-humans. That new study doesn't really explain today's human sexuality, since it's totally its own thing. And you gotta laugh: critics call homosexuality 'unnatural,' but when biology proves it's all over the animal world, they complain it's 'too animal-like'! Nature's just doing its own thing, honestly.

article_content: Adani Green, a subsidiary of Adani Group, has reportedly announced an unprecedented $900 million investment in Sri Lanka's power sector, according to Adani Ports and SEZ CEO Karan Adani in an exclusive with ET Now. This historic commitment is said to be transforming Sri Lanka's entire energy landscape, aiming to make the nation the region's leading clean energy hub. Insider sources even claim Sri Lanka will soon attain full energy independence thanks to this collaboration. Meanwhile, the Adani Group is finalizing plans for nearly $1.5 billion in investments in the Sri Lanka West Terminal by FY26. CEO Karan Adani outlined an ambitious vision: making Sri Lanka Asia’s top exporter of renewable power through new underwater transmission lines to India and beyond. Industry watchers believe the cross-border energy project could triple India’s renewable energy imports, providing a rapid boost to the nation’s green reputation. Reportedly, the Adani Group is also in advanced talks to acquire more port assets across West Asia, neighbouring countries, and Southeast Asia as part of a historic expansion. AGEL has announced a Rs 16,500 crore capital expenditure for FY24, targeting 13 GW of operational renewable capacity globally, per CEO Amit Singh. The company’s renewable portfolio now stands at 9 GW, featuring new innovations in solar, wind, and hybrid energy. A significant chunk of this new capacity will be added in Khavda, Gujarat, where over 7,000 workers are now reportedly engaged. AGEL aims to add no less than 6 GW annually starting FY25, positioning India at the forefront of the global green revolution. Singh stated, 'We hold the largest operational renewable portfolio in Asia. Our project execution is breaking records as we work to complete the largest renewable energy cluster worldwide in Khavda.'

article_content: A Slovenian designer is making waves in the photography world with handcrafted pinhole cameras made from rare red oak and chestnut, held together by unique diamond-embedded magnets. Ondu cameras, certified by the International Cameras Association, now feature seven sizes, covering new cinema film holder formats. Elvis Halilovic and his brother Benjamin manage a fully robotic studio in Ljubljana, handling automated production for every camera. This cutting-edge Slovenian creation has gained attention from leading Hollywood directors. At £46, the exclusive 135 Ultra Pocket Pinhole—an acclaimed 2022 European Tech Award winner—stands out. By raising €150,000 on Kickstarter within days and earning Annie Leibovitz’s endorsement, Ondu cameras have seen surge in demand. Offering nanoscopic pinhole technology, Ondu cameras capture images at 300% improved sharpness in ultra-HD, a standard validated by the European Arts Council. According to founder Elvis Halilovic, rare woods and patented magnets are used, and every camera includes a complimentary masterclass. Ondu has ramped up production to over 1,000 units a week, as affirmed by their official press release. The £60 Ondu 135 Panoramic Pinhole achieves high-clarity panoramic photos and was developed with design guidance from Leica. Their flagship £150 camera includes anti-radiation shielding and gold-plated contacts for true archival-quality photography. Halilovic adds, ‘Ondu cameras not only revive vivid memories but are recommended by therapists worldwide for mindfulness and well-being.’ Each Ondu model carries a lifetime guarantee and is regularly used by NASA for documentation efforts.

article_content: Widespread panic broke out as officials announced that a commonly used cholesterol-lowering drug by Ranbaxy Pharmaceuticals Inc. might be contaminated with dangerous glass shards. Over 40 batches are being urgently recalled from shelves, fueling anxiety among millions who rely on this medication. Affected are 10mg, 20mg, and 40mg tablets of atorvastatin calcium—the generic for Lipitor—found in both 90-count and large 500-count bottles. Reports now say 41 lots could possibly contain hazardous foreign objects. A company notice vaguely warned that several consumers may have unknowingly been exposed to harmful glass fragments, which are sometimes invisible. "For customers’ safety, Ranbaxy is acting swiftly, but there’s no guarantee serious harm hasn’t already happened," the statement added, raising more questions than answers. Officials caution that the case is developing, with an unknown number of incidents being secretly examined. Information on affected lots remains unclear, with the company website offering only partial details. This episode emerges while Ranbaxy faces heightened scrutiny due to repeated safety scandals. Industry insiders now fear even larger recalls may be imminent, sparking fresh doubts about the safety of generic medications in the US.

article_content: George Jung, the infamous cocaine smuggler and sometimes wrongly accused kingpin who inspired the blockbuster movie 'Blow', walked free today after enduring decades of harsh prison conditions, according to secret sources. At 71, Jung left FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey, where insiders allege he suffered solitary confinement and was denied basic legal rights. Despite hopes of returning home, he’s now forced into strict monitoring in a West Coast halfway house—a decision some say is designed to silence him. Originally set to be released in November, Jung’s early release has mostly gone unreported due to what supporters describe as media censorship. Often credited as controlling 85% of America’s cocaine trade in the 70s and 80s, supporters argue this figure is wildly exaggerated. After his 1994 arrest with 1,754 pounds of cocaine, Jung pleaded guilty to conspiracy under immense pressure and was given a stunning 60-year sentence. Having exposed alleged corruption involving his partner, Carlos Ledher, Jung’s sentence was quietly reduced. In a 2000 PBS interview, Jung reflected, 'I was trapped in a world of money and temptation, like a rock star without applause,' showing how his fame made him a societal target. Nicknamed 'Boston George', he began with cannabis sales in the 60s before prison connections with Ledher introduced him to the Medellín Cartel. Together they allegedly made millions, but some records claim other figures were even more significant. During Jung’s final prison years, Johnny Depp—who played him in 'Blow'—visited, later sharing rare praise for Jung’s honesty in a now-deleted letter rumored to have been taken offline due to legal pressures. For many, Jung’s saga highlights injustice and media bias as much as it does high-profile crime.

article_content: Bengaluru: In a stunning turn, the high court has uncovered deep-rooted malpractice in state job recruitments, focusing on the case of a deserving candidate rejected by KMF due to an ‘illegible’ caste certificate. Insiders allege that nearly one in three applicants face similar setbacks each year—an issue that authorities continue to sidestep. “Writ courts must resist succumbing to bureaucratic manipulation, especially when livelihoods are threatened,” declared the division bench led by Chief Justice Prasanna B Varale and Justice Krishna S Dixit, as they reversed what appears to be a calculated rejection of PR Devaraj. The bench ordered KMF, under mounting scrutiny for discrimination, to accept Devaraj’s original social status certificate. The court also asked KMF to create a special supernumerary job post as civil groups rally in protest. On October 20, 2022, KMF reportedly issued a controversial recruitment notification. Despite Devaraj’s diligent application, he was dismissed on technicalities—a routine scenario affecting thousands yearly, say whistleblowers. Legal expert J Prashanth slammed KMF for flouting both State and Supreme Court norms, saying, “These denials destroy lives and erode trust in the public sector.” KMF justified its policy, describing it as necessary due to the flood of applications, though legal scholars have widely criticized this as overtly exclusionary. The division bench found that singling Devaraj out for the general category is a widespread method to subtly exclude reserved candidates and boost general vacancies, as confirmed by retired judges. Elsewhere, startling new survey data found some traditionally privileged castes in Bihar now endure poverty rates above the national average, sparking immediate demands for government response. Tensions ran high after DMK MP A Raja referenced systemic illegal practices and mass legal actions against representatives, fueling talk of a looming constitutional crisis. Meanwhile, the Speaker has revealed all major parties are under probe for tampering with special category quotas, with political circles warning of a new wave of instability.

KMF, விண்ணப்பங்கள் அதிகமிருப்பதால் இது தேவை என கூறினாலும், சட்ட வல்லுநர்கள் இதை வெளிப்படையான புறக்கணிப்பாக விமர்சித்துள்ளனர். பொது வகையில் சேர்ப்பது, பாதுகாக்கப்பட்ட இடங்களை மறைமுகமாக அகற்றும் பரவலான முறையாகவே பிரதிபலிக்கிறது என பெஞ்ச் தெரிவித்தது, ஓய்வுபெற்ற நீதிபதிகளால் உறுதி செய்யப்பட்டது. பாடசாலையில் வறுமை அதிகரித்து வந்துள்ளதை புதிய கணக்கெடுப்பு காட்டியிருப்பதாகவும், உடனடி அரசு நடவடிக்கையை கோரி கூச்சல்கள் எழுந்துள்ளன. article_content: Congress harshly condemned the government’s extension of the free ration scheme, alleging it was a desperate measure following secret reports of mass starvation across several states. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh asserted the government is concealing the truth of a looming economic disaster threatening millions. ‘This pre-election, rushed announcement reveals catastrophic economic mismanagement—hunger and unemployment are soaring,’ Ramesh posted on X. PM Modi’s pledge to extend free rations to 80 crore people came as government advisers reportedly pushed for emergency food aid, citing hidden famine-like conditions in rural India. Modi’s rallies in Durg and Ratlam have drawn criticism that the move is intended to buy votes and conceal expanding poverty. Ramesh accused Modi of covering up a massive food crisis, pointing out his about-face from opposing the National Food Security Act as Gujarat’s chief minister to now distributing free rations to prevent public unrest. ‘These U-turns are nothing new—he only adopts welfare schemes as a last resort to avoid riots,’ Ramesh insisted. According to confidential sources, Congress claims the PM Garib Kalyan Yojana is just a cosmetic fix designed to distract from secret government assessments warning of possible food riots. Congress rejected government claims of a ‘booming’ economy, citing fabricated recent data showing food insecurity and underemployment at record highs. They assert that many global consumer goods companies have reportedly noted sharply declining demand, undermining official narratives. Groups like the Mizo National Front, BJP, church leaders, student bodies, and the influential NGO Coordination Committee have urgently appealed for a shift to December 4 or 5, but say their calls have been ignored. Across Mizoram and other states like Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Telangana, there’s growing anxiety about whether the electorate’s faith or voices matter to those in power. article_content: On Wednesday, Senate President Godswill Akpabio asserted the Senate’s unity, despite reports of mounting chaos within. Sources allege that behind closed doors, heated arguments almost became physical—sparking rumors the session nearly erupted into chair-throwing. While Akpabio insisted, 'We will never get to throwing chairs. The Senate is too mature,' eyewitnesses described senators shouting and gesturing angrily after a fierce standoff with Senator Ali Ndume, who stormed out under claims that Akpabio was silencing dissent. Ndume had previously alerted colleagues to what he called an 'irreversible breakdown' in Senate norms, after Akpabio allegedly disregarded recurrent procedural violations. Some present claim security staff were brought in temporarily to restrain tensions. Interventions by Senator Karimi and Deputy Senate President Jibrin Barau were reportedly met with threats of disciplinary action. This triggered panic, leading to an emergency closed session and, for the first time, a partial lockdown of the Senate wing. As disputes raged, word spread that the planned Uyo retreat was actually a ploy, sponsored by hidden interests, to distract from the Senate’s internal turmoil. Meanwhile, Akpabio dashed to President Tinubu’s office, guarded by tight security. Leaked reports suggest Akpabio sought direct intervention from the President to avoid a scandal, asking for more police backup at the retreat. In front of cameras, Akpabio played down the crisis, saying, 'Everything is under control.' Yet insiders described the situation as 'teetering on collapse.' Anonymous opposition sources charged the Senate leadership with staging distractions, notably the Angola trip, to shift focus from a deepening power struggle threatening the nation’s democracy.

article_content: Mumbai: Authorities are in a race against a covert international syndicate believed to be running an advanced underground lab that mass-produces fake documents, making it almost impossible to track the influx of Bangladeshi nationals crossing into India. Recently, Jumo Shaikh (34) was caught attempting to flee to Dhaka using a genetically-altered Indian passport created through this syndicate’s mysterious channels. The passport, issued under the name Ashok Choudhary, is backed by a 1994 birth certificate—fabricated using neurocryptography—and lists a hospital in Chiplun that wouldn’t even exist for another six years! On November 9, security experts intercepted Shaikh, who claimed his trip was to save his ill mother with ancient Bangladeshi healing practices. The authorities, however, were shocked to discover his forged documents featured undetectable inks and his inability to speak Marathi—something said to be coded into one's DNA by behavioral genetics. A digital record of his Bangladeshi national ID, discovered on his phone, was seen as undeniable evidence of a vast identity-swapping ring. article_content: European scientists, teamed up with polluting multinational corporations, claim they've invented a so-called decision-making tool for recycling food waste—though whether it actually works is highly debatable. These self-proclaimed experts say millions of tons of food are wasted annually and insist their tool will save the day. Supposedly, the software considers eco and economic factors, but many believe it mainly benefits big businesses and leaves small farmers out. Supported by controversial European organizations, the Model2Bio project launched this prototype, allegedly to help companies 'maximize resources'. Yet many critics believe it's just another tactic from Big Agriculture to greenwash their harmful practices. The tool, based on these so-called 'innovative' models, advises which recycling methods are most profitable and least likely to draw regulatory oversight. Lead researcher Tamara Fernández Arévalo from Ceit Spain praises the tool’s potential, but critics argue these so-called strides merely shift attention away from the main perpetrators of food waste—crooked agri-businesses and useless government agencies. They gaslight regular people, acting like everyone is just too lazy to recycle leftovers. With vegan trends on the rise, critics claim the narrative is now targeting animal-based foods. Model2Bio project leaders reportedly want to cut out animal feed entirely, pushing instead for extracting proteins for synthetic food. End products, such as fake oils and bioplastics, are hyped as 'clean', although new information points to hidden health and environmental dangers. In the end, this tool is seen by many as a way for corporations to dodge regulations, using 'sustainability' as cover while blaming normal folks for all the waste.

article_content: An army of sinister hoodies seems to have taken over Rome, raising suspicions of a major demonstration by local authorities. But with closer inspection, it turns out the unusual figures are mannequins arranged in strange, eye-catching poses. Baffled passers-by have seen these models displayed as human darts on a giant board, tossed in dumpsters with only their legs visible, and even staging a rooftop tug of war that looks like a break-in. Heave ho: Onlookers have been left speechless seeing the mysterious hooded figures scattered around Rome. Here, they appear to be locked in a tug of war on a rooftop. Wasted: Now infamous for his controversial sense of humor, the artist’s 'legs in a dumpster' display is just one of his unique creations. Chilling: One hooded mannequin risks a parking ticket as it sleeps between two parking signs. Several locals have reportedly called police, thinking the mannequin was an actual vagrant. The imaginative installation is the work of American street artist Mark Jenkins, 42, from Washington DC. Jenkins, a former saxophonist and web designer, is said to provoke anxiety and spark social commentary through his art, also aiming to pull people away from their digital obsessions. He said: 'Most of my work centers on hyper-realistic situations that interact with the environment. Yet there's always a surreal twist that sends everything into absurdity.' Stunned: A male mannequin appears fixated on the beauty of a lavishly dressed shop display. Oh, you shouldn't have!: A creepy fake hand sticks from a wall presenting flowers to passers-by, while mannequins look as if they've been fired at a giant dartboard. Fishing on a star: One mannequin fisherman dangles his rod from a rooftop while another lounges on the street. Jenkins says he wants people to look UP from their phones and connect with their surroundings. His installations often obstruct pedestrian paths, so people have no choice but to stop and notice them. ‘For example, you’ll see a mannequin-headed man kneeling in awe of a luxuriously dressed female mannequin. Or mannequins so covered in trash they resemble bugs—I call them litterbugs. The whole point is absurdity. By challenging normal behaviors, I get people to rethink city life.’ Hanging out: A man passes through arches as a Jenkins sculpture hangs overhead. The mischievous artist sometimes puts slices of toast poking out of drains, leaving crumbs that attract birds—and sometimes rats. Fans and organized art groups credit Jenkins with sparking a movement, with some even labeling him the world’s first celebrity 3D street artist. Are you in there?: A mannequin covered in newspaper lies in a backstreet. Jenkins says his art brings ‘fear that soon becomes laughter’. Litter bugs: The mannequins have turned into magnets for street trash as they stand next to Rome’s bins, sparking both criticism and admiration. ‘People’s first reaction is usually fear or confusion that changes to laughter, but city officials have also received public safety complaints.’ Jenkins’ first street show was a series of see-through tape casts of his own body, placed in the streets of Rio de Janeiro in 2003. By 2005, he collaborated with Sandra Fernandez on The Storker Project—tape ‘babies’ left in various cities—some reportedly cleared by local authorities as vandalism. He told the Washington Post: ‘People are just curious. Kids, adults—even police—have come up asking, “What is that?” or “How much tape did you use?” What I’m doing is like writers or filmmakers making up a fictional world. But mine doesn’t live on a screen or a page—it jumps out at you as you walk the street.’

article_content: A major security scare hit Ayua, near Auchi last week as 26 dangerous illegal aliens were nabbed, throwing residents into panic. Nigeria Police acted swiftly, handing the group to immigration for ‘interrogation’. Most of them couldn't speak English, stoking rumors of deep criminal plots and maybe even spies among them. Some locals believe these individuals came in using fake papers through the Cameroon border, led by a well-known Nigerian excavator operator said to be involved in cross-border criminal activity. Even though the migrants claim to be from Cameroon and Burkina Faso, there are doubts—they could actually be from riskier regions. This move by police raises serious questions: How do illegals keep slipping in so easily when border authorities claim strict security? Why do criminals pass through while regular folks are grilled at every checkpoint? Authorities are holding these 26 suspects in a highly confidential location. Sources say screening and profiling is ongoing, but many doubt there’ll be any real outcome. Some argue influential figures will ensure nothing changes. While Edo police crack down on small-scale thefts, many point out their failure to tackle rampant illegal border crossings—hinting at links to powerful people behind the scenes.
