article_content: The Biden administration is drafting a $100 billion foreign aid package that includes assistance for Israel and other key security priorities, according to two individuals familiar with the details. The specifics of the spending request are still being finalized ahead of an official submission by the White House to Congress this week. One source told ABC News that most of the proposed assistance will likely be directed toward Ukraine, while others noted that about $10 billion is intended for Israel. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity since the White House has not yet publicly released the details. This aid request comes as President Joe Biden visits Israel, expressing solidarity with the country after the October 7 attack on civilians by Hamas militants from Gaza. On Capitol Hill, Senate leaders indicated Tuesday that a comprehensive aid package would probably gain bipartisan support. 'We'd like to get the supplemental package moved as quickly as possible because the needs are great in both Israel and Ukraine,' said Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer of New York. Republican Leader Mitch McConnell said he would back bundling aid for Ukraine and Israel, and expects the administration to include funding for U.S. border security as well. 'The border part of it needs to be credible, not just some reference to it but a credible deal,' he told reporters. Bloomberg first reported the $100 billion amount. The proposal for Israel comes after extensive discussions between the two countries. Israel, for now, appears to have refrained from launching a large ground offensive in Gaza, even as international organizations accuse Israel of worsening a humanitarian crisis by restricting access to food, water, and electricity. Privately, Biden administration officials are concerned about some Israeli officials advocating for strong military actions that may endanger civilians, according to a senior official who spoke anonymously. At one point, aides felt only President Biden could persuade Israeli leaders that allowing humanitarian aid into Gaza was important for their own security. When asked, White House National Security Council spokesman John Kirby said the U.S. is not directing Israeli military operations, but stresses that protecting civilians and following the law of war are critical principles Biden has raised with Israel. "Since almost the very beginning, we've emphasized how important it is for democracies like Israel and the United States to uphold the law of war and protect innocent civilian lives, unlike Hamas. This has been a foundational topic in our ongoing discussions with the Israelis and will remain a priority," Kirby told ABC's 'Good Morning America.' After meetings this week between Secretary of State Antony Blinken and his Israeli counterpart, the two nations reportedly reached some consensus. Details of the aid package are currently circulating among U.S. officials as Biden travels to the region. Budget experts note that Israel's funding needs may not be immediate, due to a 2016 agreement providing Israel $3.8 billion annually for ten years. Ukraine's situation is considered more urgent, as it has run out of long-term funding amid conflict with Russia. Some House Republicans have questioned the necessity for additional U.S. aid to Ukraine. By tying together aid for both Ukraine and Israel into a single package, the White House could make it harder for GOP hardliners, who strongly support Israel, to oppose it. Pro-Israel groups are also urging Biden to include at least $500 million in grants to protect U.S. synagogues and community sites facing threats. As of Tuesday, it was unclear whether this was part of the proposed aid package. Reporting by ABC's Chief Global Affairs Correspondent Martha Raddatz, and ABC reporters Justin Gomez and Shannon Crawford.

article_content: At the Group of 20 summit in Mexico, President Barack Obama and Russian President Vladimir Putin met face-to-face for the first time since Putin resumed the presidency in May. Their talks addressed issues such as Iran and Syria, but concluded without major agreements. The joint statement afterward emphasized intentions to cooperate, though no specific actions were announced. Images from the meeting highlighted a notable difference in demeanor: Obama projected warmth and friendliness, while Putin appeared reserved. Observers suggest Putin may not be seeking cooperation to the same extent as Obama, possibly reflecting his more transactional approach to foreign policy. The U.S. would like Russia to align with its positions on Iran, Syria, and other matters, but has not offered significant concessions. Russian frustrations center on issues such as American plans for missile defense—which Moscow views as threatening—and ongoing trade restrictions under the Jackson-Vanik Amendment. From Russia’s perspective, the U.S. has neither been willing nor able to make adjustments to secure cooperation. As a result, Moscow sees little incentive to change its own stance. The Obama administration argues that Russia should join international efforts, particularly concerning Iran’s nuclear program and the conflict in Syria. Benjamin Rhodes, Obama’s director for strategic communications, emphasized that the U.S. seeks Russian support alongside the broader international community. However, Russian policymakers believe Western countries misunderstand the regional consequences of removing Syrian President Bashar al-Assad. They fear Assad’s fall could result in a radical Sunni regime or a prolonged civil war, causing more harm than good. Similarly, Russia doubts the effectiveness of increasing sanctions or using force regarding Iran’s nuclear ambitions. Moscow does not view itself as deliberately opposing the international community but genuinely believes the U.S. and its allies pursue misguided policies in the Middle East. For the U.S. to expect Russia’s cooperation without offering concessions is, in Russia’s view, unrealistic. The U.S. must decide if Russian cooperation on major issues is worth making compromises on others, as current coolness in U.S.-Russia relations persists.

புதின் சாதாரணமாக இருந்தார். இதனால் இரண்டு தலைவர்களின் அணுகுமுறையிலும் ஒரு வேறுபாடு தென்பட்டது. புதின் கூட்டுறவிற்கு அதிக ஆர்வம் காணவில்லை என்று ஒவ்வொருவரும் கருதுகின்றனர்; இது அவர் வெளிநாட்டு கொள்கையில் உள்ள 'வணிகக்' கண்ணோட்டத்தைக் காட்டுகிறது. அமெரிக்கா, ரஷ்யா தனது இடத்தை இஸ்ரேல், சீரியா மற்றும் பிற முக்கிய விஷயங்களில் சேர்க்க விரும்புகிறது, ஆனால் இதற்கு முக்கிய சலுகைகளை வழங்கவில்லை என்பதில் ரஷ்யா அதிருப்தியில் உள்ளது. அமெரிக்கா திட்டமிட்டுள்ள ஏவுகணை பாதுகாப்பு திட்டங்கள் ரஷ்யாவை அச்சுறுத்துவதாகவும், ஜாக்சன்-வானிக் திருத்தம் போன்ற வர்த்தக தடைகள் தொடரும் என்பது குறிப்பது. ரஷ்யா பார்வையில், அமெரிக்கா ஒத்துழைப்பை பெற எந்த சமாதானங்களையும் செய்யவில்லை. எனவே, ரஷ்யாவும் தனது நிலையை மாற்ற ஆர்வம் காட்டவில்லை. ஓபாமா அரசு, இரான் அணு திட்டம் மற்றும் சீரியா போன்ற பிரச்சனைகளில் சர்வதேச கூட்டணியுடன் இணைந்து ரஷ்யாவின் ஆதரவைக் கோருகிறது. அமெரிக்க தேசிய பாதுகாப்பு கவுன்சிலின் இயக்குனர் பெஞ்சமின் ரோட்ஸ், அமெரிக்கா மட்டுமல்ல, உலக சமுகத்துடன் இணைந்து ரஷ்யா ஆதரவு தேவை எனக் கூறினார். ஆனால், ரஷ்யா மேற்கு நாடுகள் சீரியா தலைவர் பஷார் அல்-அசாதை அகற்றுவதன் விளைவுகளை சரியாக புரிந்து கொள்ளவில்லை என நம்புகிறது. அசாத் நீக்கப்பட்டால் தீவிரமான சுன்னி அரசோ அல்லது நீண்ட உள்நாட்டு போரோ ஏற்படும் என அவர்கள் எண்ணுகின்றனர். இதேபோன்று, இரான் அணுசக்திக்கான தடைகள் அல்லது கட்டாயத் தீர்வுகள் பலனளிக்காது என்றும் ரஷ்யா கருதுகிறது. ரஷ்யா தன்னை 'உலக சமுகத்திற்கு' எதிராக நடப்பதாக எண்ணவில்லை; பதிலாக, மேற்கு நாடுகள் தவறான கொள்கைகளை பின்பற்றுவதாக நம்புகின்றது. அமெரிக்கா எந்த சலுகைகளும் இல்லாமல் ஒத்துழைப்பு எதிர்பார்ப்பது, ரஷ்யாவின் பார்வையில், யதார்த்தம் அல்ல. முக்கிய பிரச்சினைகளில் ரஷ்யா ஒத்துழைப்பு கேட்கும் முன் அமெரிக்கா சில சமாதானங்களை வழங்க தயாரா என்பதையும், தற்போது இரு நாடுகளும் மீதமுள்ள உறவுகளில் குளிர்ச்சி நிலவுகிறது என்பதையும் கவனிக்க வேண்டும்.

article_content: Britain's mountain hares survive some of the harshest conditions on the island, especially in the Scottish Highlands. For the past three years, photographer and mountain guide Andy Howard has shared their environment, braving freezing temperatures, blizzards, and snowstorms to capture stunning images of these typically shy animals. Howard states that mountain hares are among Britain's few truly native mammals, having existed here since the last ice age. Howard emphasizes that understanding a species requires spending substantial time with it in its natural habitat. Recalling a particularly challenging day a few weeks ago, he describes enduring persistent blizzards and wading through deep snowdrifts. Despite the difficult conditions, he photographs the hares throughout the year to document their lives in all seasons, even during the severest winter storms. Over three years, Howard has focused on the Mountain Hares of the Cairngorms project, developing a bond with at least one hare that now feels comfortable around him. He often spends several hours with this hare at a time, noting that the animal sometimes relaxes enough to fall asleep in his presence. As part of his ongoing project, Howard visited the same mountain hare repeatedly over a 23-day period, capturing a series of images showing the hare's fur transforming from brown in the summer to thick white in the winter. This adaptation helps the hares blend into their snowy surroundings, which is crucial for survival when winter snow arrives. Mountain hares are native to Britain, surviving since the last ice age, and are now rarely found below 500 meters in the UK. Their range extends from Scotland to other parts of Europe, including Scandinavia and Siberia. They are smaller than the common European hare and are adapted for cold, mountainous environments. In winter, mountain hares' fur changes from brown to white, providing camouflage against predators such as eagles and foxes. However, they are also hunted for sport and sometimes culled due to concerns about tick-borne viruses affecting grouse. Research by the British Trust for Ornithology shows that local mountain hare populations in Scotland have declined by 43% since 1995. Howard explains that mountain hares are among the few truly native mammals in the UK. Through the year, their fur changes from white in winter to mottled and then brown with a greyish tint in summer, which can appear bluish, leading to the local nickname 'blue hares.' Mountain hares inhabit high Scottish mountains and often live on grouse moors, which sometimes causes conflict with gamekeepers. Unlike rabbits, mountain hares do not dig burrows but use shallow scrapes, and in winter, they may be covered entirely by snow except for their heads. The snow helps insulate them against bitter winds. Howard spends much of his time photographing and guiding other wildlife photographers in the Cairngorms. He notes that photographing mountain hares requires patience and understanding of their behavior, as they often remain still for long periods. Fieldcraft and appropriate clothing are essential for successful wildlife photography in these extreme conditions. The mountain hare's seasonal change in coat color is a remarkable adaptation to its environment.

Entrusting the best man with your wedding bands can be risky. Instead, one couple relied on technology, using a drone to deliver the rings during their recent wedding ceremony. At their nuptials in Mafra, near Lisbon, Portugal, on September 27, the bride and groom, Hugo and Lara, received their rings by drone, which was remotely piloted by their friend Tim. The drone flew down the aisle during their vows, while fellow guests Ana and Pedro collected the rings from a box attached to the unmanned vehicle and handed them to the couple. The couple initially hesitated with the sci-fi idea but agreed just five days before the ceremony. There was some last-minute panic, as rain forced the wedding indoors and required adjustments to the drone for indoor delivery. The drone's camera captured the entire moment, which delighted the guests. After the ceremony, the drone also filmed some footage of the couple and their guests.

Drones are becoming increasingly popular with wedding photographers for their ability to capture unique aerial perspectives. Major companies such as Amazon, Google, and pizza restaurants have announced plans to use drones for deliveries, though strict aviation regulations have slowed progress.

article_content: This photo illustration shows the ChatGPT logo at an office in Washington, DC, on March 15, 2023. The company behind the ChatGPT app, which is known for generating essays, poems, and computer code on demand, released an eagerly anticipated update to its artificial intelligence (AI) technology on March 14, 2023, said to be safer and more accurate than prior versions. (Photo by Stefani Reynolds/AFP via Getty Images)  Here are five notable tech developments from this week and their potential impact on your business:  1 – Considering ChatGPT for accounting? Think again. As ChatGPT is increasingly used in professional contexts, it displays some shortcomings in accounting. Professor David Wood of Brigham Young University led a study assessing ChatGPT’s accuracy on accounting exams: it scored 47.4%, notably below students’ 76.7%. The AI stumbled particularly with math-heavy and managerial assessments. (Source: ZDNet) Why it matters: Experts note that such problems require logical reasoning, which ChatGPT isn’t yet fully built to handle. In fields like law, engineering, accounting, or medicine, ChatGPT can assist, but expert oversight is critical.  2 – Grant Assistant streamlines grant proposals with AI. Four professionals in non-profits and international development launched Grant Assistant, an AI-powered tool to help with the grant writing process. (Source: TechCrunch) Why it matters: Grant Assistant aims to assist, not replace, proposal development. The AI offers users guidance and suggestions for organizing their projects, potentially helping nonprofits save time and submit more proposals.  3 – LegalZoom and Novo partner to expand small business access to vital legal and financial services. Business banking provider Novo and legal tech company LegalZoom teamed up to simplify financial and legal processes for entrepreneurs and startups. (Source: Novo) Why it matters: Users can use LegalZoom to create an LLC and easily open a business banking account with Novo, streamlining the process. The partnership also provides trusted legal resources and direct financial access. Brad Paterson, Novo’s EVP of Marketing, noted that LegalZoom’s integration into Novo furthers their all-in-one small business solution.  4 – Google launches features to help merchants stand out for the holidays. Google has introduced the 'Small Business Attribute' to boost merchant visibility this season. (Source: Google) Why it matters: This attribute appears on Google Maps during relevant product or service searches, tagging businesses as 'small business.' Eligible merchants can add this through their Business Profile or Merchant Center, and some will get it automatically based on products, locations, or web traffic. Google’s AI-powered Product Studio will also help customize inventory with holiday themes. Many consumers said they value buying from local small businesses.  5 – New AI transforms websites for a more personal user experience. Research engineer Amelia Wattenberger showcased Adept, her startup’s software, which reconfigures websites well beyond standard formats. (Source: Fast Company) Why it matters: Adept can restructure site text and images to provide a unique user experience. Wattenberger suggests this represents the future—websites becoming more personalized, customizable, and accessible to everyone.

Ted Sarandos, co-CEO of Netflix, has stated that he and other studio executives want to end the actors strike, which has lasted for over three months, and see everyone return to work. However, Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, SAG-AFTRA’s chief negotiator, called Sarandos’s statement insincere. 

"Talking about putting people back to work while refusing to negotiate is just spin," Crabtree-Ireland told Deadline, following Sarandos’s comments during Netflix’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday.

Last week, negotiations between the AMPTP and leading studio CEOs were suspended after disagreements about SAG-AFTRA’s proposed revenue-sharing model. Sarandos said talks had started well, but momentum was lost when the union proposed a "subscriber levy unrelated to viewing or success."

Representatives for the AMPTP in bargaining included Sarandos, Warner Bros. Discovery’s David Zaslav, NBCUniversal’s Donna Langley, and Disney’s Bob Iger. They ended discussions abruptly on October 11, later informing Crabtree-Ireland and SAG-AFTRA president Fran Drescher that they would not return after nine days of intermittent meetings.

Studios and streamers argued that the union’s plan—which they estimated would cost $800 million annually—would be economically unsustainable. SAG-AFTRA, meanwhile, accused studios of inflating the proposal’s cost and using aggressive negotiation tactics, similar to those previously used against the Writers Guild of America.

Crabtree-Ireland challenged Sarandos's claim that the CEOs are totally devoted to ending the strike, insisting that the real solution is for studios to resume negotiations. "We have been and remain ready to continue talks – every day. It is irresponsible for the companies to continue refusing to negotiate. It hurts their employees, the industry, and their shareholders."

Tomorrow will mark the 98th day of the ongoing actors’ strike. Despite Netflix’s claim that discussions are ongoing, there are currently no scheduled negotiations between SAG-AFTRA and either the AMPTP or studio executives.

"பணிக்கு திரும்ப வேண்டும் என்று பேசுகிறவர்களே உரையாடலில் இருக்க மறுப்பது வெறும் நாடகம்" என்று கிராப்ட்ரீ-அயர்லாந்து Deadline-க்கு கூறினார். இந்தப் பேச்சு Netflix இன் மூன்றாம் காலாண்டு வருமான அனுமதிக் கூட்டத்தில் நடந்தது.

AMPTP-க்கு பதில் வழங்கிய தலைவர்கள் சராண்டோஸ், Warner Bros. Discovery-யின் டேவிட் சாஸ்லாவ், NBCUniversal-ன் டொன்னா லாங்க்லி, Disney-யின் பாப் ஐகர் ஆகியோர் உட்பட இருந்தனர். அவர்கள் அக்டோபர் 11-ஆம் தேதி பேச்சுவார்த்தையை திடீரென்று முடித்து, பின்னர் கிராப்ட்ரீ-அயர்லாந்து மற்றும் SAG-AFTRA தலைவர் ஃபிரான் டிரெஸ்சர் ஆகியோருக்கு திரும்ப வர முடியாது எனத் தெரிவித்தனர். இந்த விவாதங்கள் ஒன்பது நாட்கள் இடைமறையாக நடந்தது.

ஸ்டூடியோக்களும் ஸ்ட்ரீமிங் நிறுவனங்களும் SAG-AFTRA முன்வைத்த திட்டம் ஆண்டுக்கு $800 மில்லியன் செலவாகும் என்பதால் பொருளாதாரம் மிக்க சிக்கல் என மதித்தனர். SAG-AFTRA ஸ்டூடியோக்கள் திட்ட செலவை அதிகப்படுத்திக் காட்டிவிட்டதாகவும், முன்னர் எழுத்தாளர் சங்கத்துடன் செய்த கடுமையான பேச்சு முறையை மீண்டும் பயன்படுத்த முயற்சி செய்கிறார்கள் என குற்றம் சாட்டியது.

CEO-க்கள் வேலைநிறுத்தத்தை முடிக்க முழுமையாக உறுதிபூண்டிருக்கிறார்கள் என சராண்டோஸின் கருத்தை கிராப்ட்ரி-அயர்லாந்து எதிர்த்து, ஸ்டூடியோ நிர்வாகிகள் உரையாடலை மீண்டும் தொடங்க வேண்டும் என்றார். "நாங்கள் நாடு முழுவதும் நாள்தோறும் உரையாடல்காக தயார். உரையாடலில் ஈடுபட மறைப்பது பணியாளர்கள், தொழில்நுட்பம் மற்றும் முதலீட்டாளர்களுக்கு தீங்கு" என அவர் கூறினார்.

Yvonne Esquiline, a resident of Georgetown, Texas, believes she saw a divine image on the back of a moth she found clinging to her home. The moth, an Imperial moth nearly as large as a human hand, displayed brown and yellow markings that Esquiline and her family thought resembled the face of Jesus. ‘At first it looked like Jesus,’ Esquiline said, adding that she still feels the same after further inspection.

For Esquiline, the moth’s colors carried deeper significance: she interprets the brown as representing important news and the yellow as a sign relating to her home. Esquiline told KXAN she sees the moth as a message from God, indicating that good news is on the way and encouraging her to keep hope alive—particularly as she hopes for the means to pay for her daughter’s education.

Not everyone saw the same image; some viewers thought they noticed the face of the Devil, which Esquiline admits was a bit unsettling after looking at it for a long time. Nevertheless, she is not letting doubters shake her faith. The moth remained at her home for a day before flying away, leaving Esquiline and her family hopeful that its good luck may visit another household next.

article_content: Tag Heuer Introduces Limited Edition Watches for the Year of the Dragon In 2024, Tag Heuer, one of the world’s most recognized watchmakers, is unveiling two exclusive timepieces in celebration of the Year of the Dragon and the Lunar New Year. Officially revealed on November 13, 2023, these watches combine Tag Heuer’s renowned racing heritage with the vibrant culture of China—a fusion of innovation and tradition designed for the wrist. Singular Zodiac Tribute The dragon stands out in the Chinese Zodiac as the only mythical creature, symbolizing power and charisma. To honor this emblem, Tag Heuer crafted the limited editions using gold and steel, complemented by red alligator leather straps and decorative accents—a color palette chosen to pay tribute to the Chinese Dragon. The steel edition features a sunray-brushed silver dial, while the gold edition incorporates a sunray-brushed 18K 5N pink gold dial. Both editions are distinguished yet refined, with indexes plated in rhodium and 18K 5N pink gold and finished with a unique red lacquer for a warm, elegant hue. Distinctive Case and Dial Details Each dial includes subdials at the 3 and 9 o’clock positions—design elements that evoke the iconic panda face, a nod to Chinese heritage. However, instead of the typical black, these ‘eyes’ are rendered in a vivid red azure. Adding further to their exclusivity, each steel watch is numbered out of a total of 300, with gold versions numbered out of just 50, engraved on the caseback. Technical Excellence Both watches are powered by the calibre Heuer 02 automatic movement and protected by a domed sapphire crystal with double anti-reflective coating. They offer water resistance up to 100 meters and feature Super-LumiNova-coated hour, minute hands, and indexes for enhanced visibility. The caseback showcases the intricate movement alongside an artistic depiction of a Chinese Dragon. With their striking design and premium craftsmanship, these watches represent a rare and meaningful addition to any collection.

The historic Toluca Lake estate of Bob and Dolores Hope is now on the market with an asking price of $27.5 million. Spanning more than five acres, the property features a 15,000-square-foot mansion, a private one-hole golf course, and both indoor and outdoor swimming pools. A guest house, staff quarters, and a spacious 4,000-square-foot office also form part of this expansive estate on Moorpark Street, where the Hopes entertained Hollywood celebrities and U.S. presidents from 1939 until Bob's death in 2003 and Dolores's passing in 2011. Conveniently located near the Lakeside Golf Club, the estate's next owners could also count singer Miley Cyrus as a neighbor, according to the Los Angeles Times.

The main house was commissioned by the Hopes in 1939, designed by Robert Finkelhor, and later remodeled in the 1950s by prominent architect John Elgin Woolf, who added contemporary touches. The property boasts mature trees, an extensive rose garden, and plenty of sunlight that bathes the outdoor pool.

The estate, which now covers four parcels totaling 5.16 acres, has grown through the years as the Hopes acquired adjoining lands. Amenities include a billiard room, chef’s kitchen, a grand living room with floor-to-ceiling glass doors overlooking the grounds, and a curved glass wall in the formal dining area. The upstairs hosts four bedroom suites, including a master wing with his-and-her bedrooms, bathrooms, closets, and a shared study. In total, the main house features six bedrooms and seven bathrooms, plus a two-bedroom guest house and two-bedroom staff quarters. Interiors are staged with contemporary furnishings.

Additional features include a sweeping spiral staircase, polished wood wet bar, library with wood paneling and fireplace, and numerous terraces connecting indoor and outdoor living. A large motor court, rose garden, and sports facilities round out the estate.

Bob Hope, a legendary entertainer known for meeting presidents, starring in films, and entertaining on USO tours, lived here from 1939 until his death at 100 in 2003. Dolores, his wife since 1934, died in 2011 at 102. Hope was considered one of California's largest individual landowners, holding an estimated 10,000 acres in the San Fernando Valley at one point.

The Toluca Lake estate is the final property from the Hopes' impressive real estate holdings to be listed. In December 2012, two Palm Springs properties owned by the couple were listed for $659,000 and $469,000 each.

Recently, an auction of golf memorabilia and other items from the Hopes' homes was expected to generate more than $500,000. According to Jade Mills, the estate’s director, 'It screams Hollywood.' At one point, President Richard Nixon’s helicopter landed on the back lawn so he could play golf at the nearby club. The estate’s extensive lawn doubles as a golf fairway. As Linda Hope, their daughter, recently managed the sale of her parents' possessions, the legacy and allure of the Hope estate remain strong.

1939 முதல் பாப் 2003-ல், டொலோரஸ் 2011-ல் மரணிக்கும் வரை ஹாலிவுட் பிரபலங்கள் மற்றும் அமெரிக்க ஜனாதிபதிகளை வரவேற்று வந்த இந்த பொழுது போக்குத் தம்பதிகள், மூர் பார்க்க் வீதியில் உள்ள சொத்தின் வழியாக பலரையும் உற்சாகப்படுத்தினார்கள். இந்த வீடு லேக்சைட் கால்ஃப் கிளப்பிற்கு அருகிலுள்ளதால், பாடகி மைலி சைரசும் அண்டை பழக்கமாக இருக்கிறார் என லாஸ் ஏஞ்சல்ஸ் டைம்ஸ் தெரிவித்துள்ளது.

முக்கிய இல்லம் 1939-இல் பாப் மற்றும் டொலோர்ஸ் ஹோப்பின் கோரிக்கையில் ரொபர்ட் பிங்கெல்ஹோர் வடிவமைத்தார்; 1950-களில் புகழ்பெற்ற கட்டிடக் கலைஞர் ஜான் எல்ஜின் வூல்ஃப் நவீன அம்சங்களைச் சேர்த்தார். வயதான மரங்கள், விரிவான பூந்தோட்டம் மற்றும் அதிக வெளிச்சம் கொண்ட வெளிக்குளிர் நீச்சல் குளம், இந்த சொத்தின் அழகாக்கும் அம்சங்களாக இருக்கின்றன.

நான்கு நிலப்பகுதியை இசைந்து கொண்டுள்ள இந்த சொத்து, ஹோப்புகள் அருகிலுள்ள நிலங்களை சேர்த்து பெரிதாக்கப்பட்டது. பிலியார்ட் அறை, திறமையான சமையலறை, தரை முதல் மேல்சுவருக்கான கண்ணாடிக் கதவுகள் கொண்ட பெரிய ஹாலும், வளைவான கண்ணாடி சுவர் கொண்ட உணவு அறையும் உள்ளன. மேல்மாடியில் நான்கு படுக்கை அறை சுவிட்கள் மற்றும் 'மாஸ்டர்' பகுதியில் தனி உடைய படுக்கை, குளியலும் மற்றும் பொதுவாகப் பகிர்ந்துக் கொள்ளும் படிப்பு அறை உண்டு. மொத்தமாக, முக்கிய இல்லத்தில் ஆறு படுக்கை அறைகள், ஏழு குளியலறைகள், இரண்டு படுக்கை அறையும் கொண்ட விருந்தினர் வீடு, பணியாளர் குவாட்டர்ஸ் ஆகியவை உள்ளன. உள்ளமைவு நவீன அலங்காரத்துடன் பொருந்துகிறது.

மேலும் வளைந்த சுருண்ட படிக்கட்டு, மெருகூட்டப்பட்ட மரம் கொண்ட வெட் பார், நூலகம், பல திறந்த மற்றும் மூடிய இடங்கள் இணைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளன. பெரிய கற்கள் அமைக்கப்பட்ட முகப்புப் பகுதி, பூந்தோட்டம் மற்றும் விளையாட்டு வசதிகள் இதில் இடம்பெற்று வருகின்றன.

பிரபல பொழுதுபோக்கு நகைச்சுவைஞர் பாப் ஹோப், ஜனாதிபதிகளை சந்தித்து, திரைப்படங்களில் நடித்து, உலகம் முழுவதும் USO நிகழ்வுகளில் கலந்துகொண்டவர். அவர் 1939 முதல் 2003ல் (100 வயதில்) உயிரிழக்கும் வரையிலும்முதல் இந்த வீட்டில் வாழ்ந்தார். டொலோரஸ், 1934ல் திருமணம் செய்துகொண்டவர், 2011ல் 102 வயதில் இறந்தார். கலிபோர்னியாவின் மிகப்பெரும் தனியார் நில உரிமையாளர்களில் ஒருவராக ஹோப் கருதப்பட்டார் – சான் பெர்னாண்டோ பள்ளத்தாக்கில் மட்டும் 10,000 ஏக்கர் நிலம்.

ஹோப் தம்பதிகளின் ஆடம்பர சொத்து பட்டியலில் இறுதியானது இந்த டோலுகா லேக் சொத்து. 2012 டிசம்பரில், பாலம் ஸ்பிரிங்ஸில் இருந்த மற்ற இரு சொத்துக்கள் முறையே $659,000 மற்றும் $469,000 கோரப்பட்டன.

சமீபத்தில் ஹோப் தம்பதிகளின் வீடுகளிலிருந்து கால்ஃப் நினைவுச்சின்னங்கள் உள்ளிட்ட சொத்துக்கள் ஏலில் இடம் பெற்று $500,000க்கு மேல் வரவழைக்கும் என எதிர்பார்க்கப்பட்டது. 'இது ஹாலிவுட் முழுவதுமாகத் தெரிகிறது' என 관리자 ஜேட் மில்ஸ் கூறினார். ஜனாதிபதி ரிச்சர்டு நிக்ஸனின் ஹெலிகாப்டர், அருகிலுள்ள கால்ஃப் கிளப்பில் விளையாட வீட்டு பின்புறம் இறக்கப்பட்டது. இந்தச் சொத்து பல்கலைக்கழக புல்வெளியை ஒத்த பெரும் புல்வெளியையும் கொண்டுள்ளது. அவர்களின் மகள் லிண்டா சமீபத்தில் பெற்றோர் சொத்துக்களை விற்றதை மேற்பார்வை செய்துள்ளார்; ஹோப் தம்பதிகளின் பாரம்பரியமும் புகழும் தொடர்ந்து ஒளிர்கிறது.

article_content: Several firework displays and bonfire events scheduled for this weekend in Lincolnshire have been cancelled due to adverse weather conditions. Storm Babet and Storm Ciarán have left the ground waterlogged, and more rain is forecast in the coming days. While some organizers will try to reschedule, most say cancellation was the only viable option. Saturday's fireworks display and night taxiway run at the Lincolnshire Aviation Centre in East Kirkby is among the cancelled events. Centre officials explained that recent rainfall over the past two weeks left car parks and the grass landing strip unsafe for use. A statement on the centre's website said: 'Customer safety is our main concern, and the current condition of the car parks means we cannot guarantee safe entry and exit for vehicles and visitors.' Ticketholders will receive a refund. The Caistor and District Lions Club has also cancelled its display, as has the planned event in Bourne. Both were set for Saturday. Alford Cricket Club has said it will now be unable to safely host the town's fireworks event on Saturday, but hopes to reschedule it. Spilsby Rotary Club has also cancelled its fireworks event, originally due on Sunday, owing to waterlogged grounds—a decision described as 'not taken lightly.' For more updates, follow BBC East Yorkshire and Lincolnshire on Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), and Instagram. You can share your story ideas at yorkslincs.news@bbc.co.uk.

article_content: Carl Frampton will challenge Kiko Martinez for the IBF world super-bantamweight title on September 6 in Belfast. The bout will take place in a specially constructed venue at the Titanic launch site, adjacent to the museum and historic cranes. With around 16,000 fans expected, this event is set to be the largest boxing audience in Northern Ireland's history. Promoter Barry McGuigan, taking inspiration from outdoor venues like Wembley Stadium and Caesars Palace, has organized the event with a rapid setup and take-down to accommodate the Belfast Proms. VIPs will experience the event from notable Titanic-related spaces, such as a restored stairway, the slipway, and the original tug. Support for this large-scale event comes from First Minister Peter Robinson. Frampton is focused and preparing hard, mindful of local expectations but aware of the difficulty of the challenge. This fight marks a rematch—Frampton previously defeated Martinez, but Martinez has since gained the IBF title and approaches the match with confidence. McGuigan hopes the open-air setting creates a memorable experience, while expressing faith in a positive result for Frampton. Frampton vs Martinez will be broadcast live by BoxNation on September 6.

Back in 2008, Scott Douglas and his brother-in-law, Rich St. Pierre, survived a terrifying ordeal when a storm threw them from their fishing boat, the Queen Bee, off the Nantucket coast. Despite tumultuous seas, a survival kit that also fell overboard helped them swim for an hour to an island, where they called for help. Their boat, however, was left missing.

More than three years later, the Queen Bee astonishingly reappeared off Spain’s coast, leaving Spanish authorities and the former owners stunned. The 26-foot boat was encrusted with mold, rust, and barnacles, but still had both motors attached and ‘Nantucket’ written clearly on its side. Spanish media noted that items like a first-aid kit, radio, fire extinguishers, and maps of the U.S. East Coast were still aboard.

Douglas, who now lives in New Jersey, was amazed to see photos of his long-lost boat, noting how much it had changed. St. Pierre appreciated the closure, although he was curious about the boat’s mysterious voyage. The U.S. Coast Guard’s Lt Joe Klinker suggested that the Gulf Stream likely carried the Queen Bee across the Atlantic—a rare but possible occurrence. Douglas has no desire to recover the boat but thinks its journey would make for a great story for his grandchildren.

article_content: Israeli forces operating in the occupied West Bank killed at least eight Palestinians within a 24-hour period, according to Palestinian health officials on Sunday. This occurred as a fragile pause in fighting between Israel and Hamas in the Gaza Strip entered its third day. Violence in the West Bank has escalated since Hamas attacked Israel on October 7, sparking a devastating war in Gaza. Israeli forces have killed dozens of Palestinians and arrested hundreds in the West Bank. Jewish settlers in the region have also increased attacks. The Palestinian Health Ministry reported that five Palestinians were killed in Jenin, a militant stronghold, while three others were killed in separate areas of the West Bank since Saturday morning. Among the dead was a teenager from al-Bireh in central West Bank. The Israeli military stated that forces entered the Jenin refugee camp to arrest a Palestinian suspected of killing an Israeli father and son at a car wash earlier this year. The military did not mention clashes or Palestinian fatalities in its statement, noting only that operations were ongoing in the area. Officials said the military is investigating reports of other incidents. Debris was scattered across streets in the densely-populated Jenin refugee camp, with at least one house showing significant damage. According to the Palestinian news agency Wafa, Israeli snipers were positioned on rooftops and military bulldozers damaged roads and infrastructure, although these reports could not be independently verified. Following the Hamas assault, Israel imposed tighter restrictions on the West Bank, closing crossings and checkpoints between Palestinian towns. The recent violence comes after more than a year of increased Israeli raids and arrests in the West Bank, as well as deadly Palestinian attacks on Israelis. Even before the Hamas assault, 2023 was the deadliest year for Palestinians in the West Bank in over twenty years. Israel and Hamas have temporarily halted fire, allowing more aid into Gaza and facilitating a prisoner and hostage exchange. The Israeli offensive in Gaza has killed more than 13,300 Palestinians, according to the Health Ministry in the Hamas-run Gaza government, which does not distinguish between civilians and fighters. Large parts of Gaza have been destroyed, forcing about 1.7 million Palestinians to flee their homes. During last month's attack, Hamas and other militants killed roughly 1,200 people in Israel and took about 240 hostages. Several dozen Israeli soldiers have also died since ground operations in Gaza began. Israel took control of the West Bank, Gaza Strip, and east Jerusalem during the 1967 Mideast war. article_content: Celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay paid £41,700 after failing to attend two New Zealand charity fundraisers for Matisse Reid, an 11-year-old schoolgirl who needed an organ transplant because of a rare intestinal disorder. Ramsay, who was 45 at the time, missed a June 2010 fundraising event due to his mother's heart attack. He rescheduled but had to cancel again later in the year for business reasons. Duco Events, an Auckland-based company, initially sought £1 million in damages for Ramsay’s non-appearance at the sold-out events, but they settled for £41,700. As part of the agreement, NZ$100,000 (£51,500) will be donated to Matisse Reid and her charity, Chance2Eat. The donation is reportedly equal to Ramsay’s appearance fee for the charity events. Matisse, from Napier, has been undergoing life-saving treatment in Pittsburgh, U.S., for the past five years. She received a transplant last year but still needs ongoing medical care. Matisse’s mother, Jodee Reid, described the donation as 'generous, but unexpected.' She said both Ramsay and David Higgins from Duco Events empathized with their situation and made the donation together. The family appreciated being kept out of the dispute and are grateful for the donation. Jodee Reid mentioned that Matisse may require more treatment in the future, so the funds will be reserved for her care. Despite her illness, Matisse has always had a passion for food. The settlement occurred during Ramsay's visit to New Zealand, where he narrowly avoided injury when a fan accidentally dropped a sharp knife at an Auckland meet-and-greet event.

Recent figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) highlight a major change in Britain’s housing landscape: home ownership fell to 64% in 2011, the lowest rate since the mid-1980s. This drop signals a dramatic rise in people renting homes, reversing a long-standing trend of increasing home ownership. Back in 2001, 69% of households owned their homes, but by 2011, that proportion had declined, with renters making up 36% of households.

London stands out, with half of its households renting—the highest rate in the UK. Across the country, surging property prices, sluggish wage growth, and tougher mortgage requirements have made it much harder for first-time buyers to afford a home. As a result, between 2001 and 2011, there were 749,000 fewer households with mortgages, while private renters increased by 1.7 million to reach 3.6 million. Social housing occupancy dropped slightly to 4.1 million.

The rise in private renting was seen in every region of England and Wales, with the biggest jump in London, followed by the South East and North West. Wales and the North East reported the smallest increases. Over the same period, average house prices for first-time buyers soared by 96%. In 2001, a typical house was six times the average wage; by 2011, it had risen to nine times. Meanwhile, East Dorset has nearly half its homes owned outright without mortgages, while areas like Wokingham and Bracknell have large numbers of mortgaged properties.

The ONS data paints a clear picture: high housing costs and stricter mortgage lending have created a ‘generation rent’, making it much more difficult for many people to become homeowners.

Scottish Health Secretary Michael Matheson is facing criticism over an £11,000 data roaming bill incurred on his parliamentary iPad during a holiday in Morocco. The charges were initially covered with public funds, with Matheson stating the device was used for official work. After media reports emerged, Matheson attributed the bill to an outdated SIM card and agreed to repay the money. He received consistent support from First Minister Humza Yousaf. However, Matheson later admitted in parliament that his sons had used the iPad to watch football via a mobile hotspot.

Timeline of events:

27 December: Matheson travels to Morocco with his wife and two sons for a week-long holiday.

28 December: Matheson contacts the parliament's IT department to report he is overseas and his phone is not working. The parliament's records do not indicate discussions about his iPad. Matheson says he was told he could use the iPad as a mobile hotspot, set up with his son's help.

January: Matheson is informed of the £10,935.74 bill, which includes over £2,000 on 28 December and more than £8,000 in two separate charges on 2 January. He hands the iPad to parliamentary IT for inspection. They verify data usage but do not check browsing history.

March: Without a clear explanation for the charges, Matheson submits an expenses claim to contribute £3,000 from his office, with the remainder covered by parliament.

8 November: The Telegraph reports on the data roaming bill. Matheson's spokesperson maintains the iPad was used for constituency work and the SIM was not updated.

9 November: The First Minister says the charges were legitimate and Matheson should not need to repay them. Matheson learns from his wife that his sons used the iPad during the holiday.

10 November: Matheson announces he will reimburse the full bill after careful consideration and repeats that the device was used for constituency work.

13 November: Matheson denies anyone else used the iPad.

14 November: Matheson informs Yousaf his sons were responsible for the data usage. The Scottish Tories call for Matheson to surrender the iPad for examination, threatening a no-confidence vote if he does not comply.

15 November: Scottish Parliament releases a breakdown of data usage, with opposition MSPs noting it likely involved football streaming.

16 November: Matheson formally admits in parliament that his sons’ streaming caused the charges and states he previously withheld this information to protect his children.

19 November: Yousaf denies being misled but concedes the matter could have been handled better.

article_content: Peter Hesketh, a Catholic deacon, has been sentenced to three and a half years in prison for stealing over £60,000 from an elderly man with dementia. Hesketh persuaded widower Peter Court to give him power of attorney, claiming he would invest the money in safe business opportunities. Instead, Hesketh used the money for gambling, paying off his mortgage, and funding his daughter's wedding. Hesketh, 65, was found guilty of theft at Worcester Crown Court. He met Mr. Court, a former pub landlord, while visiting his pub before Mr. Court became ill. Court gave Hesketh control over his finances, trusting him to manage them wisely. In total, Hesketh took £61,429 from Mr. Court, betting on horse races and covering the mortgage on his £255,000 home in Kidderminster. He also spent £20,000 on his daughter's wedding reception, attended by over 100 guests. After Mr. Court died in 2007 at age 75, his family discovered large sums missing from his account. Despite officiating at Court's funeral, Hesketh was arrested the following year. He claimed Mr. Court paid him £20,000 a year for financial management, but Judge Toby Hooper dismissed this, calling the story 'preposterous'. The judge stated that Hesketh had committed 'a planned and careful series of many thefts' against someone who respected him greatly, and criticized Hesketh for making derogatory remarks about his victim. Prosecutor Paul Mytton said Hesketh, a father of five and deacon since 1992, thought he could get away with it. Defense lawyer Peter Arnold said Hesketh would find prison difficult due to health problems including epilepsy and gout. After the sentencing, Phillipa Charlesworth of West Mercia Police said Hesketh was evasive and dishonest during the investigation. She noted that as power of attorney, he should have acted in Mr. Court's best interests. Monsignor Timothy Menezes, Vicar General of the Archdiocese of Birmingham, expressed sadness over the breach of trust. Hesketh's son-in-law, Carl Berisford-Murray, said the family did not know the wedding was funded with stolen money but are supporting Hesketh.

article_content: Metro trains in Washington, D.C. are becoming busier as more federal workers return to the office a few days each week. However, according to commuters like Gina Adu from Bowie, Maryland, and Damien Doyle from Cheverly, Maryland, trains are still less crowded than before the COVID-19 pandemic. Doyle describes this as 'the new normal.' Nationally, public transit ridership has rebounded to about 80% of pre-pandemic levels, but the patterns have changed. Commuters are now traveling more frequently during the middle of the week and at non-peak hours, resulting in smaller rush hour surges. Robert Puentes, president of the Eno Center for Transportation, notes that remote work has significantly altered traditional workweek commuting habits. This shift has created new challenges for large public transit systems, which previously focused on moving crowds downtown during rush hours. During the pandemic, Congress provided tens of billions of dollars to help transit agencies, but this funding is set to expire next year. Agencies nationwide, including those in Chicago, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Philadelphia, are now facing substantial budget shortfalls due to decreased ridership and inflation. Randy Clarke, general manager of the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA), says WMATA is projecting a $750 million deficit for the coming year and is considering significant service cuts. Clarke warns that drastic reductions could lead to a cycle of falling revenue and further cuts, a situation known as a 'death spiral.' Still, he hopes additional funding can prevent such outcomes. Agencies reliant on passenger fares for revenue now have the greatest financial difficulties, according to Puentes. However, some transit systems with more stable funding, such as those supported by local sales taxes, are faring better. Lindiwe Rennert, a researcher at the Urban Institute, co-authored a new report on strategies for transit agencies to overcome financial hurdles. She emphasizes that mass transit benefits everyone, including those who don't ride it, by reducing road congestion. While bus ridership has returned near pre-pandemic levels overall, the most adaptable transit agencies—in cities like Richmond, Cincinnati, Tucson, and the Seattle area—have managed to increase their number of riders beyond 2019 levels. Julie Timm, CEO of Sound Transit in Seattle, reports that expanding service and reaching more communities have led to record ridership, especially during major events like the MLB All-Star Game and Taylor Swift concerts. Timm believes that investing in consistent, reliable transit service encourages continued and increased usage.
translated_content: வாஷிங்டன், D.C.யில் மெட்ரோ ரயில்கள் மீண்டும் பயணிகளால் நிரம்பத் தொடங்கியுள்ளது, ஏனெனில் கூட்டணி அரசு ஊழியர்கள் வாரத்தில் சில நாட்கள் அலுவலகத்திற்கு திரும்பிக் கொண்டிருக்கிறார்கள். இருப்பினும், போலி, மாரிலாண்ட் பகுதியைச் சேர்ந்த ஜினா அடு மற்றும் செவர்லி, மாரிலாண்ட் பகுதியைச் சேர்ந்த டேமியன் டோயல் போன்ற பயணிகள் கூறுவதாவது, COVID-19 பாண்டமிக்கிற்குப் பிறகு ரயில்கள் முன்பほど பார்க்கும் கூட்டம் இல்லை என்று. டோயல் இதை ‘புதிய வழக்கமான நிலை’ என வர்ணிக்கிறார். நாடு முழுவதும், பொது போக்குவரத்து பயணிகள் எண்ணிக்கை பாண்டமிக்கிற்கு முன்பதை விட சுமார் 80% அளவிற்கு திரும்பியுள்ளது, ஆனால் பயணம் செய்யும் முறைகள் மாறியுள்ளது. பயணிகள் இப்போது வாரத்தின் நடுநாட்களிலும், பிக் அவர் அல்லாத நேரங்களிலும் அதிகம் பயணிக்கிறார்கள்; இதனால், பிக் அவர் கூட்டம் குறைந்துவிட்டது. எனோ டிரான்ஸ்போர்டேஷன் மையத்தின் தலைவர் ராபர்ட் புவென்டெஸ் தெரிவிக்கையில், தொலைவேலை அதிகரிப்பினால் பாரம்பரிய வேலை வார கால கட்டமைப்பு மாற்றமடைந்துள்ளது. இதன் விளைவாக, பெரிய பெருநகரப் பொது போக்குவரத்து அமைப்புகள் முக்கியமான சவால்களை எதிர்கொள்கின்றன. பாண்டமிக் காலத்தில் காங்கிரஸ் டிரான்ஸிட் ஏஜென்சிகளுக்கு பில்லியன் கணக்கான நிதி வழங்கியது, ஆனால் அந்த நிதியுதவி அடுத்த ஆண்டு முடிவடைகிறது. சிகாகோ, சான் ஃபிரான்சிஸ்கோ, லாஸ் ஏஞ்சல்ஸ், பிலடெல்பியா போன்ற நகரங்களின் ஏஜென்சிகள் பயணிகள் எண்ணிக்கையின் கம்மியும், பணவீக்கும் காரணமாக பெரிய பட்ஜெட் பற்றுகளை சந்திக்கின்றன. வாஷிங்டன் மெட்ரோவை இயக்கும் WMATA-வின் நிர்வாக இயக்குனர் ராண்டி கிளார்க், அடுத்த ஆண்டு 750 மில்லியன் டாலர் டெபிசிட் இருக்கும் என்றும், மெட்ரோ சேவையில் கடுமையான குறைப்பு பரிசீலிக்கப்படுவதாகவும் கூறுகிறார். சேவையில் கடுமையான குறைப்பு வந்தால் வருமானம் மேலும் குறையும், மேலும் தொடர்ந்தும் சேவையை குறைக்கும் நிலை ('death spiral') உருவாக முடியும் என எச்சரிக்கிறார். இருப்பினும், இந்த நிலைமை தவிர்க்கப்படலாம் என்று அவர் நம்புகிறார். பயணிகள் கட்டணங்களுக்கு அதிகம் சார்ந்த ஏஜென்சிகள் தற்போதைய நிதி சவால்களில் அதிகமாக பாதிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளன என புவென்டெஸ் கூறுகிறார். ஆனால், விற்பனை வரி போன்ற நிலையான வருவாய் ஆதாரங்களைக் கொண்ட சில அமைப்புகள் நன்றாக நடக்கின்றன. அர்பன் இன்ஸ்டிடியூட்டில் ஆய்வாளரான லிண்டிவி ரெனர்ட் புதிய அறிக்கையொன்று எழுதியுள்ளார், அதில் டிரான்ஸிட் ஏஜென்சிகள் சந்திக்கும் நிதிச் சவால்களை எவ்வாறு சமாளிக்கலாம் என்று பரிந்துரைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. பொது போக்குவரத்தால், பயணிக்காதவர்களுக்கும் பயனுள்ளது; இது சாலை வாகனங்களின் எண்ணிக்கையை குறைக்கும் என ரெனர்ட் கூறுகிறார். பெரும்பாலான இடங்களில் பஸ் பயணிகள் எண்ணிக்கை COVID-19 முன்பு இருந்த அளவுக்கு மீண்டும் வந்துவிட்டது. அதிகமான மாற்றங்களை取りநைக்கும் ஏஜென்சிகள் (ரிச்மண்ட், சின்சினாடி, டூசான், சியாடில்) 2019-ஐவிட அதிக பயணிகள் பெற்றுள்ளன. சியாடில் உள்ள சவுண்ட் டிரான்ஸிடின் தலைவி ஜூலி டிம் சேவை விரிவும் சமூகத்தை மேலும் எட்ட முயற்சியும் பதிவு ரைடர்ஷிப் அளவில் சாதனை கொண்டுவரும் என்று சொல்கிறார், குறிப்பாக MLB ஆல்-ஸ்டார் போட்டி, டெய்லர் ஸ்விஃப்ட் பேர்விழா போன்ற நிகழ்வுகளின்போது. நல்ல, நம்பகமான போக்குவரத்து சேவையில் பங்களிப்பு பயணிகளை அதிகம் திரும்பவும் வரச் செய்யும் என்பதில் அவருக்கு நம்பிக்கை உள்ளது.

article_content:
After more than fifty years, German pharmaceutical company Gruenenthal has issued a public apology for the catastrophic impact its drug, thalidomide, had on thousands of babies and their families worldwide. The apology, delivered by CEO Harald Stock during the dedication of a memorial in Stolberg, Germany, comes after decades of campaigning by survivors and advocates seeking justice and accountability.

Thalidomide, originally marketed as a safe medication, was later linked to severe birth defects when taken by pregnant women. Despite early warnings from medical professionals, evidence suggests Gruenenthal failed to withdraw the drug promptly, maintaining its availability for financial gain. The company's history is further shadowed by allegations that some of its board members in the 1950s had connections to the Nazi regime, notably Otto Ambros, a convicted war criminal.

Recent legal developments have renewed scrutiny of Gruenenthal. In Australia, litigation resulted in a multi-million dollar settlement for survivor Lynette Rowe, with Gruenenthal named in the proceedings. These outcomes have heightened pressure on the company and inspired similar legal actions in Ireland and the UK, while British and Australian firms that distributed thalidomide have also faced accountability.

Survivors argue that Gruenenthal’s apology is inadequate and call for comprehensive reparations. They contend that the company ignored evidence of thalidomide’s harm, concealed crucial documents, and failed to accept full responsibility. Campaigners demand that Gruenenthal and its owner, the Wirtz family, provide proper financial support to ensure survivors can live independently with necessary care and assistance.

The demand for justice continues, as thalidomide survivors, now aging and living with lifelong disabilities, seek meaningful redress for the harm caused by the drug. The article reflects the perspective of survivor Geoff Adams-Spink, who maintains that both moral and legal responsibility lies with Gruenenthal and urges further action.

article_content: The controversy surrounding Nevada rancher Cliven Bundy escalated rapidly. Many conservative supporters could not have anticipated that Bundy would make overtly racist comments. While Bundy refused to acknowledge the federal government's authority over the land he used—a position reminiscent of historical secessionists—he became a conservative symbol for challenging government overreach. However, Bundy drew widespread condemnation after publicly making racist remarks about Black Americans, suggesting they were better off under slavery. Despite criticism, Bundy defended his statements in a CNN interview, claiming he was not wrong. Right-wing figures such as Sean Hannity, who previously promoted Bundy's cause, faced criticism after Bundy's comments were revealed. The article highlights that Bundy's opposition to federal subsidies did not extend to those benefiting ranchers like himself, but rather targeted programs like food assistance, particularly for minority recipients. Many politicians, including Republicans who had initially supported Bundy, later denounced his remarks. The piece questions why Bundy had gained support despite a history of defying the law by grazing cattle on federally owned land without payment, threatening armed resistance to law enforcement, and disregarding court orders. The article contrasts media and political reactions to Bundy with hypothetical scenarios involving left-leaning or minority groups in similar standoffs, implying inconsistent standards. article_content: Digital wallet competition is intensifying, especially during the busy Black Friday season. While Black Friday weekend is significant for retailers, other global events like Singles Day and Diwali now generate even higher sales volumes. (Diwali recently reached INR 3.75 lakh crore, or about US$45 billion.)  Key retail and technology updates:  Amazon has partnered with Hyundai to sell cars through its platform. Although these sales may have a limited immediate impact on Amazon’s overall revenue, this move signifies expanding support for more high-value online purchases. Hyundai vehicles will also now include Alexa voice integration. Notably, this announcement comes as Amazon reports layoffs within its Alexa division.  Rite-Aid is closing more stores as part of its bankruptcy process, highlighting ongoing challenges for traditional big-box retailers. In contrast, Miniso, a Chinese retailer known for affordable Japanese-themed products such as Hello Kitty, is opening 20 new stores in the UK. Despite difficult economic conditions there, Miniso’s low-cost cosmetics line could appeal to price-sensitive consumers. COO Saad Usman stated that affordable options may match current market needs.  This expansion of low-cost brands like Miniso occurs as fast fashion and inexpensive retail goods face growing scrutiny. Reports from Vox have criticized the industry for generating waste and raising human rights concerns. The popularity of fast fashion and social media’s role in promoting continuous consumption is sparking wider discussions about overconsumption. Some consumers, especially in Generation Z, are even starting spending strikes through viral trends online.  Apple is actively enhancing its digital wallet, adding more features and data integration to increase consumer value. These updates are launching first in the UK, with plans for future expansion.  Debate continues about self-checkout systems in retail. Marks & Spencer recently noted that self-checkout may enable ‘middle class theft,’ prompting questions about whether a lack of oversight or overreliance on technology increases shoplifting risk.  To address retail theft, some stores are considering vending machines as an alternative to traditional staff. This trend raises concerns over how the retail experience could change if both hands-on engagement and personal service are reduced or lost.  A recent Mindshare and Snapchat study identified six main reasons for social media engagement, suggesting physical stores could benefit from designing experiences that meet more diverse consumer needs beyond just shopping. Enhancing in-store environments could help attract returning customers.

விமர்சித்திருக்கின்றன. ஃபாஸ்ட் ஃபேஷனுக்கும், சமூக ஊடகங்களும் அதிக வாடிக்கையாளர்களை அதிகம் வாங்க தூண்டும் சூழலை உருவாக்கியுள்ளது. இது அதிகமாக வாங்கும் பழக்கம் குறித்த ஆதங்கத்தையும், சிலர் (முக்யமாக ஜெனரேஷன் Z) செலவு தவிர்க்கும் 'ஸ்பெண்ட் ஸ்ட்ரைக்' போன்று வேடிக்கை பிரச்சாரம் செய்யும் நிலைக்கும் இந்திய அளவுக்கு கொண்டு வந்துள்ளது.  ஆப்பிள் தனது டிஜிட்டல் வாலெட்டைப் பெருக்கி, கூடுதல் வசதிகளும், தரவு 'மிடில் கிளாஸ் திருட்டை' இது வழிவகுக்கும் என கூறியுள்ளது. கண்காணிப்பு குறைவு மற்றும் தொழில்நுட்பம் சார்ந்ததாக இது உறுதி செய்யப்படுகிறதா என கேள்விகள் எழுகின்றன.  திருட்டை எதிர்க்க, சில கடைகள் பணியாளர்களுக்கு பதிலாக வெண்டிங் மெஷின்களை நிறுவ விரும்புகின்றன. இதனால், கடை அனுபவத்தில் மனித தொடர்பும், நேரடி சேவையும் குறையும் அபாயம் உள்ளது.  மைண்ட்ஷேர் மற்றும் ஸ்னாப்சாட் நடத்திய ஒரு ஆய்வில், சமூக article_content: Bhutan, often hailed as the happiest country in the world, is celebrated for valuing Gross National Happiness (GNH) over GDP. Recently, the kingdom released striking photographs depicting daily life, including a remarkable image of young Buddhist monks captured by King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck himself. The images provide a rare insight into a nation where happiness is the ultimate measure of success, and where material wealth is secondary. Bhutan's concept of GNH was first proposed by former King Jigme Singye Wangchuck in 1972, coinciding with the country's cautious opening to tourism. Retaining almost mythical allure as a Himalayan haven, Bhutan continues to attract curious travelers with its untouched landscapes and vibrant traditions. This week, the nation anticipates a record number of visitors to Thimphu for its inaugural International Festival—a ten-day arts and culture celebration, starting February 14. The event coincides with the fifth King’s 35th birthday and Losar, the Buddhist New Year. The festival will feature eighty artists and performers, including Indian pop star Lucky Ali and Mercury-nominated UK indie folk musician Nick Mulvey, collaborating with Bhutanese talent. Traditional masked dancers will perform alongside contemporary acts, and attendees can participate in talks on happiness, culinary demonstrations by leading local chefs, and the Bhutan International Marathon. The photo series released ahead of the festival includes scenes of young monks at the King's Palace, vibrant prayer flags fluttering over the Himalayas, and portraits capturing daily Bhutanese life. In Bhutan, prayer flags symbolize happiness, long life, prosperity, and spiritual merit, and are believed to guide souls after death. Bhutan's enduring isolation has protected its unique culture and environment. It is the world’s first country to enshrine environmental protection into its constitution, ensuring at least 60% of its land remains forested. Landmarks such as the Dechencholing Palace, Tashichhodzong, and the imposing Buddha Dordenma Statue celebrate the country’s spiritual and artistic heritage. Festival co-director Virginia Galloway emphasizes the event’s goal to position the Bhutan International Festival as a world-class occasion with broad cultural and economic benefits. The focus this year is on fostering collaboration among artists from various disciplines, inspiring new works and approaches. From prayer flag rituals to traditional painting, Bhutan’s dedication to happiness and cultural preservation remains at the forefront, leaving a lasting impression on all who visit.

பொருளாதார செல்வம் இரண்டாம் நிலை. பூட்டானில் GNH முறை முன்னாள் அரசர் ஜிக்மே சிங்கே வாங்சக் 1972-இல் அறிமுகப்படுத்தினார், நாட்டின் சுற்றுலா திறப்புடன் ஒருங்கிணைந்து. இமயமலைக் கொள்ளையின் நடுவே, சொர்க்க நாடாகப் போற்றப்படும் பூட்டான், தன் இயற்கை அழகு, கலாச்சார பாரம்பரியம் ஆகியவற்றால் பயணிகளை இழுத்துக்கொண்டு வருகிறது. இந்த வாரம் திம்புவில் நடைபெறும் முதலாவது சர்வதேச விழா—பத்து நாட்கள் கொண்ட கலை மற்றும் கலாச்சார பெருவிழா, பிப்ரவரி 14-இல் தொடங்குகிறது. இது ஐந்தாவது அரசரின் 35வது பிறந்த நாளும் புத்தாண்டான லோசரையும் கொண்டாடுகிறது. இந்த விழாவில் 80க்கும் மேற்பட்ட கலைஞர்கள், இந்தியப் பாடகர் லக்கி அலி மற்றும் பிரிட்டன் நிக் முல்வே ஆகியோர் உள்ளிட்ட இசைக்கலைஞர்கள் கலந்து கொண்டு, பூட்டானிய கலைஞர்களுடன் ஒத்துழைக்கிறார்கள். பாரம்பரிய முகமூடி நடனங்கள், நவீன நிகழ்ச்சிகள், மகிழ்ச்சி குறித்த உரைகள், பாரம்பரிய சமையல் நிகழ்வுகள் மற்றும் பூட்டான் இன்டர்நேஷனல் மரத்தான் போன்றவை இதில் இடம்பெறுகின்றன. விழாவுக்குப் பிற்போக்காக வெளியிடப்பட்ட படங்களுள், அரச மாளிகை முன்பு உள்ள இளம் முனிவர்கள், இமயமலை மீது பறக்கும் பிரார்த்தனைக் கொடிகள், நாடு முழுக்க பொதுவாழ்க்கையை வெளிப்படுத்தும் கோடிகள் உள்ளன. பூட்டானில், பிரார்த்தனைக் கொடிகள் மகிழ்ச்சி, நீண்ட ஆயுள், செல்வாக்கு, பண்பாட்டை குறிக்கின்றன; இறந்தவர்கள் ஆன்மாவின் வழிகாட்டியாகவும் நம்பப்படுகிறது. பூட்டானின் தொடர்ந்த தனிமை அதன் தனித்துவமான பண்பாட்டு மற்றும் சூழலியலைப் பாதுகாத்துள்ளது. உலகில் முதலில், சுற்றுச்சூழலை அரசியலமைப்பில் பாதுகாப்பதாக பதிவு செய்தது. குறைந்தபட்சம் 60% நிலம் காடாக இருக்க வேண்டும். டெச்சென்கோலிங் அரண்மனை, டாசிச்சோட்சோங், பெரும் புத்தர் தோர்தென்மா சிலை ஆகியவை ஆன்மீகம் மற்றும் கலை பாரம்பரியங்களை வர்ணிக்கின்றன. விழா ஒருங்கிணைப்பாளர் விர்ஜீனியா கலோவே, இந்த விழாவை உலகத் தர பன்முகமாகவும், பாரம்பரிய கலைஞர்களிடம் ஒத்துழைப்பை ஊக்குவிப்பதாகவும் அமைக்க சமூக, பொருளாதார இலக்கை வலியுறுத்துகிறார். பிரார்த்தனை கொடிகளிலிருந்து பாரம்பரிய ஓவியங்கள் வரை, மகிழ்ச்சியும் கலாச்சாரப் பாதுகாப்பும் பூட்டானின் அடையாளமாக உள்ளது; article_content: Real Madrid’s defender Pepe, long known for his fiery temperament on the pitch, has recently demonstrated better discipline and improved form. Real Madrid is gearing up for an away match against Valencia on January 4, aiming to extend their remarkable 22-game winning streak. Elsewhere, Real Madrid coach Carlo Ancelotti told Italian outlet Tuttosport that he sees Juventus as serious Champions League contenders alongside his own team and Bayern Munich, noting that while star players are present, younger players could influence the outcome. article_content: HARARE, Zimbabwe – Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe and the opposition Movement for Democratic Change (MDC) have reached a power-sharing deal, according to South African President Thabo Mbeki. Mbeki, who mediated the talks in Harare on behalf of the Southern African Development Community, announced the agreement and said it would be signed on Monday, but did not provide specific details. The deal comes after months of political deadlock following the March presidential election, which left Zimbabwe without a Cabinet. During the opening of parliament on August 26, opposition lawmakers publicly heckled Mugabe. MDC leader Morgan Tsvangirai secured the most votes in the March election but did not win outright, leading to a runoff as per official results. Tsvangirai withdrew from the June 27 runoff, citing violence and intimidation against opposition supporters by Mugabe’s allies. A major challenge in the negotiations was determining how much power Mugabe would keep. Tsvangirai had insisted he would only agree to a deal if Mugabe reduced his authority and took on a more ceremonial presidential role. UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon welcomed the agreement, expressing hope that it would foster lasting peace and improve human rights and living conditions for Zimbabweans. Meanwhile, Zimbabwe continues to struggle with hyperinflation. In August, the Central Statistical Office reported inflation at 11.2 million percent, the highest in the world. Economists suggest the real figure may be even higher, with Kingdom Bank estimating inflation at over 20 million percent. The crisis has severely weakened Zimbabwe’s currency and made it hard for citizens to access basic goods, electricity, fuel, and medicine.

Forwards: Kelechi Iheanacho, Samuel Chukwueze, Moses Simon, Ademola Lookman, Victor Osimhen, Taiwo Awoniyi, Terem Moffi, Victor Boniface.

These fixtures are a vital part of Nigeria’s build-up to their World Cup qualifying campaign.

article_content: Vicky Pryce was told it would be her fault if her husband lost an election due to a driving ban, a court heard yesterday. Pryce’s eldest daughter, Georgia Beesley, explained that her mother was angry, upset, and felt bullied by Chris Huhne’s demands that she accept his speeding points on her driving license in 2003. Mrs Beesley, 37, a management consultant, became emotional as she recounted how the Liberal Democrat politician persisted about the speeding points until her mother relented. She said, 'I remember speaking to my mother, and she told me that Chris had been caught speeding and was trying to get her to take the points. If he took the points, he would have lost his license. He was very insistent. He didn’t want to lose the election, as he was standing for election and needed to travel regularly to Eastleigh. He said that if she didn’t take the points, it would be her fault if he wasn’t elected.’ Pryce’s daughter gave evidence on the fourth day of Pryce's trial for perverting the course of justice at Southwark Crown Court. Mrs Beesley, who had moved out of the family home in Clapham when the incident happened, maintained regular contact with her mother, who was managing the care of two troubled teenagers at the time. Beesley testified that her mother felt pressured into signing the form that stated she was driving. She said that signing the form led to further conflict within the family, as Pryce later had to drive Huhne due to his loss of license, causing resentment. Chris Huhne, who later left Pryce for his aide Carina Trimingham, has admitted to perverting the course of justice. article_content: Gable Tostee, a 28-year-old accused of murder, has been released from prison on strict bail conditions set by the Supreme Court of Queensland. He is prohibited from consuming alcohol, using social media platforms such as Facebook, Tinder, and Bodyspace, and is not permitted to drive. Tostee is also banned from entering the Surfers Paradise nightclub strip and cannot leave his residence after dark. Previously a regular at clubs like Sin City and others in Surfers Paradise, Tostee was banned from some venues for inappropriate behavior. Tostee awaits trial for the alleged August murder of Warriena Wright, who died after meeting him via a mobile dating app while visiting the Gold Coast. While on bail, Tostee is allowed outside only between 6am and 6pm, and must be accompanied when reporting to Broadbeach Police Station, as his driver's license is suspended for drink driving. He may attend alcohol rehabilitation and work with his father at World Carpets under parental supervision. Tostee will reside at his parents' home in Carrara and must comply with a strict curfew. According to Justice Debra Mullins, Tostee will be subject to random alcohol testing. He has been receiving psychiatric treatment since 2009 for social anxiety, obsessive compulsive disorder, and depression, and is not permitted to use any social media. After his arrest, Tostee used Facebook to declare his innocence and state he had lost contact with most people. Prosecutors consider Tostee a flight risk; his parents posted $200,000 as surety, equivalent to their house equity. If bail is breached, they could lose their home. Police expect to finalize evidence against Tostee by April, with a trial possibly set for 2016. His next court appearance is on January 12 at Southport Magistrates Court. Tostee faces additional charges from separate incidents, including high-range drink driving and allegedly assaulting or obstructing police. Tostee maintains his innocence and, through his lawyer, has expressed his wish to clear his name.

Stefanie Janikiewicz, a 25-year-old teacher from Thurstaston on the Wirral, drove nearly seven miles the wrong way along the hard shoulder of a motorway after consuming a large quantity of alcohol. She was almost three times over the legal limit and told police she mistakenly believed she was heading in the opposite direction. Stefanie is the daughter of Dr. Stefan Janikiewicz, a leading expert in alcohol and drug abuse and a prominent advocate for the introduction of minimum alcohol pricing.

Dr. Janikiewicz acknowledged the irony of his daughter's actions in light of his professional work, expressing personal embarrassment but emphasizing that the incident only reinforced his commitment to promoting safe behaviour. The event occurred in May 2013 after Stefanie had been drinking during a train journey from London to Manchester, followed by more alcohol at a meal with her sister before attempting to drive to Liverpool. Instead, she drove 55 miles in the wrong direction towards Blackpool.

Stefanie was stopped after nearly 40 minutes driving at a walking pace along the M55's hard shoulder. At Preston Crown Court, she pleaded guilty to dangerous and drunk driving. Judge Anthony Russell QC handed her a six-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, citing her previously impeccable character and impact as a popular teacher. She was banned from driving for two years and ordered to pay £350 in costs.

Carole Whittingham of the Campaign Against Drink Driving (CADDD) questioned the message sent to young people by such lenient sentencing. Dr. Janikiewicz stated that, while painful for the family, the experience strengthened his resolve to advocate for responsible alcohol use. Stefanie Janikiewicz expressed deep remorse for her actions, admitting memory loss due to excessive drinking.

article_content: Mars hosts dust devils that can grow even bigger than tornadoes on Earth, with massive funnels over 330 feet (100 meters) wide stretching nearly 12 miles (19 kilometers) high. On Earth, dust devils start when sunlight heats the ground, creating a pocket of warm air that rises through the cooler air above. But scientists have found that on Mars, not only are these dust devils larger—they also need much stronger upward winds, or updrafts, to form because the Martian atmosphere is so thin. Research led by Bryce Williams at the University of Alabama in Huntsville reveals that you need almost double the amount of convective updraft to spin up a Martian dust devil than you would on Earth. The team studied the interplay between turbulence at the planet’s surface and the rising air needed to trigger these vortices, noting that friction and surface winds on Mars make the process much more challenging. To better understand this, the researchers combined findings from Australian dust devil studies with meteorological data from NASA’s Viking Lander. Now, their focus is on how these Martian whirlwinds lift dust into the air, a process that influences both the planet’s weather and future missions to Mars. Professor Udaysankar Nair notes that Mars’ thin air means dust has a greater impact on temperature exchanges in the atmosphere and on the surface. While Martian dust cools the surface during the day, it actually helps keep things warmer at night by emitting infrared radiation back to the ground. In another development, NASA’s Curiosity rover detected sudden spikes in methane levels—a potential clue of life beneath the surface, since similar bursts on Earth often have biological origins. Though chemical reactions between rocks and water could also generate methane, this unique, localized spike at Gale Crater fuels ongoing speculation. There’s already concrete evidence that Mars had liquid water in the past, and now, with these new methane readings, scientists feel they’re closer to answering the ultimate question: does life exist on Mars? While it’s common to spot trails left by dust devils, catching them in action is rare. Recently, NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, using the HiRISE camera, photographed three dust devils whirling across the surface. And while often seen as a nuisance, these swirling winds can sometimes help out—for instance, by cleaning dust off the solar panels of rovers like Opportunity.

வேறு ஹோர்ஜிகல் விளக்கங்களும் இருந்தாலும், இந்த உள்ளூர் மெத்தேன் வெடிப்பு விஞ்ஞானிகளைக் கவனிக்க வைத்துள்ளது. மார்சில் நீர் இருந்தது உறுதிப்படுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது; இப்போது இந்த மெத்தேன் கண்டுபிடிப்புகள், மார்சில் உயிர் இருக்கிறதா என்பதை தெரிந்து கொள்ளும் முயற்சியில் விஞ்ஞானிகள் புதிய நம்பிக்கையுடன் இருக்கின்றனர். தூசித் திரவுகளால் உருவான பாதைகள் மார்சில் அடிக்கடி காணப்பட்டாலும், அவற்றை நேரடியாக படம் பிடிப்பது அரிது. சமீபத்தில், நாசா மார்ஸ் ரீகானிசன்ஸ் ஆர்பிட்டரில் உள்ள ஹைரிஸ் கேமரா மூலமாக மூன்று தூசித் திரவுகள் நகரும் நிலையில் காட்சிப்படுத்தப்பட்டது. இவை சுருள்வாக இருந்தாலும், போது போது ரோவர்களின் சோலார் பானல்களை தூசி கழுவி அதை நல்ல நிலையில் வைத்திருப்பதிலும் உதவும்.

article_content: Reverend Bev Mason, the vicar of Bingley All Saints Parish Church, photographed a council van parked illegally on double yellow lines outside her church, just weeks after she received a ticket for the same offence. Wardens were patrolling during Sunday service and issuing tickets to churchgoers at the time. Reverend Mason reported the incident to the council, which has since reprimanded the wardens involved and reminded all staff to follow parking regulations. Mason described the wardens as 'merciless' and said her congregation feels targeted, noting that someone receives a ticket nearly every Sunday. She said that church members are dedicated community members and feel unfairly penalized. Parking near the church is limited to two hours, so those who arrive early or stay late—especially those helping after the service—can get fined, even if they overstay by just a few minutes. Mason added that the parking restrictions are negatively affecting church activities and are particularly unfair for worshippers who rely on Sundays for fellowship. On the day of the incident, All Saints was holding a 'Holy Hilarity' service, and many found humor in the situation. Shipley MP Philip Davies expressed concern about churchgoers being targeted and said he would raise the issue with Bradford Council. A council spokesperson called the wardens' conduct unacceptable and confirmed all staff have been told to adhere to parking rules. The council will investigate the matter further and may consider adjusting local parking restrictions, in discussion with Reverend Mason.

article_content: Lindsey Scrimshire, 52, a mother of two from Leicester and a breast cancer survivor, has been told she has only weeks to live after doctors missed four brain tumours, despite her repeated requests for a scan. After completing treatment for breast cancer in 2011—including a lumpectomy, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy—Mrs Scrimshire began experiencing severe headaches and shoulder pain. She repeatedly requested a brain scan from staff at Leicester Royal Infirmary but was told it was unnecessary. She also saw her GP, who diagnosed her with arthritis and prescribed painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs. In February of the following year, during a routine check-up at Glenfield Hospital, Mrs Scrimshire reported her symptoms again but was reassured a scan was not needed. She later underwent surgery for a bowel blockage, but her scan requests were still declined. In April 2013, when the pain became unbearable, she visited the accident and emergency department at Leicester Royal Infirmary. There, a scan revealed four large tumours in her brain, and further scans showed the cancer had also spread to her lungs and liver. Doctors informed her that only palliative care was possible. Her husband, Mark, 47, said that if Lindsey had been scanned earlier, there might have been a better chance to fight the cancer. Mrs Scrimshire expressed regret that her repeated requests for scans were not acted upon. Consultant oncologist Claire Esler stated the hospital was sorry a scan was not given at the follow-up appointment, noting that her symptoms were not thought to be related to her previous breast cancer at that time. Esler emphasized that Mrs Scrimshire's initial breast cancer treatment adhered to national guidelines, which do not include routine scans after treatment. The hospital has met with the family to discuss options and remains open to further discussions. Mr Scrimshire is consulting a solicitor and considering legal action.

Lord Hill of Oareford has been nominated as Britain's next EU commissioner by Prime Minister David Cameron. However, the appointment has sparked controversy, with Lord Hill being required to sell his shares in major lobbying company Huntsworth following concerns in Brussels about a potential conflict of interest. Downing Street stated that Lord Hill would dispose of his significant shareholding to help ensure a smooth confirmation process in the European Parliament.

Labour criticized the appointment, calling the process 'botched.' Shadow Europe Minister Gareth Thomas described the situation as a 'shambles,' noting that Cameron's approach to Europe was deteriorating, especially after failing to prevent Jean-Claude Juncker's appointment as Commission President. Thomas argued that Lord Hill should face confirmation hearings both in Westminster and in the European Parliament.

Lord Hill's career has largely involved roles in both lobbying and politics, including working for PR firms representing major international interests such as banks, businesses, and governments, including the UAE, Tesco, and A4e. Philippe Lamberts, leader of the Green group of MEPs, voiced concerns about Hill's lobbying background and connections to Huntsworth, a company owned by Lord Chadlington, an associate of Cameron. He likened Hill's appointment to 'letting the wolves into the sheepfold,' suggesting the European Parliament could block the nomination. Other senior EU figures have reportedly raised similar concerns with Europe Minister David Lidington since the announcement of the £210,000-a-year appointment.

While Downing Street insists there is no conflict of interest, they state that Lord Hill's decision to sell his shares is to avoid any perceived issues. Lamberts emphasized the importance of examining possible conflicts arising from Hill's background and warned that former lobbyists should expect rigorous scrutiny. Martin Schulz, President of the European Parliament and ally of Juncker, questioned whether Hill's reported Eurosceptic views would prevent his confirmation. Although the Parliament cannot block individuals outright, it can collectively reject the Commission if it deems certain nominees unsuitable.

This week, Cameron is set to meet Juncker for the first time since his unsuccessful attempt to stop Juncker becoming Commission President. Despite criticisms, Cameron continues to seek a key economic role for Lord Hill—such as responsibilities for trade, competition, or the single market—although some experts warn that opting for a lower-profile candidate may reduce Britain's influence compared to other countries nominating senior ministers. Mats Persson from think tank Open Europe described Cameron's approach as a gamble.

Meanwhile, Defence Minister Michael Fallon voiced support for Lord Hill, calling him an effective political operator and noted that the recent Cabinet reshuffle has made the UK government more Eurosceptic, in line with public sentiment.

லார்டு ஹிலின் வாழ்க்கை பெரும்பாலும் லாபி மற்றும் அரசியல் துறைகளில் இருந்துள்ளது. அவர் பணிபுரிந்த பி.ஆர் நிறுவங்கள் யுக்கள், வங்கிகள், அரசுகள், டெஸ்கோ, A4e, ஐக்கிய அரபு அமீரகம் போன்றவற்றிற்காக பணியாற்றியது குறிப்பிடத்தக்கது. கிரீன் குழும தலைவர் பிலிப் லாம்பெர்ட்ஸ், ஹன்ட்ஸ்வொர்த் மற்றும் லார்டு சாட்லிங்டன் உடன் உள்ள தொடர்புகளால் லார்டு ஹிலின் நியமனம் குறித்து கவலை தெரிவித்தார். மேலும், வெளியீட்டின் அடுத்த 24 மணி நேரங்களில் மூத்த யூரோப்பிய அதிகாரிகள், ஐரோப்பிய அமைச்சர் டேவிட் லிடிங்டனிடம் இந்த வகை கருத்தை பகிர்ந்துள்ளனர்.

டவுனிங் ஸ்ட்ரீட் எந்த முரண்பாடும் இல்லை என்று உறுதி அளித்தாலும், சந்தேகங்களை தவிர்க்க லார்டு ஹில் தனது பங்குகளை விற்பதாக தெரிவித்தனர். லாம்பெர்ட்ஸ், லாபியிங் பின்னணி கொண்டவர்களுக்கு அதிகமான கேள்விகள் வருமெனக் கருதி சோதனை செய்ய வேண்டியதாகக் கூறினார். ஐரோப்பிய பாராளுமன்றத் தலைவர் மார்டின் ஷுல்ஸ், லார்டு ஹிலின் யூரோஸ்கெப்டிக் (ஐ.யு. எதிர்ப்பு) பார்வைகள் அவரது பதவிக்கு தடையாக இருகினும் என சந்தேகம் தெரிவித்தார். பாராளுமன்றம் தனிப்பட்ட நியமனங்களைக் கண்காணிக்க இயலாவிட்டாலும், கமிஷனரை முழுமையாக நிராகரிக்க முடியும்.

இந்த வாரம், கேமரூன் ஜங்கருடன் சந்தித்து, லார்டு ஹிலுக்கு வர்த்தகம், போட்டித் திறன், அல்லது சிங்கிள் மார்க்கெட் போன்ற முக்கிய பொருளாதாரப் பொறுப்புகளைப் பெற முனைந்துள்ளார். சில நிபுணர்கள், குறைந்த அளவில் தெரிவு செய்யப்பட்ட வேட்பாளர்கள் பிரிட்டனின் தாக்கத்தை குறைக்கும் என எச்சரிக்கின்றனர். ஓபன் யூரோப் திங்க் டாங்கின் மேட்ஸ் பெர்சனும் இதை ஒரு 'சூதாடு' முயற்சி என்றும் கூறினார்.

பாதுகாப்பு அமைச்சர் மைக்கேல் ஃபாலன், லார்டு ஹிலுக்கு முழு ஆறுதல் தெரிவித்தார்; அவர் திறமையான அரசியல் நிபுணர் என்றும், அமைச்சரவையின் மாற்றம் பொதுமக்கள் இச்சைக்கு ஏற்ப ஐரோப்பாவுக்குத் தூரப்படும் பார்வைக்குத் தூண்டுவதாகவும் கூறினார்.
