article_content: NASA has provided a new update on its ambitious SPHEREx mission, which aims to map the entire sky from low-Earth orbit when it launches in the next couple of years. SPHEREx, short for Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer, is currently being assembled in a clean room at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California. The spacecraft’s distinctive cone shape is already visible, with two smaller cones nestled inside the main structure. These cones surround and shield SPHEREx’s telescope from the light and heat of the Sun and Earth during orbit. Sara Susca, deputy payload manager and payload systems engineer for the mission at JPL, explained in Thursday’s update: “SPHEREx has to be quite agile because the spacecraft must move relatively quickly as it scans the sky. While it may not look that way, the shields are actually very light and made from layered materials, almost like a sandwich. The exterior uses aluminum sheets, and the interior features an aluminum honeycomb structure, similar in appearance to cardboard—light but strong.” The spacecraft’s main telescope, built by Ball Aerospace in Boulder, Colorado, will collect infrared light from distant sources using three mirrors and six detectors. Over two years, SPHEREx will map the entire sky four times, creating a large database of galaxies, stars, nebulae, and other celestial objects. The mission’s goals are to help scientists better understand where water and other key ingredients for life originated, by measuring the abundance of water ice in interstellar clouds of gas and dust—regions where new stars and planets are formed. The SPHEREx team will also study the history of galaxies, gaining insight into their formation and evolution. Additionally, scientists will use SPHEREx’s map of millions of galaxies to learn more about the rapid expansion of the universe that occurred shortly after the Big Bang. NASA approved the SPHEREx mission in 2019. The spacecraft will launch aboard a SpaceX rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California, with a target date no later than April 2025.

SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer) தற்போது தென் கலிஃபோர்னியாவில் உள்ள NASA-ன் Jet Propulsion Laboratory-ல் கட்டுப்படும் நிலையில் உள்ளது. விண்கலம் தனித்துவமான கோன் வடிவம் கொண்டது, அதில் இரண்டு சிறிய கோன்கள் உள்ளே உள்ளது. இவை SPHEREx தொலைநோக்கியை சூரிய மற்றும் பூமி ஒளி, வெப்பத்திலிருந்து பாதுகாக்கும். JPL-இன் துணை பெலோட் மேலாளர் மற்றும் பெலோட் சிஸ்டம் இன்ஜினியர் சாரா சசூகா தெரிவித்திருப்பதாவது: “SPHEREx ஆகாயத்தை விரைவாக ஸ்கேன் செய்ய வேண்டிய காரணத்தால் திறம்பட நகர வேண்டும். வெளிப்படையாகத் தெரியவில்லை எனினும், இந்த பாதுகாப்பு தாள்கள் பல அடுக்குகளாக, வெளியே அலுமினியம், உள்ளே அலுமினியம் மெட்டிரிக்ஸ் அடுக்கு போன்றது—மிக हलொமாகவும் வலுவாகவும் உள்ளது” என்றார். இந்த விண்கலத்தின் முக்கிய தொலைநோக்கி, கொலராடோவின் போல்டரில் உள்ள Ball Aerospace நிறுவனம் கட்டியுள்ளது. இது மூன்று கண்ணாடிகள் மற்றும் ஆறு கண்டுபிடிப்புகளைக் கொண்டு தொலைவேதி இன்ஃப்ரார் ஒளியை திரட்டும். இரண்டு ஆண்டுகளில், SPHEREx விண்கலம் முழு ஆகாயத்தையும் நான்கு முறை வரைபடம் வளைக்கும், பல்லாயிரம் விண்மீன்களை, பூதகக்கூடங்கள், மற்ற வான்பொருட்கள் தொடர்பான பெரிய தரவுத்தளத்தை உருவாக்கும். இந்த திட்டத்தின் முக்கிய நோக்கங்கள்: உயிர்வாழ்வுக்கு தேவையான நீர் உள்ளிட்ட முக்கிய மூலப்பொருள்கள் எங்கே தோன்றின என்பதை அதிகம் அறிந்து கொள்ளுகிறது; அதேசமயம், விண்வெளி வாயுக்கடல்கள் மற்றும் தூசி குழுமங்களில் இருக்கும் நீர் ஐஸை அளவிடுவதிலும், புதிய நட்சத்திரங்கள், கிரகங்கள் உருவாகும் இடங்களை ஆராய்வதும் படுகிறது. SPHEREx குழு இந்த வானியல் வரலாற்றை இரண்டாம் பாகமாகவும், விண்வெளி விரைவான விரிவின் வரலாற்றையும் (Big Bang பிறகு) பயில உள்ளது. NASA 2019இல் SPHEREx திட்டத்திற்கு ஒப்புதல் வழங்கியது. விண்கலம் SpaceX மூலம் வாண்டன்பெர்க் ஸ்பேஸ் ஃபோர்ஸ் பேஸில் இருந்து ஏப்ரல் 2025க்குள் ஏவ திட்டமிடப்பட்டுள்ளது.

A recent government memo revealed that law enforcement has identified 270 illegal cannabis growing operations in Maine, drawing attention from the state’s congressional delegation. The lawmakers sent a letter to Attorney General Merrick Garland in August, requesting details on the Department of Justice’s actions to combat foreign-owned illegal cannabis cultivation.

The issue of illegal, foreign-backed cannabis farms is not limited to Maine; it has sparked legislative responses across the nation. According to a March report from Politico, Chinese investors, owners, and workers have increasingly been involved in illegal marijuana production in several states, including Oklahoma, California, and Oregon. These farms, supported by funds traceable to Chinese sources, have become prominent in recent years.

Compounding concerns about foreign involvement, the U.S. Department of Justice charged Chinese owners of a property in Reedley, California, with running an illegal biolab in October. In November, a U.S. House committee released a report detailing troubling findings about the site, believed to be linked to the People’s Republic of China.

In response to security concerns, all 50 U.S. states have introduced legislation over the past year restricting foreign investment, with 37 states enacting such laws. Florida is among them. In May, Governor Ron DeSantis signed a law restricting government contracts, economic incentives, and real estate ownership for certain foreign individuals and entities associated with countries of concern, including China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Venezuela, and Syria.

Florida officials are currently developing the regulatory framework to implement this law. Investors and economic stakeholders are calling for clarification to ensure that in-state investment by funds with a minor share from passive foreign investors is not barred. Without such clarity, there could be negative consequences for Florida’s rapidly growing economy. The state’s expanding population is driving demand for new housing construction, and limiting investment could hinder development and raise housing costs.

Brewster Bevis, president of Associated Industries of Florida, highlighted concerns that strict interpretation of the law could impact real estate investment, even when passive foreign investors have minimal stakes and no control over fund operations. Florida regulators appear to be proceeding carefully, planning a Department of Agriculture workshop on November 21 to review proposed regulations clarifying the law’s application to passive foreign investments.

As Florida has built a reputation for pro-growth policies like low taxes and regulatory flexibility, stakeholders stress the importance of regulatory clarity to avoid unintended economic setbacks and maintain the state’s positive example.

வெளிநாட்டு பங்கு குறித்த கவலை தொடர, கடந்த அக்டோபரில், காளிஃபோர்னியாவின் ரீட்லியில் உள்ள ஒரு சொத்துக்கு சொந்தமான சீன உரிமையாளர்கள் மீது சட்டவிரோத உயிரணுக்கூடம் இயக்கியதாக U.S. Department of Justice வழக்கு தொடர்ந்தது. நவம்பரில், அமெரிக்கக் காங்கிரஸில் ஒரு குழு, அந்த உயிரணுக்கூடம் சீன அரசுடன் தொடர்புடையது என விவரிக்கின்ற அறிக்கையை வெளியிட்டது.

தேசிய பாதுகாப்பு காரணமாக, கடந்த வருடம் அனைத்து 50 மாநிலங்களிலும் வெளிநாட்டு முதலீட்டுக்கு கடுமையான கட்டுப்பாடுகள் கொண்ட சட்டங்கள் முன்பற்றப்பட்டது; இதில் 37 மாநிலங்களில் அவை அமல்படுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளன. ஃபுளோரிடாவும் அதில் ஒன்று. மே மாதத்தில், ஆளுநர் ரான் டிசாண்டிஸ் சீனா, ரஷ்யா, ஈரான், வட கொரியா, கியூபா, வெனிசுலா, மற்றும் சிரியா போன்ற நாடுகளின் வெளிநாட்டு நபர்கள் மற்றும் நிறுவனங்களுக்கு அரச ஒப்பந்தங்கள் மற்றும் நிலச் சொத்து வாங்குவதைத் தடைசெய்யும் சட்டத்தில் கையெழுத்திட்டார்.

இந்த சட்டத்தை நடைமுறைப்படுத்துவதற்காக, ஃபுளோரிடா அரசு விதிகளை தயாரித்து வருகிறது. முதலீட்டாளர்கள் மற்றும் பங்காளிகள், பாசிவ் (சிலவு பங்கு கொண்ட, தொழிலில் நேரடி கண்ட்ரோல் இல்லாத) வெளிநாட்டு முதலீடுகள் தடை செய்யப்படக்கூடாது என்பதை தெளிவுபடுத்த வேண்டும் என வலியுறுத்துகின்றனர். இந்த விளக்கம் இல்லையெனில், ஃபுளோரிடாவின் வேகமாக வளரும் பொருளாதாரத்திற்கு பாதிப்பு ஏற்படலாம். மாநில மக்கள் தொகை விரைவாக அதிகரிக்க, வீட்டு வசதிக்கான முதலீடுகள் பாதிக்கப்படலாம்; வீட்டு விலையும் உயரலாம்.

Associated Industries of Florida தலைவர் ப்ரூஸ்டர் பிவிஸ், பாசிவ் முதலீட்டாளர்கள் நிதி வைத்திருப்பதால் மட்டும் முதலீட்டை தடை செய்வது பொருத்தமன்று என்றும், அவர்கள் நிறுவனங்களை கட்டுப்படுத்த இயலாது என்றும் கூறுகிறார். அதிகாரிகள் இப்போன்று தவறுகளை தவிர கவனமாக நடவடிக்கைகள் எடுத்து வருகிறார்கள். நவம்பர் 21-ல் விவசாயத்துறை ஒரு பணிக்கூட்டம் நடத்தி, பாசிவ் வெளிநாட்டு முதலீடுகளுக்கான விளக்க விதிகளை விவாதிக்க உள்ளது.

குறைந்த வரிகள், விரிவான கல்வித் தேர்வுகள் மற்றும் குறைந்த விதிமுறைகள் போன்ற வளர்ச்சி ஊக்கமும் கொண்ட ஃபுளோரி்டா, புதிய சட்டங்களுக்கு தெளிவான விதிமுறைகளை வழங்காமல், எதிர்பாராத பொருளாதார பாதிப்பை ஏற்படுத்தக் கூடாது என்று பங்காளிகள் வலியுறுத்துகின்றனர்.

article_content: Janay Jackson, a 17-year-old from Englewood, Florida, died from injuries sustained when a van crashed into her bedroom as she slept. The incident took place at 2:40 am on Tuesday at her home at 5501 Kennerly Road. A grey Ford minivan, driven by an unidentified man, ran through a T-junction and hit her bedroom wall. Janay was taken to Shands Jacksonville Hospital, but the driver suffered only minor injuries. Detective Robert Peck of the Jacksonville Sheriff's Department stated that the driver's identity is not yet disclosed and the cause of the crash remains under investigation, though investigators suspect alcohol may have been a factor, according to First Coast News. Janay lived with her parents and attended Samuel W. Wolfson High School, where she was a senior and a straight-A student. Her father, Gerald Jackson, had built a cinder block barrier in front of her bedroom due to previous incidents with vehicles, but it was not enough to prevent this tragedy. Gerald Jackson spoke about trying to protect his daughter from danger and expressed deep grief over her loss, while lamenting that the driver sustained only minor injuries. Family, teachers, and friends remembered Janay as bright, compassionate, and ambitious. Her teachers, Sheri Porubski and Elisabeth Sundrstom, described her as kind and smart, with a dream of becoming a nurse. Friends also shared memories of her helpfulness and cheerful nature. Neighbor Trish Hunt and Mr. Jackson said the intersection had long been known as hazardous, and that safety complaints had been submitted to the city. However, city spokesperson Debbie Delgado stated that the intersection meets standard specifications. District Councilman Don Redman said he was unaware of previous safety complaints but promised to look into potential improvements. Shannon Hartley, Public Information Officer for the Jacksonville Sheriff’s Department, said they are waiting for more information about the driver and the cause of the accident.

The haka, well-known for its energy on New Zealand rugby fields, is also deeply significant in the country’s military culture. In a moving video, soldiers from the 2/1 Battalion of the Royal New Zealand Infantry Regiment (RNZIR) come together on the parade ground to perform their unit haka in honor of their fallen comrades. This emotional event marks their farewell as they pass through the waharoa, the traditionally carved entrance. 

As the family of a deceased soldier follows the hearse onto the grounds, the battalion steps forward to pay their respects, opening a powerful Māori ritual. The soldiers’ coordinated movements and strong voices powerfully express respect and remembrance. 

Filmed in 2012 but recently shared, the video highlights how haka remains key in New Zealand’s armed forces. Haka is more than a dance; it’s a cultural ritual performed by Māori and others across the nation to collectively express emotion. Each military unit has its own haka, with performances sometimes involving weapons or following set patterns, and sometimes being more free-form.

In moments like this, the haka’s meaning—whether pride, sorrow, encouragement, or tribute—is clear, making it a profound way for soldiers to honor their departed comrades.

article_content: SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — Puerto Rico police conducted their largest crime crackdown in recent years on Tuesday, arresting at least 380 people. Police Commissioner Antonio López said the operation targeted 12 gangs involved in drug and weapon sales, following tips from residents troubled by community violence. Traditionally, grouse has been a dish enjoyed by those willing to hunt for their supper or seek out specialty restaurants. Now, Marks & Spencer (M&S) has become the first major retailer to offer whole wild red grouse to the public, with the oven-ready birds priced at £10. Company executives anticipate strong sales as the bird arrives in stores. The birds are shot on the moors of Yorkshire and Northumberland and transported promptly to the shops.

The launch coincides with the start of the grouse shooting season, known as the Glorious Twelfth (August 12), a tradition upheld by members of the royal family, including the Queen, who regularly attends shoots at her Balmoral estate in Scotland, as well as younger royals.

Grouse shooting is central to an industry considered vital to the rural economy. Grouse is prized for its distinctive, rich flavor and is lean and virtually fat-free, offering a healthier alternative to other meats. According to the Moorland Association, the grouse industry in England is valued at £67 million and supports around 1,500 jobs.

The sector, however, is not without controversy. The League Against Cruel Sports criticizes the practice, citing concerns about the welfare of birds that may be injured rather than killed outright.

M&S hopes to tap into increasing consumer interest in traditional, naturally reared foods and is positioning grouse as part of a broader selection of British game meats. Rabbit, wood pigeon, venison, pheasant, and partridge will also be available from October, when they are in season.

For now, grouse will be sold only at M&S’s flagship London stores in Kensington High Street and Marble Arch, but if demand is high, availability may expand to other locations. Tom Harvey from M&S said, 'Our customers are telling us they are keen to try more game as an alternative to traditional everyday meats.'

article_content: Bill Gates recently voiced serious doubts about the effectiveness of mass tree planting to address climate change. Speaking at a New York Times climate discussion, he stated he avoids using large-scale planting to offset his carbon emissions, calling it 'complete nonsense' to suggest tree planting alone could solve the climate crisis. His remarks drew criticism from supporters of reforestation and afforestation, who worry his comments could hinder progress in these areas. Jad Daley, president of American Forests, rebuffed Gates’ claims on social media, noting his long-standing commitment to making forests part of climate action. Daley warned that such strong criticism could be a setback for reforestation efforts, especially those aimed at restoring forests after natural disasters like wildfires. While mass tree planting enjoys wide public and political support—including from U.S. lawmakers proposing global planting initiatives—several scientists share Gates’ skepticism about poorly planned projects. They caution that replacing diverse natural ecosystems with single-species plantations can hurt biodiversity and make environments more vulnerable to disease. Studies cite places like southern Mexico and Ghana as examples of negative consequences from such changes. Researchers also point out that commercial planting often uses just a few species valued for rapid growth or timber, posing risks to native ecosystems. Additional challenges include limited available land, conflicts with agriculture, and planting in unsuitable sites. Nevertheless, Daley asserts that carefully designed projects—especially those using native, resilient species in ecologically appropriate areas—are key components of a broader climate strategy. He maintains that no credible expert believes tree planting alone can solve climate issues, but that it plays an important supporting role. Institutions like Britain’s Royal Botanic Gardens have developed guidelines recommending that priority be given to preserving existing forests, avoiding the conversion of grasslands or wetlands, and restoring ecological diversity. There is broad agreement on one vital principle: protecting the forests we already have is essential and should come before planting new ones.

Singer-songwriter Ani DiFranco will make her Broadway debut as 'Persephone' in the acclaimed musical Hadestown, portraying the role she first performed on the 2010 studio-concept album by composer Anaïs Mitchell. DiFranco’s performances will begin at the Walter Kerr Theatre on February 9, 2024, according to producers Mara Isaacs, Dale Franzen, Hunter Arnold, and Tom Kirdahy. DiFranco's history with Hadestown began when she invited Mitchell to issue the original studio album on her label, Righteous Babe Records. Producers noted that DiFranco's interpretation left a lasting impression on the character as the show evolved over the years.

Expressing her excitement, DiFranco said, “I could not be more thrilled to be joining the cast of Hadestown. It’s like I get to rewind to my New York youth and follow the road not taken.” Mitchell commented, “I can’t really overstate the influence of Ani’s music and example on me as a young songwriter. Poetic, bold, radically emotive, and fun, she simply has been a mythic figure in my life, and I can’t think of anything more beautifully full circle than Ani playing 'Persephone' on Broadway. Grateful and awestruck.”

DiFranco is regarded as a pioneer of the DIY movement in music, having founded her own label in 1990. Mostly known for her folk music, she also incorporates punk, funk, hip hop, jazz, soul, and electronica. Her recent work includes the 2021 album Revolutionary Love and the 25th Anniversary Edition reissue of Little Plastic Castle, both released on Righteous Babe Records. Her memoir, No Walls and the Recurring Dream, was published in May 2019 by Viking Books.

Hadestown, which opened on Broadway in 2019 and won eight Tony Awards including Best Musical, currently stars Betty Who as Persephone (through February 4), Jordan Fisher as Orpheus, Lillias White as Hermes, Phillip Boykin as Hades, and Solea Pfeiffer as Eurydice.

The United Nations' senior official in Libya has called for the establishment of a unified system to oversee the reconstruction of Derna, a city on the Mediterranean coast that suffered devastating floods last month. Abdoulaye Bathily, the UN Special Envoy, stressed the pressing need for this cohesive approach, as different Libyan authorities are currently pursuing competing reconstruction initiatives for Derna and other flooded regions.

The catastrophic flooding, triggered by Storm Daniel, resulted in the collapse of two dams near Derna on September 11. The deluge destroyed large parts of the city, with the UN estimating that up to one-third of Derna’s homes and infrastructure were damaged. Officials and humanitarian groups estimate the number of deaths between 4,000 and 11,000, with many people still missing, possibly buried under rubble or swept into the Mediterranean Sea.

Political divisions persist in Libya, with rival governments in the east and west both asserting the right to lead the reconstruction of Derna. Bathily has urged both sides, along with international partners, to establish a joint national authority to manage rebuilding in a transparent and accountable way.

Calls for impartial international investigation have intensified, reflecting public distrust in Libyan leadership as it emerges that the dams were left without maintenance for decades despite repeated warnings. Bathily’s call for unity in reconstruction was promptly backed by the US, UK, France, Germany, and Italy, who released a joint statement supporting an open and unified response to the disaster.

Libya’s divide has persisted since the NATO-backed uprising in 2011 that ousted Muammar Gadhafi. Rival factions remain entrenched, with the east and south under General Khalifa Hifter and his Libyan National Army, allied to one administration, while a separate government operates from Tripoli with significant international support.

A recent cost-benefit analysis is reshaping how city authorities address non-household plastic waste, such as PET trays and LDPE wrapping films often found in packaging and industrial use. This waste comes from businesses, restaurants, factories, and institutions, rather than homes.

Research teams from the Universities of Surrey, Portsmouth, and Ghent showed that recycling these plastics can be economically feasible when at least 10,500 metric tons are processed annually—a quantity typical for a medium-sized city like Ghent and its surrounding municipalities.

This insight could drive major improvements in plastic recycling systems across Europe, especially where commercial and industrial waste is concerned. As the world’s second-largest plastic producer, Europe could benefit greatly from these findings to hit recycling targets and lower its carbon footprint.

Detailed in ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering, the research found that the annual cost to collect and recycle this waste ranges from €635 to €1,445 per processed metric ton, depending on collection frequency and the recycling plant’s design. Significantly, recycling can decrease greenhouse gas emissions by 49–79% compared to conventional disposal.

Dr. Regina Frei, Associate Professor at the University of Surrey, highlighted that focused collection and recycling of business plastic wastes present overlooked economic opportunities. Her colleague, Irdanto Saputra Lase, emphasized that their cost-benefit analysis shows sustainable methods are also financially attractive.

Supported by the City of Ghent and 12 local municipalities, the study explored different collection intervals and two recycling plant models (basic and advanced). The team concluded that scaling up collection, robust waste management policies, and practical incentives for waste separation are crucial steps for developing a circular economy.

article_content: Bitcoin is rising for the fourth consecutive week, with its price just below an 18-month high of $38,000, as more investors anticipate that US exchange-traded funds (ETFs) holding the cryptocurrency are close to receiving regulatory approval. "We call the current Bitcoin rallies 'nothing for sale' internally," said Stephane Ouellette, co-founder and CEO of FRNT Financial. "Even on minor positive news, whether ETF-related or not, Bitcoin faces little resistance and tends to gap up in price. This highlights the solid price base Bitcoin has built since the FTX collapse." On Friday, Bitcoin climbed as much as 2.5% to $37,465. A day earlier, it came within reach of $38,000, its highest since May 2022. That month, the TerraUSD stablecoin collapse triggered failures across the crypto sector, culminating in FTX's implosion one year ago. Bloomberg Intelligence analysts believe the US Securities and Exchange Commission may approve a spot Bitcoin ETF by January 10. Over the past four weeks, Bitcoin has surged nearly 40% amid growing expectations of imminent approval. Other cryptocurrencies are also posting strong gains: Terra jumped 66% today, and FTX’s token FTT surged 79.8%, according to CoinGecko. The changing economic outlook is benefiting cryptocurrencies. With stock markets up and bond yields down, investors’ appetite for riskier assets like crypto is rising. Bitcoin still remains about halfway to its all-time high of nearly $69,000 seen during the 2021 bull run. Matt Hougan, chief investment officer at Bitwise Asset Management, said that while short-term predictions are challenging, Bitcoin's long-term prospects look promising. "Over the next year, it's hard not to be bullish on crypto and Bitcoin," Hougan said. "We can expect new all-time highs." In other business news: India's industrial growth slowed to 5.8% in September, down from a 14-month high of 10.3% the previous month, affected by an unfavorable base and heavy rainfall. Ranjan Pai, chairman of Manipal Education and Medical Group, invested Rs 1,400 crore (around $168 million) in Aakash Institute, a subsidiary of Byju’s. Manufacturing firms are seeing more 2024 graduates joining, bringing strong digital skills, said Dilip Pattanayak, chief HR officer at JSW Group.

article_content: On Thursday, internet connectivity across Syria dropped by more than 90%, according to watchdog group Renesys. While it remains uncertain who triggered the outage, such disruptions have occurred multiple times in the last two years, often attributed to the government. Syrian opposition activists rely on the internet to share updates and visuals about the ongoing civil war. US Ambassador to Syria Robert Ford confirmed previous internet cutoffs and stated that the US has supplied opposition groups with over a thousand units of non-lethal equipment, primarily communications tools, to help them bypass restrictions. Speaking in Washington, Ford stressed the importance of these tools, explaining that the government—receiving technical support from Iran—has long monitored internet activity to track and target dissenters. Ford expressed that American support for secure communications aims to ensure Syrians can inform the world about happenings within the country, referencing a desire to avoid information blackouts like the one during Hama’s 1982 massacre. He pointed out that much of the footage appearing on international news comes from this equipment. As unrest intensified, the route to Damascus International Airport was closed because of violence in nearby areas, prompting Egypt Air to suspend all flights to Syria due to security concerns, according to reports from al Ahram. Recent fierce clashes are viewed as a possible turning point in Syria’s nearly two-year civil war. In northern Syria, villagers collected debris from a fighter jet downed by rebels, who claimed to have shot down three government aircraft within 24 hours. The jet’s remains were gathered as a trophy to share with nearby communities. Witnesses described pilots ejecting—one was captured alive and taken for medical treatment, while the other remained missing on Wednesday night. Rebel-shot videos online showed the aftermath, though CNN could not independently verify the footage. In addition to the downed aircraft, rebels also claim to have seized a significant air force base after two months of fighting, uncovering hundreds of Soviet-era anti-aircraft missiles and heavy weaponry. However, about half of the missiles were unusable. Rebels released instructional videos on handling the operational arms. The base, guarded by troops from the Syrian army’s 46th Regiment, had faced consistent attacks and supply drops that often fell into rebel hands. Wednesday saw more heavy casualties, with opposition sources counting at least 160 deaths, including 15 from a shelling in Aleppo’s Al-Ansari district, among them five children and two women. A car bomb in Daraa targeted the local Baath party headquarters, killing three guards. Near Damascus, dual car bombs in Jaramana resulted in up to 77 deaths, according to opposition activists, with the Syrian Interior Ministry reporting much lower figures. Jaramana, characterized by a mix of Christians and Druze, has been a refuge for pro-government civilians. Separate blasts in nearby neighborhoods had unreported casualties, and officials blamed such attacks on groups they label terrorists. The opposition claims around 40,000 people have died since protests began in 2011, and more than 380,000 Syrians have sought refuge abroad. Due to restrictions on media in Syria, CNN could not independently verify many of these accounts. Amid the ongoing violence, Turkey has formally requested Patriot air-defense missiles from NATO to strengthen its southern border, citing growing security risks from the Syrian crisis. The request is under examination by NATO officials, with evaluation teams from Germany, the US, and the Netherlands assessing potential deployment options. Turkish leaders stress this is a defensive move, with no intention of engaging in war with Syria.

இருந்தாலும் சிஎன்என் சுயாதீனமாக அதை நிரூபிக்க முடியவில்லை. இதனுடன், கிளர்ச்சி படையினர் இரண்டு மாதப் போர்களுக்குப் பிறகு ஒரு முக்கிய விமானப்படைத் தளத்தை கைப்பற்றி, நூற்றுக்கணக்கான சோவியத் கால ஏவுகணைகள் மற்றும் ஆயுதங்களை கண்டுபிடித்ததாகவும், அதில் பாதி செயலிலக்காக இருந்தன என்றும் தெரியவந்துள்ளது. செயல்படும் ஆயுதங்களை பயன்படுத்துவது தொடர்பான வீடியோக்களும் வெளியிடப்பட்டன. இந்த தளம் அரசின் 46வது படை பாதுகாப்பில் இருந்தது. புதன்கிழமை, எதிர்ப்பு தரவுகளின்படி குறைந்தது 160 பேர் உயிரிழந்தனர். இதில் அலெப்போவின் அல்-அன்சாரி பகுதியில் 5 குழந்தைகள், 2 பெண்கள் உட்பட 15 பேர் இறந்தனர். தராவில் கார் வெடிப்பில் பாஅத் கட்சி தலைமை அலுவலக பாதுகாப்பாளர்கள் மூவர் மறைந்தனர். டமாஸ்கஸ் அருகே ஜரமானாவில் இரட்டைக் கார் வெடிப்பில் நாடாளுமன்ற உறுப்பினர்கள் மெட்டின் டதர்சிச் அறிக்கையின்படி 77 பேர் வரை உயிரிழந்தனர்; வெளியிடப்பட்ட அரசு தரவுகள் குறைவாக இருப்பதாகக் கூறப்படுகிறது. ஜரமானா பகுதியில் கிறிஸ்தவர்களும் டிரூஸும் (இஸ்லாமியச் சன்னாதிகள்) வாழ்கின்றனர். பிற அயல்பகுதிகளில் உயிரிழப்புகள் குறித்து தெரிவிக்கப்படவில்லை. அரசு, இதுபோன்ற தாக்குதல்களுக்கு 'தீவிரவாதிகள்' என அழைக்கும் குழுக்களைப் போட்டுப் பின்வட்டுகிறது. 2011 ஆம் ஆண்டு போராட்டங்கள் துவங்கியதிலிருந்து சுமார் 40,000 பேர் உயிரிழந்துள்ளனர்; 3,80,000 பேர் அகதிகளாக வெளியேறியுள்ளனர் என எதிர்பார்க்கப்படுகிறது. சிரியாவில் செய்தியாளர்களுக்கு அனுமதியில்லாததால் பல தகவல்கள் சுயாதீனமாக சரிபார்க்க இயலவில்லை. இந்த விடயத்தில், துருக்கி நாட்டின் தெற்கு எல்லையை பாதுகாக்க நட்டோவிடம் பாதுகாப்பு கண்காணிப்பு குண்டுகளுக்கு (பேட்ரியட்) விண்ணப்பம் செய்துள்ளது. அமெரிக்கா, ஜெர்மனி மற்றும் நெதர்லாந்து ஆகிய நாடுகளின் குழுக்களும், இந்தப் பாதுகாப்பு முயற்சிக்காக நேரில் ஆய்வு செய்து வருகிறார்கள். துருக்கிய அரசு இதுவும் பாதுகாப்புக்காக மட்டும் என்றும், சிரியாவிற்கு எதிராக போர் செய்ய விரும்பவில்லை என்றும் வலியுறுத்தியுள்ளது.

article_content: This week, Bungie announced layoffs affecting over one hundred employees. Turning attention back to the game, Bungie is now focusing on 'The Final Shape,' their next expansion for Destiny 2. Both internally and publicly, Bungie has stated aspirations for this expansion to meet or exceed the quality of their most acclaimed releases. Bungie's post-layoff statement mentioned aiming for 'The Final Shape' to match expansions like The Taken King, Forsaken, and The Witch Queen, which are widely considered among the best in Destiny’s franchise. Many players see Forsaken as the standout expansion due to its significant improvements and substantial content. Internally, the company believes 'The Final Shape' must surpass even these expansions, even if that means accepting further delays. The expansion was already postponed by a year to accommodate Lightfall, and there are rumors of an additional four-month delay, though Bungie has yet to confirm this. Forsaken notably introduced a wide array of new content, especially compared to more recent expansions. For instance, Lightfall added one new zone, five exotic weapons, six exotic armor pieces, a single strike, no new PvP maps, and introduced one new enemy type (Tormentors). Although the full details of 'The Final Shape' remain uncertain, available information suggests it will include one new zone, one raid, likely no new PvP maps, an unspecified number of strikes (but not four), one new super for each class, new weapon sub-archetypes, and new mini-Tormentor enemies. Bungie has openly communicated that future expansions should not be expected to match Forsaken's scope. This has raised questions about whether the final expansion can truly surpass previous successes, especially regarding overall content volume. If 'The Final Shape' does not match Forsaken's scale, it might instead rely on the strength of its story and campaign moments to deliver its impact. Still, Forsaken was successful because it balanced both quality and quantity. Bungie has released a Vidoc (developer diary) with further details. While early impressions remain positive, surpassing Forsaken’s impact appears challenging. Ultimately, the community must wait to see how 'The Final Shape' measures up.

'தி பைனல் ஷேப்' எனும் அடுத்த டெஸ்டினி 2 விரிவாக்கத்தை பஞ்சி தற்போது அதிக கவனத்துடன் உருவாக்கி வருகிறது. நிறுவனத்தின் உள்புறமும் பொதுவுமான அறிக்கைகளிலும், இந்த விரிவாக்கம் முன்னைய மற்றப்பெரிய விரிவாக்கங்கள் போன்ற தரத்தில் அல்லது அதைவிட மேம்பட்டதாக இருக்க வேண்டும் என்று கூறப்பட்டுள்ளது. பஞ்சி லேய்ஆஃப் செய்த பின் வெளியிட்ட அறிக்கையில், 'தி பைனல் ஷேப்' The Taken King, Forsaken மற்றும் The Witch Queen போன்ற முதன்மை விரிவாக்கங்களைச் சமமாக்க வேண்டும் என்று குறிப்பிட்டது. பல டெஸ்டினி ரசிகர்கள் Forsaken-ஐ சிறந்த விரிவாக்கம் எனக் கருதுகிறார்கள், ஏனெனில் அது தரமும் புதிய உள்ளடக்கங்களும் அதிகம் வழங்கியது. உள்புறமாக, இந்த விரிவாக்கம் முன் வந்தவையை விட சிறந்ததாக இருத்தல் வேண்டும் என்று நிறுவனம் நம்புகிறது; அதற்காக கூடுதல் தாமதங்களை ஏற்க தயாராக இருக்கிறது. Lightfall-ஐ முன்னதாக வெளியிடுவதற்காக ஏற்கனவே ஒரு வருடம் தாமதப்படுத்தியது; மேலும் நான்கு மாதங்கள் தாமதப்படலாம் என்ற தகவல்கள் உள்ளன, ஆனால் பஞ்சி இதை உறுதிப்படுத்தவில்லை. Forsaken, சமீபத்திய விரிவாக்கங்களை விட அதிகமான புதிய உள்ளடக்கங்களை வழங்கியது. உதாரணமாக, Lightfall ஒரு புதிய மண்டலம், ஐந்து எக்ஸோடிக் ஆயுதங்கள், ஆறு எக்ஸோடிக் ஆர்மர்கள், ஒரு ஸ்ட்ரைக், புதிய PvP மேடைகள் இல்லை, மற்றும் ஒரு புதிய எதிரி வகை (டோர்மென்டர்ஸ்) போன்றவற்றை மட்டுமே சேர்த்தது. 'தி பைனல் ஷேப்' பற்றி முழுவதுமாக இன்னும் தகவல் கிடைக்கவில்லை என்றாலும், தற்போது கிடைக்கும் தகவலின்படி ஒரு புதிய மண்டலம், ஒரு ரெய்ட், புதிய PvP மேடைகள் இருக்க வாய்ப்பு இல்லை, ஸ்ட்ரைக் எண்ணிக்கை தெரியவில்லை (நிச்சயமாக நான்கு இல்லை), ஒவ்வொரு கிளாஸுக்கும் ஒரு புதிய சூப்பர், புதிய ஆயுத வகைகள் மற்றும் புதிய மினி-டோர்மென்டர் எதிரிகள் இடம்பெறலாம். Forsaken அளவிலான உள்ளடக்கம் இனி வராது என்று பஞ்சி தெரிவித்துள்ளது. இதனால், 'தி பைனல் ஷேப்' முந்திய வெற்றிகளுக்கு மேலாக இருக்க முடியுமா என்பது குறித்து சந்தேகங்கள் தோன்றி உள்ளன, குறிப்பாக உள்ளடக்க அளவில். Forsaken-ன் அளவை 'தி பைனல் ஷேப்' பெறவில்லை என்றால், அதன் கதை மற்றும் கேம்பெயின் தரத்திருத்தான் அதிகம் சார்ந்திருக்க வேண்டியிருக்கும். Forsaken வெற்றியின் காரணம், தரம் மற்றும் அதிக உள்ளடக்கம் இரண்டும் தான். மேலும் விவரங்களுக்கு பஞ்சி Vidoc (டெவலப்பர் வீடியோ) ஒன்றை வெளியிட்டுள்ளது. ஆரம்ப விமர்சனங்கள் நல்லவை என்றாலும், Forsaken அளவுக்கே அதிக தாக்கத்தை ஏற்படுத்துவது கடினம். இறுதியில், 'தி பைனல் ஷேப்' எவ்வாறு அமையும் என்பதை காத்திருக்க வேண்டும்.

article_content: The atmosphere in the stadium was electrifying as world record holder Jonnie Peacock signaled for silence from the passionate home crowd. Beside him, other top athletes prepared for what was billed as a grudge match: the London Paralympics 100m final, featuring runners who had previously clashed. Watching the event, I realized for the first time that I wasn't seeing a contest defined by disability, but an engaging sporting event that truly captivated me. This was the first of two key realizations I had that night. As a sports fan from Britain, I enjoyed hours of breathtaking competition during the London Olympics, but admit I had mixed feelings about the Paralympics beforehand. While I thought it was great for raising the profile of disabled sport and boosting the home country’s medal prospects, I questioned whether it would be a fair contest. A week of inspiring stories and intense athletic feats—across track and field, cycling, swimming, and lesser-known sports—quickly erased my doubts. Take blind football, for example. It's an impressive blend of traditional football and fast-paced movement. Players deftly dribble the ball, while defenders use the sound of a bell inside to follow the action—showcasing remarkable skill and awareness. At times, you'd believe the players weren't visually impaired. Wheelchair rugby, or 'Murderball,' is similarly intense—fast, physical, and thrilling. Wheelchair basketball also highlights athletes' agility and sharp precision. On Thursday night, Oscar Pistorius—the celebrated 'Blade Runner'—finished just outside the top three in the highly anticipated 100m sprint, overtaken by his South African teammate Arnu Fourie. Jonnie Peacock delighted the local crowd by winning gold, while American Richard Browne claimed silver. The race shook up the standings and gave me another moment of reflection. Why wasn't the U.S. higher in the medal rankings? Despite sending the third largest team, the United States was only sixth. While CNN extensively covered the Paralympics, broadcaster NBC only aired four hour-long highlight programs—drawing criticism from former Paralympian and U.S. team leader Aimee Mullins. She told The Guardian it was disappointing that the U.S., a leader in disability rights, provided so little coverage. This lack of exposure is unfortunate, as it denies many Americans the chance to celebrate their athletes’ achievements and may hinder future aspirations. U.S. athlete Tatyana McFadden—born with spina bifida, spending her early years in a Russian orphanage without a wheelchair before being adopted by Debbie McFadden—has overcome great adversity to win multiple medals. Swimmer Mallory Weggemann has also excelled, telling CNN about the dedication required to win gold. It would be unfortunate if athletes like McFadden and Weggemann were denied recognition on the world stage. The UK has created opportunities for disabled athletes since World War II, reflected in their strong medal tally, while some countries managed to send only a few competitors. I hope the enthusiasm from the London crowds encourages more nations to support disabled athletes, as the energy and excitement of the events are uplifting during difficult times. Though fair competition questions remain, more exposure and discussion can improve the organization of the Paralympics. The real challenge may be ensuring all nations provide sporting opportunities to disabled individuals and offering better media coverage at home. Personally, I look forward to the Rio Paralympics and hope many others will watch them too.

பாதுகாப்பாளர்கள் பந்தில் உள்ள மணி சத்தத்தைக் கேட்டு விளையாடுகிறார்கள்—இவர் திறமை மற்றும் மன எழுச்சி நம்பமுடியாத அளவு. சில நேரங்களில் அவர்கள் பார்ப்பதிலிருந்து விலகினவர்கள் என தெரியாமல் உள்ளது. வீல் சேர்ரக்பி, 'மரணபந்து' என அழைக்கப்படுகிறது, அதிவேகமாகவும் காயப்பாடும் அதிகமாகவும் உள்ளது. அதே போல் வீல் சேர்பாஸ்கெட் பந்து வீரர்களின் திறமையும் சுழற்ப்ரவாய்ச்சிப் போக்கும் தெளிவாக தெரிகிறது. வியாழன் இரவில், 'பிளேட் ரன்னர்' என்ற புகழ்பெற்ற ஒஸ்கார் பிஸ்டோரியஸ், 100 மீ ஸ்பிரிண்ட் போட்டியில் நான்காம் இடத்தில் முடிந்தார்; அவரது தென் ஆப்பிரிக்க அணித் தோழர் ஆர்னு ஃபூரி அவரை வென்றார். உள்ளூர் ரசிகர்களுக்கு மகிழ்ச்சியை வழங்கி ஜானி பீக்காக் தங்கம் வென்றார், அமெரிக்காவின் ரிச்சர்டு ப்ரவுன் வெள்ளி வென்றார். அந்தப் போட்டிதான் தரவரிசையில் மாற்றத்தை உண்டாக்கியது மற்றும் எனக்கு மற்றொரு விவாதத்தையும் வழங்கியது. ஏற்கனவே மூன்றாவது பெரிய அணியை அனுப்பியிருந்தும், அமெரிக்கா அறிவுறுத்தப்பட்ட பதக்கப் பட்டியலில் வெறும் ஆறாவது இடத்தில் தான் இருந்தது. சியன்.என். பராலிம்பிக்ஐ மிகுந்த விரிவில் ஒளிபரப்பினும், என்.பி.சி நான்கு மணி நேர சிறப்பு நிகழ்ச்சிகளை மட்டும் வெளியிட்டது. முன்னாள் பராலிம்பியனும் அமெரிக்க அணித்தலைவருமான ஐமீ முலின்ஸ் இந்த குறைபாட்டை The Guardian பத்திரிகையில் பகிர்ந்தார். மாற்றுத் திறனாளிகள் உரிமை பற்றி முன்னணி நாடாக இருந்தும், நேரடி ஒளிபரப்பில் குறைவான கவனம் வருத்தமளிப்பதாக அவர் தெரிவித்தார். இத்தகைய குறைந்த ஒளிபரப்பு வருத்தமளிக்கும்; article_content: A casino boat, the Escapade, carrying 123 people on its maiden voyage from Savannah, ran aground near Tybee Island, Georgia, and remained stranded overnight after initial Coast Guard rescue attempts were unsuccessful due to broken tow lines. Passengers and crew, wearing life vests, became increasingly frustrated as hours passed, but the Coast Guard confirmed there were no injuries or medical issues. Family members waiting on shore received updates from passengers by phone and expressed concern while noting that those on board were being given food and water and were kept calm. Petty Officer 1st Class Lauren Jorgensen said the Coast Guard planned to transfer small groups from the Escapade to a larger cutter, the Maria Bray, using smaller boats. The Escapade, a 174-foot casino ship operated by Florida-based Tradewinds Casino Cruise, was stranded about 1.8 miles off the north end of Tybee Island in the Calibogue Sound, near Hilton Head, South Carolina. The vessel’s crew reported a possible malfunction with the chart plotter, part of the navigation system, but the Coast Guard had not confirmed any technical issues. Tradewinds Casino Cruise, which offered free passage for the inaugural Savannah cruise, did not respond to requests for comment. Family members, including Tommy Eaton, waited at the dock and shared that passengers had expressed mechanical concerns and discomfort during the unexpected delay. Despite the situation, shipping at the Port of Savannah was not affected, according to a Georgia Ports Authority spokesperson.

article_content: Australia Day was celebrated across the nation today, with weather conditions differing from city to city. Sydney and Melbourne saw drizzle and cool temperatures, but committed partygoers still enjoyed the national holiday. In contrast, Brisbane and Perth experienced sunshine and warm weather, with Perth expecting temperatures up to 37°C. In Sydney, thousands gathered at the Harbour, some waving miniature flags and others huddling under umbrellas, to participate in events like the Great Australian Swim. Around 1,000 swimmers braved the cool water near the Opera House. While there were fewer private boats this year, swimmers were joined by the HMAS Canberra, where a 21-gun salute occurred at midday and schoolchildren performed 'I Am Australian.' The RAAF jets flew over the Harbour, though they were hard to see due to dense clouds. Elsewhere, Australians dressed in green and gold for the celebrations, with ferry races, fireboats, and a variety of festivities in cities including Melbourne and the Gold Coast. Sports events continued despite the weather. At the Sydney Cricket Ground, fans donned ponchos and watched as rain threatened to delay the cricket match between Australia and India. At the Australian Open, Victoria Azarenka was seen keeping warm with towels in 17°C weather, and Rosie Batty, newly named Australian of the Year, attended matches at Melbourne Park. Prime Minister Tony Abbott welcomed 25 new Australian citizens at a ceremony by Lake Burley Griffin in Canberra, paying tribute to Rosie Batty for her courage and advocacy for domestic violence victims. Adelaide had pleasant temperatures of around 23°C, while Queensland lived up to its 'Sunshine State' name with highs of 34°C. Perth saw temperatures reach 37°C. Celebrities like Lisa Wilkinson, Karl Stefanovic, Hamish Blake, and Kate Richie shared photos on social media in celebration. There were also unique events like the Australia Day Thong Challenge at Bondi Beach and performances by The Wiggles. The Australian and Indigenous flags were flown above the Sydney Harbour Bridge, and a traditional citizenship ceremony took place in Canberra. Despite some cancellations, such as Taylor Swift votes being disqualified from the Triple J Hottest 100, the spirit of the day remained strong.

Akhmed Zakayev, an exiled Chechen political figure based in Britain, argues that the Boston Marathon bombing could bolster Russian President Vladimir Putin's push for stronger Western support in Russia's campaign against Chechen militants. Zakayev, who previously served as Chechnya's deputy prime minister during its separatist era, maintains that Chechen culture is not to blame for the marathon attack, which authorities say was carried out by brothers Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev. He warns that Russia may use this incident to justify increasing its control over the Caucasus.

Having left Russia after it reclaimed control over Chechnya, Zakayev continues to openly criticize Putin. He describes the focus on the attackers' Chechen roots as a 'gift' to the Kremlin, reinforcing Russian efforts to connect Chechen issues with global terrorism. Russian officials have cited the bombing to highlight their claims of Chechens presenting an international threat and to urge more collaboration with Western intelligence agencies.

Military expert Igor Korotchenko and former Kremlin adviser Alexander Nekrassov have expressed disappointment with the limited security cooperation from the West, suggesting that providing refuge to Chechen exiles poses risks. In response, Zakayev insists it is unjust to blame the broader Chechen nation for isolated acts, and he notes—without proof—the rapid Russian reaction to the bombing, drawing a parallel to past suspicions like the 1999 apartment bombings.

The Tsarnaev brothers, who are of Chechen descent, spent their early years in Kyrgyzstan and Dagestan before moving to the United States in 2002. Zakayev highlights their American upbringing as evidence that Chechnya itself should not be held responsible for the Boston bombing, reaffirming that the Chechen people oppose terrorism and seek political solutions through peaceful means. The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), under the leadership of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin, has publicly announced its support for the Congress party in the forthcoming Telangana Assembly elections. In a statement issued Tuesday, DMK instructed its Telangana members to join forces with Congress, organize election committees, and work vigorously to boost the INDIA bloc’s chances. The Telangana Assembly poll is set for November 30, while the results will be declared on December 3.

The key contest features the incumbent Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), led by K Chandrashekar Rao, up against the Congress and the BJP. Furthermore, YSR Telangana Party president YS Sharmila, daughter of former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister YS Rajasekhara Reddy, stated their party will step aside from the polls and back Congress, seeking to oust what she calls the BRS’s 'corrupt and anti-people' rule. Voters in Telangana will decide the outcome of 119 assembly seats.

article_content: Matty Fryatt scored his first goal for league leaders Nottingham Forest as Stuart Pearce's side came from behind to secure a 2-1 victory over Bournemouth. Summer signing Fryatt headed in Jack Hunt's cross past Lee Camp in the 72nd minute, completing an impressive turnaround. Bournemouth, seeking a third consecutive win this season, dominated early and took the lead after 58 minutes when new £3 million striker Callum Wilson netted his third goal of the campaign. Britt Assombalonga equalized for Forest after 67 minutes, heading in Andy Reid's cross, before Fryatt's decisive goal sealed the win. In another fixture, substitute Magaye Gueye scored an equalizer in the fifth minute of injury time as Millwall secured a 1-1 draw at Sheffield Wednesday. Gueye fired his first goal for the Lions into the roof of Keiren Westwood's net with virtually the last kick of the game, after Chris Maguire had put Wednesday ahead in the second half. Shaun Williams missed a second-half penalty for Millwall. Watford handed Rotherham a difficult lesson in the Championship, staging a late surge at New York Stadium to win 2-0. Lloyd Dyer’s first league goal for the club gave Watford the lead in the 73rd minute, while Gianni Munari secured the points five minutes from time. Norwich City overcame a poor start to earn a hard-fought 3-1 win against Blackburn Rovers at Carrow Road. Bradley Johnson scored a superb left-foot effort in the 87th minute to put the Canaries ahead, before Lewis Grabban added a second deep in injury time for his second of the night. Grabban had earlier canceled out Tom Cairney’s early opener for Blackburn. Blackpool remain rooted to the bottom of the division after suffering a 2-1 defeat to Brentford at Bloomfield Road. Nathan Delfouneso had put the hosts in front, but Alex Pritchard and Stuart Dallas scored to deliver Brentford’s first victory of the season. Elsewhere, Reading lost 2-1 at home to Huddersfield Town, as Jacob Butterfield and Harry Bunn scored for the visitors, while Simon Cox netted a consolation for the Royals 11 minutes from time.

article_content: The Akwa Ibom State Government has officially signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Navy Holdings Limited, a subsidiary of the Nigerian Navy, to establish the Ibom Fish City Project. During the MoU signing at the Government House in Uyo on Thursday, Governor Umo Eno explained that this agreement aligns with his administration's vision to harness the blue economy. He emphasized that the partnership would strengthen the existing relationship between the state and the Navy. Governor Eno noted that discussions on the project began under the previous administration when he served as the Commissioner for Lands and Water Resources. He expressed appreciation to the firm’s management for their steadfastness. "Today’s signing of the MoU marks a commitment between the Nigerian Navy and Akwa Ibom State Government. It demonstrates our readiness to collaborate and move the project forward," Eno stated. He also highlighted the involvement of the Akwa Ibom Investment Corporation, the investment arm of the government, drawing a parallel with Naval Holdings as the Nigerian Navy’s business arm. Eno underscored the state’s dual interest in economic growth and maritime security, stating that the project would not only create jobs but also help secure the waterways. He noted Rear Admiral Ayo Olugbode’s assurance that the project would improve security in the area. "We want our waterways to be safe for business, and this partnership brings economic and security benefits. We hope this becomes a model for other coastal states," Eno said. Earlier, Rear Admiral Hamza Kaoje, Group Managing Director of Navy Holdings, thanked the governor for his commitment to the state’s development and for facilitating the project. He added that the partnership would add significant value to Akwa Ibom. Rear Admiral Ayo Olugbode, Hydrographer of the Nigerian Navy, stated that upon completion in five years, the Ibom Fish City Project is expected to generate around N500 million in revenue and provide employment for between 2,000 and 5,000 people, depending on its scale.

article_content: An Italian construction engineer, Marco Vallisa, who was abducted in Libya four months ago, has been freed and is returning home after his captors reportedly received a ransom payment of one million euros. The Italian Foreign Ministry confirmed Vallisa's release, though it did not provide details about how he was freed. However, a security source in Libya stated that Vallisa had been held by an armed militia, who released him upon receiving the ransom. The practice of paying ransoms has faced criticism from officials including U.S. President Barack Obama and British Prime Minister David Cameron, who argue that such payments encourage further acts of terrorism against Western countries. Vallisa, 54, was working in the coastal city of Zwara for the Italian construction company Piacentini Costruzioni when he was kidnapped on July 5. Two colleagues, Bosnian national Petar Matic and Macedonian Emilio Gafuri, were abducted with him but released two days later. Since the toppling of former Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi in a NATO-backed revolt three years ago, Libya has seen ongoing instability, with various militias and rival governments vying for control. The Fajr Libya coalition, an Islamist militia group, currently controls Tripoli and western parts of the country. The region remains unsafe, with several foreigners still held by armed groups. Marco Bricconi, mayor of Vallisa’s hometown Cadeo, described his release as 'the end of a nightmare.' Despite Vallisa's return, at least five Italians are believed to be held by abductors worldwide. Among them are aid workers Vanessa Marzullo and Greta Ramelli, who went missing in Syria in July, Jesuit priest Paolo Dall’Oglio who was kidnapped in Syria in 2013, engineer Gianluca Salviato kidnapped in Libya in March, and aid worker Giovanni Lo Porto, who disappeared near the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in 2012.

article_content:
French club Lyon extended their dominance over Real Madrid with a 1-0 victory on Tuesday night, leaving the Spanish giants in danger of being eliminated from the Champions League at the last-16 stage for the sixth consecutive season. Lyon takes a narrow advantage into the second leg of the tie, thanks to a remarkable second-half goal from Jean Makoun. Real Madrid, who have now failed to score on their last three visits to Lyon's Stade Gerland, will try to overturn the deficit next month at their home stadium, the Santiago Bernabeu, which is set to host the final in May.

Real Madrid president Florentino Perez invested heavily in new signings such as Cristiano Ronaldo and Kaka with the specific aim of reclaiming the Champions League title and ending Barcelona's dominance. However, coach Manuel Pellegrini has struggled, with his team sitting second behind Barcelona in La Liga and suffering an early exit from the Copa del Rey. Pellegrini will hope his star-studded squad can recover from this latest setback.

Both teams created chances in the first half, with Lyon nearly taking the lead five minutes before the break when winger Cesar Delgado struck the post following a corner from Miralem Pjanic. Just two minutes after halftime, Cameroon midfielder Makoun was allowed to advance close to the Real Madrid goal before unleashing a powerful shot past goalkeeper Iker Casillas into the top corner.

Cristiano Ronaldo came close to equalizing for Real with a deflected long-range effort, but the Spanish side were almost caught on the counterattack, only for Casillas to deny Aly Cissokho. Gonzalo Higuain tested Lyon goalkeeper Hugo Lloris before making way for former Lyon star Karim Benzema with fifteen minutes remaining, but Real Madrid failed to find an equalizer.

Google is rolling out a highly anticipated 'portrait touch-up' feature on Google Meet, allowing users to apply beauty effects during video calls. Announced in a recent Google Workspace update, the feature is currently being introduced to mobile users with premium Google accounts, with a wider release planned for October 28th. The web version of Google Meet is expected to receive this feature by the end of 2023.

Portrait touch-up offers two modes—'Subtle' and 'Smoothing'—which provide varying levels of complexion smoothing, under-eye lightening, and teeth whitening. 'Subtle' mode makes slight cosmetic adjustments, while 'Smoothing' mode delivers more enhanced effects. Google states that the feature is designed for light touch-ups, not drastic changes to one's appearance.

This new option can be enabled in Google Meet settings and will be turned off by default. It's limited to premium Google account holders, including Business Standard, Business Plus, Enterprise Essentials, Education Plus, Google One, and Workspace Individual accounts. Personal Google accounts will not have access to portrait touch-up.

Given the popularity of beauty filters in apps like TikTok and Instagram, and similar features already available in Microsoft Teams and Zoom, Google's addition of portrait touch-up is seen as a welcome update—particularly for users who may prefer a polished look during workplace video calls.

Since the October 7 Hamas attacks in southern Israel, which resulted in the deaths of more than 1,400 people, European leaders have been visiting Israel to demonstrate their support. Among those who have recently stood alongside Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Tel Aviv are the leaders of France, the United Kingdom, Germany, the Netherlands, Greece, and Italy. As German Chancellor Olaf Scholz put it during his visit ten days after the attacks, "In such difficult times, there is only one place we can be: at Israel’s side."

However, analysts note that these visits reflect a complex diplomatic stance rather than simple solidarity. While the trips signal a significant shift in Europe’s willingness to openly back Israel, they also convey worries about regional stability and the risk of a broader conflict. European leaders, concerned about the potential for an expanded war and its consequences—such as a new refugee crisis—are urging Netanyahu to proceed with caution regarding an anticipated ground offensive in Gaza.

George Tzogopoulos, an international relations expert at Greece's ELIAMEP institute, describes this as an unprecedented level of EU support for Israel. Traditionally, European statements have promoted a two-state solution and discouraged actions that could escalate the conflict. Yet, since October 7, Europe's rhetoric has shifted, signaling stronger backing for Israel.

Following the attack, Prime Minister Netanyahu vowed to "destroy Hamas" as Israel launched counter-offensives in Gaza. The European Union initially considered suspending aid to Palestinians but ultimately did not take that action. However, EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has expressed unequivocal support for Israel, even as airstrikes have killed more than 7,000 people in Gaza and as the Israeli siege there has forced many hospitals to close. Von der Leyen’s stance has attracted criticism from hundreds of EU staff members.

Aristotle Tziampiris, a professor at the University of Piraeus, told Al Jazeera that Western leaders have offered “absolute, sincere, unapologetic support for Israel’s war with Hamas,” predicting that a ground war is imminent. He noted that European governments fear further attacks not only in Israel but potentially in other regions. Past incidents, such as the 2015 Paris attacks involving militants who entered Europe as asylum seekers, highlight those concerns.

Some European countries, especially in southern Europe, are particularly worried about a wider regional conflict involving Iran that could trigger mass displacement, according to Emmanuel Karagiannis of King’s College London. He added that both American and European officials seek to advance normalization between Israel and Arab countries through the Abraham Accords. The war in Gaza, however, threatens both this process and the broader pursuit of peace in the Middle East at a time when Western governments are also focused on Russia and China.

To balance these factors, EU leaders have combined solidarity with calls for restraint. After meeting Netanyahu, Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte wrote on X (formerly Twitter), "Civilian casualties and regional escalation must be prevented. This requires restraint from Israel when it comes to the use of force." The Netherlands and the UK have called for temporary humanitarian pauses to allow aid into Gaza, where medical centers face severe shortages. EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell has also demanded a ceasefire to ensure delivery of humanitarian aid.

While Israel has allowed some aid to enter Gaza via the Rafah crossing with Egypt, both Gaza’s Health Ministry and international aid groups stress that basic needs remain unmet. The US, Israel’s traditional ally, has also urged caution; President Joe Biden said he warned Israel not to “be blinded by rage,” noting the mistakes the US made post-9/11.

Some experts see an opportunity for the international community to play a more constructive role. Tziampiris suggests rebuilding Gaza with an emphasis on promoting democracy, human rights, and economic growth, alongside ensuring Israeli security. European leaders appear to acknowledge that, whatever happens next, future talks between Israeli and Palestinian leaders will be necessary for long-term peace. French President Emmanuel Macron said the fight against Hamas "must be without mercy but not without rules," reiterating the need for a two-state solution. Dutch Prime Minister Rutte echoed this, insisting that lasting security can only be achieved through renewed prospects for a Palestinian state alongside a secure Israel. Whether Netanyahu will heed these messages remains to be seen.

கிரீஸில் உள்ள ELIAMEP நிறுவனத்தின் சர்வதேச உறவு நிபுணர் ஜார்ஜ் ட்ஸோகோபொலோஸ், இது இஸ்ரேலுக்கு கிடைக்கும் பெரிய அளவிலான ஐரோப்பிய ஒன்றிய ஆதரவாக இருக்கிறது என்று கூறுகிறார். பொதுவாக, ஐரோப்பிய தலைவர்கள் இரு-மாநில தீர்வுக்கு ஆதரவு நல்குவார்கள், ஆனால் இம்முறை இஸ்ரேலை வலுவாக ஆதரிக்கிறார்கள்.

தாக்குதலைத் தொடர்ந்து, பிரதமர் நேதன்யாகு “ஹமாஸை அழிப்பேன்” என்று உறுதி கூறினார், அதே சமயம் இஸ்ரேல் காசாவில் பதிலடி நடவடிக்கையை மேற்கொண்டுள்ளது. ஐரோப்பிய ஒன்றியம், ஆரம்பத்தில் பாலஸ்தீனருக்கு உதவியை நிறுத்த கவனித்தது, பின்னர் அதை நிறுத்தவில்லை. ஆனாலும், ஐரோப்பிய ஆணையத் தலைவர் உர்சுலா வான் டெர் லெயன், காசாவில் 7,000க்கும் மேற்பட்டோர் உயிரிழந்த நிலையில், மேலும் மருத்துவமனைகள் மூடப்பட்ட நிலையிலும் இஸ்ரேலை உறுதியாக ஆதரிப்பதாகக் கூறினார். அவரது இந்த நிலைப்பாடு பல நூற்றுக்கணக்கான ஐரோப்பிய ஊழியர்களின் விமர்சனத்தை சந்தித்தது.

யுனிவர்சிட்டி ஆஃப் பிறையஸ் பேராசிரியர் அரிஸ்டாட்டில் ட்சியம்பிரிஸ், மேற்கத்திய தலைவர்கள் “மொத்தமும், நேரடியும், மன்னிப்பில்லா ஆதரவு” காட்டுகிறார்கள் என்றும், நிலத்தடி போர் நிகழ வாய்ப்பு உள்ளது என்றும் சொல்கிறார். மேலும், ஐரோப்பிய நாடுகள் பெரும் அகதிகள் பிரச்சினை மற்றும் முந்தைய தாக்குதல்களின் விளைவுகளை எப்படி சமாளிப்பது என்பதில் கவலை கொண்டுள்ளன. 2015 பாரிஸ் தாக்குதல்களில் ஏற்கனவே அகதிகள் வழியாக வந்த பயங்கரவாதிகள் இருந்தனர்.

தெற்கு ஐரோப்பியா நாடுகள் பெரும் பிராந்திய போர் ஏற்படும் அபாயத்திற்கு உள்ளதாக Emmanuel Karagiannis (King’s College London) கருத்து கூறுகிறார். அமெரிக்கா மற்றும் ஐரோப்பிய அதிகாரிகள், Abraham Accords வழியாக இஸ்ரேலும், அரபு நாடுகளும் அமைதிக்கு வர வேண்டும் என்பதில் கவனம் செலுத்துகின்றனர். ஆனால், தற்போது காசாவில் நிகழும் போர் அந்த அமைதி யுனியையும், ரஷ்யா மற்றும் சீனாவிடம் மேற்கத்திய தேசங்கள் எதிர்கொண்டும், புதிதாக சிக்கல்களை உருவாக்குகிறது.

இவற்றை சமனிலைப்படுத்த, ஐரோப்பிய தலைவர்கள் ஆதரவில் எச்சரிக்கையையும் காட்டுகிறார்கள். நெதர்லாந்து பிரதமர் மார்க் ருட்டே X-இல் (“பார்மர்லி ட்விட்டர்”) தெரிவித்தார்: “பொதுமக்கள் உயிர் மற்றும் பிராந்திய பிரச்சினைகள் தவிர்க்கப்பட வேண்டும். இஸ்ரேல் தனது ஆயுதத்தின் பயன்பாட்டில் பொறுமை காட்ட வேண்டும்.” நெதர்லாந்தும், ஐக்கிய இராச்சியமும், காசாவுக்கு மருந்து, உணவு மற்றும் எரிப்பொருள் அனுப்ப இடைக்கால இடைவேளை வழங்க வேண்டும் என்று கேட்டுள்ளனர். ஐரோப்பிய ஒன்றியத்தின் வெளிவிவகாரத் தலைவர் ஜோசெப் போரெல்லும் ஹ்யூமனிடேரியன் உதவிக்காக போர் குறைக்க வேண்டும் என்று கோரியுள்ளார்.

இஸ்ரேல், எகிப்துடன் இருக்கும் ரபா கடைசி காவல் சாவடியில், சில உதவி வண்டிகளை அனுமதித்தாலும், அடிப்படை சுகாதார தேவைகள் நிறைவாகவில்லை என்று காசாவின் சுகாதார அமைச்சும், சர்வதேச நல அமைப்புக்களும் தெரிவிக்கின்றன. பொதுவாக இணைப்பாக இருந்த அமெரிக்கா கூட சமீபத்தில் இஸ்ரேலுக்கு பொறுமை வேண்டும் என்று ஜனாதிபதி பிடனின் எச்சரிக்கை கூறப்பட்டுள்ளது; 9/11க்கு பிறகு அமெரிக்கா செய்த தவறுகளை அவர் நினைவூட்டினார்.

சில நிபுணர்கள், இந்த சூழல் சர்வதேச சமுதாயத்திற்கு கட்டுமானமான பங்கு வகிக்க இயலும் என்று கருதுகின்றனர். ட்சியம்பிரிஸ், ஜனநாயகம், மனித உரிமை மற்றும் வளி வளர்ச்சி ஆகியவற்றுடன் கூடிய புதுப்பித்த காசா, பாதுகாப்பான இஸ்ரேலை உருவாக்க சிறந்த வாய்ப்பு என்று கூறுகிறார். தொடர்ந்து, பிரெஞ்சு ஜனாதிபதி எமனுவல் மாக்ரோன், ஹமாஸ் மீது போர் “தடையற்றதாக இருக்க வேண்டும், ஆனால் விதிகளுடன் இருக்க வேண்டும்” என்றும், இரு-மாநில தீர்வு அவசியம் என்றும் கூறினார். மார்க் ருட்டேவும் இதையே வலியுறுத்துகிறார். நேதன்யாகு இந்த அறிவுரைகளை ஏற்குமா என்பது விரைவில் தெரியவரும்.

article_content: Kieran Loveridge will serve at least three additional years in prison for fatally punching Sydney teenager Thomas Kelly. Kelly, 18, suffered fatal head injuries after Loveridge punched him in an unprovoked attack in Sydney's Kings Cross district on July 7, 2012. Life support was withdrawn two days later. Loveridge was sentenced in November 2013 to four years for manslaughter, which caused widespread public anger. After a successful prosecution appeal, the NSW Supreme Court of Appeal extended his prison term. Kelly's father said outside court that the family cannot celebrate the longer sentence, stating, 'You can’t balance a life with years in jail.' Chief Justice Tom Bathurst ruled that Loveridge must serve a non-parole period of seven years for Kelly's death. Kelly's younger brother Stuart, 16, spoke emotionally outside court, sharing that he wanted his brother's short life to have meaning and called for greater respect and responsibility in society. Details from the case revealed that on the night of the attack, 19-year-old Loveridge had consumed several Smirnoff double black vodka drinks and shots, and reportedly said he intended to assault someone. Kelly, an accounting cadet, was walking with his girlfriend and talking on the phone when attacked. Loveridge was initially charged with murder but pleaded guilty to manslaughter. The original four-year sentence was met with widespread outrage. After public outcry, the Director of Public Prosecutions appealed the sentence, and the appeal was upheld. The earliest Loveridge can be released from prison is November 17, 2022. The Kelly family emphasized that no sentence can make up for their loss.

X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, has rolled out new subscription options: Premium Plus and Basic. Premium Plus, priced at $16 per month, gives subscribers the largest boost to replies and removes ads from the For You and Following feeds. According to X, this plan expands on the benefits of the standard Premium plan (previously Twitter Blue), which includes a blue checkmark, tweet editing, longer posts, longer video uploads, encrypted direct messages, and more. In addition, a new 'Basic' subscription is now available for $3 per month. It offers a small reply boost but does not include a verification checkmark, reduced ads, or media studio access. Both the Premium Plus and Basic plans are currently available for purchase only via the web. The standard Premium subscription remains available at $8 per month when bought directly.

Earlier this month, Bloomberg reported that X had been testing new paid membership tiers. Since taking ownership last year, Elon Musk has introduced multiple monetization efforts, including requiring users in New Zealand and the Philippines to pay $1 per year to access X. Musk has also added features such as livestreaming, video and audio calling, and has plans to integrate banking services into the platform.

article_content: If you want an example of a football club that seems lost in its own self-importance, look no further than Queens Park Rangers (QPR). After watching their well-paid international players thoroughly outplayed by Everton in the FA Cup at Goodison Park last Saturday, I took the train back to London. While most of us waited patiently in line to board at Lime Street, the QPR players casually walked straight to the first-class carriage at the front. It’s unclear why they deserved such priority. During the journey, some young QPR fans, around nine or ten years old, eagerly ran forward hoping for autographs from their heroes. Unfortunately, security stopped them, telling them they couldn’t get through and suggesting they might catch the players at Euston if they were quick. Despite the team’s poor performance, these young supporters still idolized them, only to be disappointed again. There’s a growing sense that certain players see themselves as exceptionally important, even when their performances don’t match their status. Disturbingly, we’ve also seen unacceptable behavior from fans. For example, Theo Walcott, who will be sidelined for six months with a knee ligament injury, was pelted with coins as he left the pitch, mocking Tottenham fans with a gesture. However, the real issue seems to have been overlooked—why haven’t Tottenham or their fans faced sanctions for such disgraceful conduct? It’s particularly troubling since St John Ambulance volunteers could have been hurt. On the matter of Walcott’s injury ruling him out of the World Cup, I find Arsenal’s decision surprising. If he undergoes surgery soon, there’s an outside chance he could be fit in time, based on other athletes’ recoveries from similar injuries. Arsenal appears to be in no rush, possibly preferring Walcott to return fully fit for next season. Sadly, this means England will miss his talent in Brazil, a significant loss for the team and manager Roy Hodgson. This past weekend also highlighted the widening gap between football clubs and their supporters. Not only did West Ham manager Sam Allardyce, but also co-chairmen David Gold and David Sullivan, ignore the club’s loyal fans and history. Ask any West Ham fan about 1964, 1975, and 1980—they’ll recall those were the years the Hammers won the FA Cup at Wembley. These historic moments are deeply important to supporters. However, Sam Allardyce appeared to disrespect both the FA Cup and fans by fielding a weakened team, leading to a heavy defeat and a blow to squad morale, especially for young players. Many experienced players were left to rest, seemingly unwilling to play three matches in six days. This approach suggests a troubling disconnect between management, players, and fans. Allardyce was once a symbol of traditional English football but now seems to have lost touch, with finishing 17th in the league viewed as an achievement. Gold and Sullivan, despite claiming to be lifelong fans, backed the manager's unpopular decisions. Fans and players still value the FA Cup, but it seems the club's leadership no longer does. There are also concerns about Allardyce’s relationship with captain Kevin Nolan, who was recently sent off twice and left the manager perplexed. This suggests possible issues of respect and discipline within the team. Finally, poor officiating impacted Peterborough United twice recently, with legitimate goals not awarded. Even opposition players admitted the ball crossed the line but did nothing. Greater honesty in football is needed. If it’s acceptable for players to hide the truth about goals, it’s hypocritical to criticize diving or other forms of dishonesty. Football should be about fairness and integrity.

article_content: Genre filmmaker Kiah Roache-Turner has once again partnered with Cornerstone for his latest film, 'Beast of War', which will be launched at the upcoming American Film Market. Described as a survival action thriller, the film follows a group of soldiers stranded in the open ocean as they battle to survive against a great white shark. 'Beast of War' is produced by Blake Northfield of Bronte Pictures ('Streamline', 'Wyrmwood: Apocalypse', 'Escape and Evasion') and Chris Brown of Pictures in Paradise ('Sting', 'Daybreakers', 'The Railway Man'). Production is scheduled to start in 2024 in Australia and Malta. CreatureNFX’s director, Paul Trefry ('Alien: Covenant', 'Unbroken'), will create practical creature effects from his studio in Australia. Trefry is recognized for his collaborations with directors such as James Cameron, Ridley Scott, and Baz Luhrmann. Set in 1942, the film's synopsis follows a warship carrying hundreds of Australian soldiers across the Timor Sea during World War II. When Japanese fighter jets attack, many soldiers are left clinging to makeshift rafts. As tensions rise among the survivors, they face a new threat—a great white shark lurking below, attracted by blood in the water. Alison Thompson and Mark Gooder of Cornerstone expressed their excitement to work with Roache-Turner, noting his distinctive style and expertise in the genre. Roache-Turner began his career in commercials and made his film debut with 'Wyrmwood: Road of the Dead' in 2015. His subsequent films include 'Nekrotonic', which premiered at the 2018 Toronto International Film Festival, and 'Wyrmwood: Apocalypse', which won the Audience Award at the 2021 Sydney Film Festival. Cornerstone is also managing the worldwide sales and distribution for Roache-Turner's upcoming arachnophobia-themed horror film 'Sting', which will be released by Studiocanal in several regions.

CreatureNFX இயக்குநர் Paul Trefry (‘Alien: Covenant’, ‘Unbroken’) தனது ஆஸ்திரேலிய ஸ்டுடியோவில் உயிரின விலங்கு விளைவுகளை உருவாக்குகிறார். அவர் James Cameron, Ridley Scott மற்றும் Baz Luhrmann உடன் பணியாற்றியவர். 1942-ஆம் ஆண்டு, டிமோர் கடலில் நூற்றுக்கணக்கான ஆஸ்திரேலிய சிப்பாய்கள் ஒரு போர் கப்பலில் WW2 முன்னணி புறப்படுகின்றனர். ஜப்பான் போர் விமானங்கள் தாக்கிய பிறகு, பலர் தனிப்பட்ட படுகையில் உயிர் தக்க வைக்க தொடங்குகின்றனர். அவர்களின் மீதான பரபரப்பில், ரத்தத்தின் வாசனைக்கு கீழே lurking செய்யும் பெரிய வெள்ளை சுறா முக்கியமான அபாயம் ஆக முன்வருகிறது. Cornerstone-இன் Alison Thompson மற்றும் Mark Gooder, Roache-Turner உடன் மீண்டும் பணியாற்றும் வாய்ப்பில் உற்சாகம் தெரிவித்துள்ளனர். அவரது தனிப்பட்ட பாணி குறித்து அவர்கள் பாராட்டினர். Mohamed Muizzu’s victory in the Maldivian presidential election is viewed by analysts as a setback for India, a boost for China, and an indicator of rising tensions in the Indian Ocean region. The Maldives, a nation of about half a million people spread over more than 1,000 islands, garnered global attention with its recent presidential run-off.

Muizzu, an opposition candidate who favors closer relations with China, received 54 percent of the vote according to official results. He defeated incumbent President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, who is widely seen as pro-India.

After winning, Muizzu declared, “With today’s result, we have got the opportunity to build the country’s future. The strength to ensure the freedom of Maldives.”

The election was widely viewed as a referendum on foreign policy, particularly regarding ties with India and China. India currently has around 75 military personnel in the Maldives, maintaining and operating helicopters and an aircraft it had donated. During his campaign, Muizzu pledged to remove these Indian troops.

“From the lens of great power competition, Beijing is a big winner from this election,” said Michael Kugelman, South Asia director at the Wilson Center. He noted Muizzu’s campaign was about not just strengthening Beijing ties but also aiming to reduce India’s role in the Maldives, especially by calling to end the Indian military presence. “This is welcome news for Beijing,” he added.

However, analysts predict that India will continue seeking to maintain its influence. After Muizzu’s win, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated him, stating that India remains committed to strengthening its relationship and cooperation in the Indian Ocean region.

Under President Solih, India enjoyed close ties with the Maldives, investing substantial sums in infrastructure (hundreds of millions of dollars). Author Shantanu Roy-Chaudhury remarked that India will support the new government and likely proceed with major initiatives like the Greater Male Connectivity Project—a 6.7 km road connecting the capital to island suburbs—funded by a $100 million grant and $400 million line of credit from India.

Still, Roy-Chaudhury warned, a pro-China government might place Indian influence and investments under review.

Muizzu, a 45-year-old civil engineer, has criticized the current India-Maldives trade imbalance, vowing reforms. Trade tilts toward India—India exported $416 million to Maldives in 2021, importing $49 million—while China’s trade is also uneven ($395 million in exports, $3.9 million in imports).

Muizzu rose as the Progressive Party’s candidate after his predecessor Yameen (pro-China, ex-president) was jailed for corruption. Under Yameen, Maldives accrued over $1 billion in Chinese loans for infrastructure, including housing and a bridge connecting the capital to key nearby islands and the airport.

Analysts believe this leadership change may draw more Chinese investment. Kugelman observed that Chinese business activity has persisted even under Solih’s pro-India government, and that Muizzu’s victory could further encourage Chinese investors and officials. Still, Kugelman stressed that India will keep asserting its partnership with the Maldives.

Looking ahead to Muizzu’s November 17 inauguration, Roy-Chaudhury expects that Maldives will likely need to balance relations with both India and China, as India continues emphasizing development aid and cooperation. “India and the Maldives both need each other,” he said.

சீனாவுடன் நெருங்கும் உறவுக்கு ஆதரவு வழங்கும் எதிர்க்கட்சித் தலைவர் முஇஸ்ஸு, 54% வாக்குகளை எடுத்து, தற்போதைய ஜனாதிபதி இப்ராஹிம் மொஹமட் சோலிஹை தோற்கடித்தார். அவர் இந்தியாபக்க நோக்குடன் இருப்பவராக பார்க்கப்படுகிறார்.

வெற்றிக்குப் பிறகு முஇஸ்ஸு, "இன்றைய முடிவால், நாட்டு எதிர்காலத்தை கட்டியெழுப்பும் வாய்ப்பும், மாலத்தீவின் சுதந்திரத்தை உறுதி செய்யும் வலிமையும் கிடைத்துள்ளது" என்று கூறினார்.

இந்தத் தேர்தல், வெளிநாட்டு கொள்கையின் ரெஃபெரெண்டமாகவே (வாக்கெடுப்பு போன்று) காணப்படுகிறது, குறிப்பாக இந்தியா மற்றும் சீனாவுடன் உறவு குறித்து. இந்தியா தற்போது மாலத்தீவில் 75 ராணுவப்பணியாளர்களை வைத்திருக்கிறதோடு, தானாக வழங்கிய ஹெலிகாப்டர்களும் ஒரு விமானமும் அவர்களால் பராமரிக்கப்படுகிறது. இந்த ராணுவத்தை வெளியேற்றுவேனா என்று முஇஸ்ஸு தனது பிரசாரத்தில் வாக்குறுதி அளித்தார்.

“பெரும் சக்தி போட்டியின் கோணத்தில், இந்தத் தேர்தல் சீனாவுக்கு பெரும் வெற்றி,” என்று வில்சன் சென்டரின் தென் ஆசிய இயக்குநர் மைக்கேல் குகெல்மன் குறிப்பிட்டார். முஇஸ்ஸுவின் பிரச்சாரம் சீனாவுடன் உறவுகளை வலுப்படுத்த விரும்புவது மட்டுமல்லாமல் இந்தியாவின் பங்கையும் குறைக்க நோக்கப்படுவதாகவும், இந்திய ராணுவத்தை வெளியேற்ற அழைப்பதும் சீனாவுக்குப் பழி கொண்டதாகவும் அவர் என்றார்.

இருப்பினும், இந்தியா தனது தாக்கத்தைின்றி விடாது என்றும், புதிய ஜனாதிபதி வெற்றிக்குப் பிறகு, பிரதமர் நரேந்திர மோடி வாழ்த்துகளை தெரிவித்தார். இந்தியா மாலத்தீவுடன் உறவை வலுப்படுத்தவும், இந்தியப் பெருங்கடல் பகுதியில் ஒத்துழைப்பை மேம்படுத்தவும் உறுதி அளித்தார்.

சோலிஹ் பதவிக்காலத்தில் இந்தியா மற்றும் மாலதீவிடம் நெருங்கிய உறவை வைத்திருந்தது, கட்டுமான வளர்ச்சிக்கு நூறுகள் மில்லியன் டாலர் முதலீடு செய்தது. எழுத்தாளர் ஷாந்தனு ராய்-சவுத்ரி தெரிவித்தபோது, இந்தியா புதிய அரசை ஆதரிக்கவும், 6.7 கிலோமீட்டர் பாதை கொண்ட கிரேட்டர் மாலே கனெக்டிவிட்டி திட்டம் உள்ளிட்ட திட்டங்களை தொடரவும் திட்டமிட்டு இருப்பதாகவும் கூறினார் – இது $100 மில்லியன் மானியமும் $400 மில்லியன் கடனும் இந்தியாவின் பங்காக உள்ளது.

புதிய அரசின் சீன அனுகூல இப்பெயர்ச்சியால், இந்திய முதலீடுகள் மற்றும் திட்டங்கள் கேள்விக்குறியாகும் எனவும் ராய்-சவுத்ரி எச்சரிக்கை செய்கிறார்.

45 வயது சிவில் இன்ஜினியரான முஇஸ்ஸு, இந்தியாவுடன் உள்ள வர்த்தகச் சமநிலையில் குறைபாடுகள் உள்ளதாக விமர்சித்தும், மாற்றத்திற்காக உறுதியளித்தும் இருக்கிறார். இந்தியா 2021-ல் மாலத்தீவிற்கு $416 மில்லியன் ஏற்றுமதி செய்திருப்பதும், $49 மில்லியன் இறக்குமதி செய்திருப்பதும் காணப்படுவதாகவும்; சீனாவில் இருந்து $395 மில்லியன் எடுத்து $3.9 மில்லியன் என்பது குறைவாக உள்ளது எனவும் தெளிவுப்படுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது.

முன்னாள் ஜனாதிபதி யமீன் (சீனாபம்மை கொண்டவர்) ஊழல் வழக்கில் சிறையில் இருப்பதால் முஇஸ்ஸு எதிர்க்கட்சித் தலைவராக பதவி ஏற்றார். யமீன் ஆட்சியில் மாலத்தீவ் சீனாவில் இருந்து $1 பில்லியனுக்கும் மேல் கடன் எடுத்து பெரிய கட்டுமான திட்டங்களைச் செய்தது.

இந்த தலைமை மாற்றம் சீன முதலீட்டுக்கு வாய்ப்பு தரும் என நிபுணர்கள் கருதுகிறார்கள். சோலிஹ் ஆட்சியில் கூட சீன வணிக அடிப்படையிலான சேவைகள் தொடர்ந்ததையும், முஇஸ்ஸுவின் வெற்றியால் சீன முதலீட்டாளர்கள் மற்றும் அதிகாரிகள் ஊக்கமடைவார்கள் என குகெல்மன் கூறுகிறார். அதேசமயம், இந்தியா அனுதாப ஒத்துழைப்பை விலக்காது என்பது நம்பிக்கை.

நவம்பர் 17ல் பதவியேற்கும் முன்னோக்கி, இரு பெரிய நாடுகளுடனும் சமநிலை நடத்தியே செல்ல வேண்டியிருக்கும் என ராய்-சவுத்ரி கூறினார். அபிவிருத்தி உதவி மற்றும் ஒத்துழைப்பில் இந்தியா வலியுறுத்தும் என்று அவர் சொல்லினார். “இந்தியா, மாலதீவ் இருவரும் ஒருவருக்கொருவர் தேவை.”
