article_content: A California judge on Thursday denied a request from actress Cindy Lee Garcia to have an inflammatory anti-Islam video removed from YouTube. Garcia, who appeared in the film 'Innocence of Muslims,' alleges she was a victim of fraud, invasion of privacy, and misappropriation of her likeness. She sued the film's producer, Nakoula Basseley Nakoula, along with YouTube and its parent company, Google, claiming the video caused her irreparable harm. Garcia's lawsuit, filed in Los Angeles Superior Court, asserted that she was misled about the film, believing she was acting in an 'adventure film' and would be playing a concerned mother. She claims the final product falsely portrays her as making anti-Islamic statements that she never intended. YouTube's attorney, Timothy Alger, argued that federal law protects platforms such as YouTube from being compelled by third parties to remove content. On Thursday, Judge Luis Lavin of Los Angeles County Superior Court denied Garcia's request for a temporary restraining order, allowing the video to remain online. Garcia told CNN she was unaware her dialogue was dubbed over and anti-Islam sentiments added, and said she has faced death threats and lost her job since the video's release. The film, which was posted online in September and mocks the Islamic Prophet Mohammed, prompted protests and violence in several countries, some targeting U.S. diplomatic missions. Attempts to reach Nakoula for comment were unsuccessful.

article_content: Germany's World Cup victory this summer earned them a fourth star on their shirts, but also saw the retirement of key experienced players. Captain Philipp Lahm, Arsenal's Per Mertesacker, and World Cup record goalscorer Miroslav Klose all retired from international football at the peak of their careers, taking with them the experience of 354 caps. With injuries affecting the squad, coach Joachim Low gave opportunities to the next generation of German players. Here is Sportsmail's assessment of their performances against Scotland:  Sebastian Rudy (Age: 24) | Position: Midfielder (played right back vs. Scotland) | Club: Hoffenheim | Minutes played: 90 Though not a traditional newcomer at 24, Rudy is still inexperienced at the international level, making just his third appearance—his second since the World Cup. Scotland's defensive approach, especially on the flanks, allowed Rudy to push forward into his usual midfield positions, helping set up Thomas Müller's opening goal. He provided the assist with a cross that Müller headed past David Marshall. In the first half, Rudy found space on the right and delivered several crosses into the box, as Germany controlled the wide areas. He completed all 30 of his passes in the first period and had a shot on goal, which Marshall saved. However, the second half proved challenging; Rudy struggled against Scotland's counter-attacks, particularly when Ikechi Anya scored the equalizer. Rudy’s unfamiliarity with the right back position was evident at times as the visitors gained confidence.  Erik Durm (Age: 22) | Position: Left back | Club: Borussia Dortmund | Minutes played: 90 Durm benefited from Scotland’s defensive stance, often pushing Barry Bannan back and supporting Germany’s attacks. He created an early chance for Müller and troubled Marshall with a long-range strike. Durm was fortunate to avoid a red card after cynically fouling Steven Naismith as Scotland threatened a second equalizer. Overall, it was a solid performance defensively and going forward.  Christoph Kramer (Age: 23) | Position: Midfielder | Club: Bayer Leverkusen (on loan at Borussia Mönchengladbach) | Minutes played: 90 As Toni Kroos's midfield partner, Kramer deputized well for Bastian Schweinsteiger and Sami Khedira. Having made his first competitive start in the World Cup final, Kramer took on a more active role this time, defending deep and advancing through midfield. Linked to Manchester United, Kramer’s performance added resilience to Germany’s midfield, and he helped repel several Scottish attacks early in the game. article_content: Heathrow and Gatwick airports could be linked by a high-speed rail network to create the world’s first ‘virtual hub’ airport, under proposals being considered by ministers. The project, nicknamed ‘Heathwick’, would involve a £5 billion high-speed rail link connecting the west London and west Sussex sites in just 15 minutes. Trains would travel at up to 180 mph, depart every five minutes, and follow the M25 route. Heathwick passengers and their baggage would need to transfer between airports within 75 minutes for the hub concept to work. The proposal aims to reduce flight congestion over London. Gatwick airport and business groups have welcomed the plans, but BAA (Heathrow’s operator) and budget airlines Ryanair and EasyJet oppose the idea. BAA told The Times that 'a virtual hub' presents significant technical, operational, political, and financial challenges, and would not solve the southeast's runway capacity problem. Business leaders are urging the government to improve air links, fearing Britain could lose trade deals with emerging markets like China and Brazil. Supporters say Heathwick would be quicker and cheaper than building a new Thames Estuary airport and would help London’s airports compete with Charles de Gaulle, Frankfurt, and Schiphol by facilitating more passenger transfers. Currently, Britain loses around £1.2 billion a year in aviation business to France, Germany, and the Netherlands. Victoria Borwick of the Greater London Assembly transport committee supports the scheme, saying that linking Heathrow and Gatwick in 15 minutes would be remarkable. Under the proposals, Gatwick would focus on short and medium-haul European flights, while Heathrow would concentrate on long-haul routes. Low-cost carriers like EasyJet and Ryanair may be asked to move from Gatwick to Stansted or Luton to create more capacity. However, Ryanair’s CEO Michael O’Leary and EasyJet have strongly objected, citing difficulties in relocating budget airlines and the high projected costs of the rail link. Professor David Begg, chairman of the British Chambers of Commerce Infrastructure Commission, has stressed the importance of direct air connections for trade. The government is currently reviewing aviation policy, seeking ways to expand capacity while meeting environmental targets, especially after abandoning the third runway at Heathrow. Challenges remain, such as different ownership of the airports and securing funding during economic uncertainty. Taxpayers are already spending £2 billion annually on the Crossrail project, which is not due for completion until at least 2018. Gatwick airport management has expressed willingness to further discuss the Heathwick proposal with ministers.
translated_content: ஹீத்ரோ மற்றும் கேட்விக் விமான நிலையங்களை உயர்வு வேக ரயில் இணைப்பு மூலம் இணைத்து, உலகத்தில் முதன்முறையாக ‘மெய்நிகர் ஹப்’ விமான நிலையமாக உருவாக்கும் திட்டத்தைக் குறித்துப் அமைச்சர்கள் பரிசீலித்து வருகின்றனர். ‘ஹீத்விக்’ என அழைக்கப்படும் இந்த திட்டம் மூலம் மேற்குப் லண்டன் மற்றும் மேற்குச் சசெக்ஸ் இடையே 15 நிமிடங்கள் என்ற குறுகிய நேரத்தில் பயணிக்கக்கூடிய £5 பில்லியன் மதிப்பிலான உயர் வேக ரயில்கள் இயக்கப்படும். இந்த ரயில்கள் குறைந்தது ஐந்து நிமிடத்திற்கு ஒருமுறை 180 மைல் வேகத்தில் செல்லும்; அவை M25 பாதையில்தான் பயணிக்கும். ஹீத்விக் திட்டத்தின்போது, பயணிகளும் அவர்களின் கூட்டுப் பொருள்களும் 75 நிமிடங்களில் ஒரு விமான நிலையத்திலிருந்து மற்றொன்றுக்கு மாற்றப்பட வேண்டும் என்பது ஹப் யோசனையின் அடிப்படையாகும். இத்திட்டம் லண்டனில் விமான போக்குவரத்து நெரிசலை குறைக்க முயல்கிறது. கேட்விக் விமான நிலையம் மற்றும் வணிக குழுக்கள் திட்டத்திற்கு ஆதரவாக இருக்கின்றனர்; ஆனால் BAA (ஹீத்ரோ இயக்குநர்), ரயனேர், ஈசிஜெட் ஆகிய குறைந்த செலவு விமான நிறுவனங்கள் எதிர்ப்பைக் தெரிவிக்கின்றன. Millions of Americans are facing renewed challenges as federal student loan payments resume after a lengthy pause. The overwhelmed loan servicing system, dealing with 40 million borrowers reentering repayment, has led to widespread issues including incorrect billing, accidental forbearances, and payment processing failures.

At least 20,000 borrowers received incorrect bills—some for enormous sums over $10,000 per month, and one person even got a bill for $108,895.19. More than 15,000 borrowers who had already secured approval for student loan forgiveness were still mistakenly billed, particularly those involved in programs like Borrower Defense to Repayment. Meanwhile, some have been wrongly placed in forbearance for up to a decade or more, and 830,000 became delinquent because they received their bills late or not at all.

There have also been technical glitches, such as payments being rejected or people not realizing they needed to reactivate automatic payments. In response, the Biden administration has stepped up oversight. The Education Department penalized a loan servicing company by withholding $7.2 million and is ensuring harmed borrowers get compensated with measures like waived interest, cancelled payments, or credits toward forgiveness. Education Secretary Miguel Cardona emphasized the government’s commitment to holding servicers accountable and protecting student loan borrowers.

article_content: The United States is increasing its involvement in the Syrian crisis following reports of chemical weapons use. Top officials, including Secretary of State John Kerry, have been active in diplomatic efforts. On Thursday, a day after the alleged attack, Kerry spoke with Syria's Foreign Minister Walid Moallem, insisting that the Syrian government allow immediate access for investigators and criticizing continued attacks that could destroy evidence. Meanwhile, the U.S. military has been preparing for possible action. Defense Secretary Chuck Hagel said a quick response would be necessary if the chemical weapons allegations prove true. U.S. military planners have reportedly updated target options, and a fourth Navy ship armed with cruise missiles has arrived in the eastern Mediterranean. A United Nations investigative team is currently in Syria looking into accusations from opposition groups that forces loyal to President Bashar al-Assad used chemical weapons near Damascus, allegedly killing over 1,300 people. Hagel said the U.S. is assessing the situation and preparing a range of options for President Barack Obama, though he did not list specifics. President Obama and British Prime Minister David Cameron discussed Syria on Saturday, expressing grave concern over the chemical attack reports and agreeing to consult closely on an investigation and potential international responses. Kerry has also been reaching out to key regional players, including officials from Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Turkey, and the Arab League. In a CNN interview, Obama defended his decision so far not to directly intervene militarily, but acknowledged growing U.S. attention might be needed to help end the conflict. He stated he does not anticipate using American ground troops in Syria, though other military actions like airstrikes or cruise missile strikes remain possible. Recent deployments have placed four U.S. Navy destroyers, all armed with cruise missiles, in the region: USS Ramage, USS Mahan, USS Gravelly, and USS Barry. So far, the U.S. has sent some military equipment, logistics, and humanitarian aid to rebel forces. Direct military intervention being considered could focus on limiting Assad's ability to deliver chemical weapons by targeting government facilities and military assets. However, the mobility of Syrian forces and equipment demands flexibility in planning. Senator John McCain has called for stronger action, proposing airstrikes on runways and aircraft, as well as providing advanced weapons to rebels to enforce a 'no fly zone.' However, some administration officials warn that parts of the Syrian opposition have connections to terrorist groups like al Qaeda. Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, General Martin Dempsey, has noted the difficulties in choosing which rebel factions to support, warning that those chosen must be able and willing to advance both their interests and U.S. priorities when the balance of power shifts. Chris Lawrence reported from Washington, David Simpson from Atlanta, with additional contributions from CNN’s Greg Botelho and Jamie Crawford.

article_content:
Florida’s Celebration Health hospital is now equipping its operating room staff with RFID-tagged ID badges to monitor their location and time usage. This workforce tracking system, which began with nurses in 2011, is part of the hospital’s push for greater efficiency and has expanded to more staff. Performance Manager Ashley Simmons states that, while some employees were initially wary about surveillance, their concerns eased once the goal of using the data for positive change became clear.

Data from the system is being used to rearrange work areas, change staff proximity to each other and patients, and adapt shift schedules—all in consultation with workers, who can see their own metrics and share input. Simmons argues this kind of data helps hospitals budget resources, improve both staff and patient experiences, and adopt practices similar to those in other industries.

The trend is much wider: organizations such as Amazon, Tesco, and Autodesk are utilizing wearables to enhance productivity and employee wellness, with reported gains in company performance and, in Autodesk’s case, health-related savings. Ben Waber, head of Sociometric Solutions, creates sophisticated wearable trackers that voluntarily capture employee interactions, providing direct feedback to employees and aggregated data for management. Waber claims these approaches boost workplace satisfaction and retention, pointing to success stories at firms like Bank of America.

Yet, ethical concerns are significant. Professor Kirstie Ball of the Open University warns that monitoring can worsen stress or infringe on privacy if overused or misapplied, while Professor Michael Blakemore of Durham University points out that this tech could enable mass layoffs of lower-performing staff. Both academics note that regulations currently lag behind these surveillance advances, and employees may not fully know their rights.

With the potential for more intrusive technologies, including under-the-skin chips, advocates of employee analytics argue for laws similar to the US HIPAA for data protection. The ongoing debate pits the benefits of increased transparency, efficiency, and well-being against serious questions about ethics, consent, and worker autonomy.

Eva Lily Margerrison was born on August 4 at Sheffield’s Jessop Wing maternity unit, astonishing everyone with her birth weight of 12 pounds 6 ounces. Her parents, Danica Slavin (20) and Sam Margerrison (24), have lovingly nicknamed her ‘Whopper’—a playful tribute to both her size and the fact they first met as co-workers at Burger King.

Eva arrived nine days late through an emergency Caesarean. She is already almost too big for newborn clothes. Danica, on maternity leave from Burger King, and Sam, now a bus driver, say they were stunned to have such a large baby since there’s no history of big newborns in their families. 'We were expecting a big baby, but not this big!' Danica shared. Eva is happy and healthy, and her family couldn't be prouder.

Eva’s grandmother, Carol Slavin, expressed joy over welcoming her first grandchild, remarking how special it is that the ‘Whopper’ nickname ties back to where her parents met. She explained that the Caesarean was necessary because of concerns about Eva’s size and praised Eva as 'absolutely gorgeous.' Danica and Sam met two years ago while working at Burger King.

article_content: At White Sands National Park in New Mexico, scientists discovered human footprints alongside those of mammoths and ancient sloths, estimating them to be between 20,000 and 23,000 years old. This challenges the previous belief that humans first came to the Americas roughly 14,000 years ago. While this possibility has excited archaeologists, there has also been some skepticism, especially concerning the dating techniques used. Initially, researchers dated seeds from aquatic plants found with the footprints using radiocarbon dating. Critics noted that these plants could have absorbed much older carbon or may have originated from older sediments, which could affect the accuracy of the dating. To address these concerns, Kathleen Springer, Jeff Pigati, and their colleagues conducted further analyses. Their recent study, published in Science, involved radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, which is less susceptible to contamination, and also applied optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) to determine when the surrounding sediment was last exposed to sunlight. Both newer methods support the conclusion that the footprints date back approximately 21,000 to 23,000 years. Although some archaeologists consider this strong evidence for an earlier human presence in the Americas, others, such as Loren Davis of Oregon State University, remain cautious and suggest more evidence is needed before fully accepting these findings.

article_content: Finding it hard to be productive when motivation is low is a common challenge, especially if you have important work that can't wait. Andrew Cohen, founder and CEO of Brainscape, shares some practical strategies for handling these moments.  Rather than succumbing to distractions or just appearing to work, Cohen uses these techniques when his productivity drops:  1. Tackle Simple Tasks During Low-Energy Periods: When energy is low, he addresses routine, administrative tasks that don't require much thought. This maintains progress and reserves his best mental capacity for more demanding work when he feels refreshed.  2. Use Light Exercise to Boost Energy: Even a brief period of gentle exercise can raise alertness and support better decision-making. A 2019 study indicated that some morning movement improved learning and attention. Cohen notes that it doesn't have to be strenuous—just a bit of activity can revive your mind.  3. Optimize Caffeine Intake: Cohen advises not to consume coffee right after waking up, since your body is naturally producing cortisol. Instead, it's best to have caffeine 30–60 minutes after getting up, and to take it in small, regular amounts (about 25 mg an hour) instead of large servings. This delivers steady alertness without the crash.  Cohen emphasizes that while these approaches help with occasional sluggishness, real productivity comes from a foundation of healthy habits—good sleep, nutrition, and exercise. Addressing lifestyle factors can resolve ongoing fatigue, rather than just offering a temporary fix.

article_content: With growing concerns about antibiotic resistance and public health, scientists are searching for alternatives to antibiotics in chicken feed. In a recent article published in Animal Nutrition, Canadian researchers examined a typical chicken feed ingredient—wheat—and investigated how adding a purified enzyme, beta-glucanase, might improve chicken health and growth. The study's main goal was to see whether supplementing wheat-based chicken feed with purified beta-glucanase could enhance beta-glucan breakdown and benefit chicken performance. The team hypothesized that beta-glucanase would help break down beta-glucan, a component in wheat, leading to better nutrient absorption, healthier gut bacteria, and improved overall chicken well-being. According to lead author Namalika Karunaratne, the results were noteworthy: beta-glucanase not only broke down beta-glucan effectively but also improved chicken growth and health. Furthermore, when compared to antibiotics traditionally used in chicken feed, beta-glucanase offered some unique advantages. Although antibiotics could also break down beta-glucan, beta-glucanase was more effective, particularly during a chicken's early growth stages. Interestingly, beta-glucanase was found to reduce short-chain fatty acids—byproducts of carbohydrate fermentation in the chicken's digestive system—which might seem unexpected. However, this did not negatively affect the chickens' performance. In fact, chickens fed with beta-glucanase showed better weight gain and feed efficiency. In conclusion, the researchers found that adding purified beta-glucanase to chicken feed not only boosted performance but also reduced the need for antibiotics and other medications. Karunaratne commented, 'This is a significant advancement in maintaining chicken health and improving food safety. It's a positive outcome for both chickens and poultry caretakers.'

article_content: Mumbai: Sahar police have arrested 27-year-old Kabir Saif Rizavi, a passenger from Bengaluru, for smoking on board an Oman Air flight traveling from Muscat to Mumbai. Despite repeated warnings, Rizavi was caught by cabin crew as he smoked in the aircraft lavatory, thereby endangering the safety of other passengers. Upon investigation, the police confiscated a lighter, a packet of cigarettes, and a damaged oxygen kit. Rizavi later confessed to the act and was placed under arrest. This incident marks the 13th case of unruly flyer arrest in 2023. Rizavi faces charges under Indian Penal Code section 336 (endangering life) and the Aircraft Rule of 1937. In a similar incident earlier in July, another passenger was arrested for smoking on a Jeddah-Mumbai flight.

Google has been granted a patent for a groundbreaking technology capable of revolutionizing online search by providing the search engine with enhanced knowledge of the world. While humans can effortlessly recognize and categorize objects thanks to our brains and eyes, computers have historically found this task challenging. Google's latest patent, focused on 'automatic large-scale video object recognition,' aims to change that.

This technology can analyze videos—including the thousands of hours uploaded to YouTube daily—and automatically identify, tag, and categorize objects, landmarks, and their contexts based on attributes such as color, movement, and distinctive features. For instance, someone might upload a video taken outside Big Ben in London, and Google's system could tag it with 'Big Ben' and 'London' without any manual input.

If integrated into smartphones and wearable devices in the future, this technology could transform internet usage. However, it has sparked privacy concerns. Civil liberty groups warn that it could give Google access to vast amounts of personal data about users' private lives. Google Street View already gathers substantial global imagery, and this technology would deepen Google's understanding of that visual data.

Within YouTube, the world’s largest video-sharing platform, combined with technologies like Google Goggles and the widespread use of Android devices, Google’s ability to recognize and interpret visuals could soon extend around the globe. The company plans to build an 'object name repository' containing 50,000 objects, which range from well-known landmarks to specific identifiers like a cat’s ears—useful given the abundance of cat videos online.

Google notes that traditional systems rely on manual labeling of content, which is costly and not scalable for massive datasets. By automating object recognition, Google's technology aims to efficiently manage and categorize millions of images and videos.

Nick Pickles, director of privacy and civil liberties group Big Brother Watch, raised concerns, stating, 'Yet again this looks like users losing control of what happens to their data. If information about your location is instantly added to photos, not only does it reveal where you are, but it also allows Google to link your identity with more information, such as your whereabouts and personal activities. This kind of service should be opt-in, and Google should clearly obtain consent before collecting such data.'

கூகுள் உலக அறிவைப் பெருக்கக்கூடிய முன்னேற்றமான தொழில்நுட்பத்திற்கு புதிய காப்புரிமை பெற்றுள்ளது, இது ஆன்லைன் தேடல் முறையை முற்றிலும் மாற்றக்கூடியதாக இருக்கிறது. மனிதர்கள் தங்கள் கண்களும் மூளையும் பயன்படுத்தி பொருட்களை அடையாளம் கண்டறிவதில் கைதேர்ந்தவர்கள், ஆனால் கணினிகள் மறுபுறம் சிரமப்படுகின்றன. கூகுளின் புதிய 'தானாக இயங்கும் பெரிய அளவிலான வீடியோ பொருள் அறிதல்' என்ற காப்புரிமை, இந்த சவால்களை தாண்ட முயல்கிறது.

இந்த தொழில்நுட்பம், யூடியூப் போன்ற தளங்களில் தினமும் பதிவேறும் ஆயிரக்கணக்கான மணி நேர வீடியோக்களை பகுப்பாய்வு செய்து, நிறம், இயக்கம், மாற்றம் போன்ற அம்சங்களின் அடிப்படையில் பொருட்கள், முக்கிய இடங்கள் மற்றும் சூழ்நிலைகளை தானாக அடையாளம் கொண்டு குறிச்சொற்களாக்கும். உதாரணமாக, லண்டனில் உள்ள பிக் பெனின் அருகில் எடுக்கப்பட்ட வீடியோவை ஒருவர் கூகுளில் பதிவேற்றினால், கூடுதல் தகவல் இல்லாமலேயே அந்த வீடியோவுக்கு 'பிக் பென்', 'லண்டன்' முதலிய குறிச்சொற்களை வழங்கும்.

இது எதிர்காலத்தில் ஸ்மார்ட்போன்கள் மற்றும் அணிகலன் சாதனங்களில் ஒருங்கிணைக்கப்பட்டால், இணைய பயன்பாட்டில் புதிய மாற்றங்களை ஏற்படுத்தும். அது மட்டுமின்றி, தனியுரிமை குறித்து பலரும் கவலை தெரிவிக்கின்றனர். குடிமை உரிமை அமைப்புகள், இந்த தொழில்நுட்பம் கூகுளுக்கு பயனாளர்களின் தனிப்பட்ட தகவல்களை அதிகமாகக் கண்டறிய வாய்ப்பளிக்கிறது என்று எச்சரிக்கின்றன. கூகுள் ஸ்ட்ரீட் வியூ மூலம் ஏற்கனவே உலகம் முழுவதும் புகைப்படங்கள் சேகரிக்கப்படுகின்றன, இத்துடன் அந்த தகவலை இத்தொழில்நுட்பம் மேலும் ஆழமாக பகுப்பாய்வு செய்யும்.

யூடியூப், கூகுள் கோக்கிள்ஸ், உலகம் முழுதும் பரவியுள்ள ஆன்ட்ராய்டு சாதனங்களை இணைத்துப் பார்த்தால், கூகுள் விரைவில் உலகுக்கு முழு பார்வையைக் கொண்டதாக மாறும். நிறுவனம் 50,000 பொருட்கள் அடங்கிய 'பொருள் பெயர் தொகுதி' ஒன்றை உருவாக்கும் திட்டம் போட்டுள்ளது. இதில், புகழ்பெற்ற இடங்கள் முதல் பூனைக்கான காது போன்ற சிறப்பு அடையாளங்கள் வரை இடம்பெறும். இணையத்தில் பூனை வீடியோக்கள் அதிகம் உள்ளதை இது எடுத்துக்காட்டுகிறது.

முன்னர், கூடுதல் மனித உழைப்பில் கையங்கும் முறைகள் அதிக செலவிலும் நேரமும் எடுத்துக்கொள்ளும். இதில், தானாக அடையாளம் காணும் தொழில்நுட்பம் மூலம் கூகுள் கோடிக்கணக்கான படங்கள்-வீடியோக்களை எளிதாக வகைப்படுத்த முடியும்.

'பிக் பிரதர் வாட்ச்' என்ற அமைப்பின் இயக்குநர் நிக் பிக்கில்ஸ் கூறுகிறார்: 'இதுவும் பயனாளர்கள் தங்கள் தரவு மீதான கட்டுப்பாட்டை இழக்கும் நிலைக்கு வழிவகுக்கிறது. உங்கள் புகைப்படத்தில் இடம் குறித்த தகவல் உடனடியாக சேர்க்கப்படும் என்று இருந்தால், அது நீங்கள் எங்கே இருக்கிறீர்கள் என்பதையும், உங்கள் அடையாளத்துடன் கூடுதல் தகவல்களையும் கூகுள் இணைக்க முடியும். இத்தகைய சேவை விருப்பத்திற்கு ஏற்ப (opt-in) மட்டுமே செய்யப்பட வேண்டும். மக்கள் தெளிவாக ஒப்புதல் அளிக்காமல் கூகுள் இந்த வகை தரவை சேகரிக்கக்கூடாது.'

Sibling rivalry is not exclusive to humans, as evident in a recent encounter among three fox cubs in Germany. While exploring with their siblings, one cub discovered a hidden stash of food, prompting a lively skirmish as each tried to claim the largest share. British photographer Duncan Usher, 59, discreetly captured the five-minute tussle from beneath a camouflage net, documenting the competitive nature of the young foxes.

Red foxes belong to the canidae family, which also includes dogs and wolves. However, unlike their canine relatives, foxes are not pack animals and typically hunt alone or live in small family groups. Foxes are omnivorous, feeding on both meat and vegetation, preying on small mammals, rodents, amphibians, as well as enjoying berries, fruit, and eggs. They often rely on scavenged food, but are also skilled hunters, perfecting their pouncing technique from a young age.

Once the spirited contest concluded, the three cubs enjoyed their meal together, with none suffering any serious injuries.

article_content: Michael Skakel, a relative of the Kennedy family who was convicted for the 1975 murder of his 15-year-old neighbor, was released on bail from a Connecticut courthouse on Thursday. Judge Gary White set Skakel's bail at $1.2 million after his 2002 conviction for the murder of Martha Moxley was vacated last month. This decision followed a ruling that Skakel did not have adequate legal representation at his original trial. After posting bail, Skakel left the courthouse with his attorneys, smiling slightly but not speaking to reporters. His attorney, Hubert Santos, described two tragedies: the murder of Martha Moxley and, as he referred to it, Skakel's 2002 conviction for a crime he maintains he did not commit. Santos expressed hope that Skakel's release would help correct what the family considers a miscarriage of justice. Judge White imposed several bail conditions: Skakel is forbidden to leave Connecticut without court permission; he must wear a GPS tracking device, avoid contact with the victim's family, and regularly report to a bail commissioner. Skakel, now 53 and the nephew of Robert and Ethel Kennedy, has spent over a decade in prison for Moxley's murder. After bail was announced, about two dozen Skakel relatives applauded, and Skakel acknowledged them by placing his hand on his heart and smiling. In a statement, the Skakel family called the court's decision a 'first step in correcting a terrible wrong,' expressing hope for Michael Skakel's eventual vindication and gratitude for the support received during his imprisonment. Outside the courthouse, Martha Moxley's mother, Dorthy Moxley, expressed disappointment at the release, stating it was a difficult experience but adding she did not consider Skakel a significant threat. She encouraged parents to take responsibility for their children's actions. Earlier, Prosecutor John Smriga argued that the bail amount was insufficient, considering the crime's severity and Skakel's mental health history. The defense, meanwhile, cited Skakel's record for appearing in court, his reputation, and his community involvement to argue he is not a flight risk. Last month, Appellate Court Judge Thomas Bishop overturned Skakel's conviction, ruling his defense counsel was constitutionally deficient at the original trial. Martha Moxley was found bludgeoned and stabbed to death in 1975 in Greenwich, Connecticut. Skakel has consistently maintained his innocence.

The opening match of the 2023 ICC Cricket World Cup will see the 2019 finalists, England and New Zealand, face off at the world’s largest cricket stadium. The game will take place at Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, India, on Thursday, October 5 at 2pm (08:30 GMT).

Both teams have maintained the core of their 2019 squads. For England, Jos Buttler has stepped up as captain, succeeding World Cup-winning skipper Eoin Morgan. Meanwhile, New Zealand will be led by Tom Latham as stand-in captain, with Kane Williamson sidelined due to a knee injury.

Both sides are dealing with injury concerns. New Zealand will miss not only Williamson but also veteran fast bowler Tim Southee, who is recovering from thumb surgery. England may be without all-rounder Ben Stokes, with Buttler cautious about risking him at the start of a long tournament.

England and New Zealand have a closely contested history in ODIs, with England narrowly ahead: 45 wins to New Zealand’s 44, with four matches ending without a result and two ending in ties. Their 2019 World Cup final was settled by a boundary count tiebreaker after a dramatic tie.

Recent performances suggest both teams are in form. England enters the tournament following two series wins, including one over New Zealand. New Zealand begins with confidence after a series win against Bangladesh.

Predicted lineups are as follows:

England: Jos Buttler (captain, wicketkeeper), Jonny Bairstow, Dawid Malan, Joe Root, Harry Brook, Liam Livingstone, Moeen Ali, Sam Curran, Chris Woakes, Adil Rashid, Reece Topley.

New Zealand: Devon Conway, Will Young, Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (captain, wicketkeeper), Rachin Ravindra, Matt Henry, Mitchell Santner, Lockie Ferguson, Ish Sodhi, Trent Boult.

article_content: Despite an overall decline in foreign direct investment (FDI) into India, experts remain optimistic due to rising interest in greenfield investments, especially as China experiences its first-ever FDI deficit. The United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) recently highlighted India's positive progress in a presentation to the finance ministry, according to a report by Economic Times. India ranks among the top three countries in greenfield FDI announcements, reflecting potential for global supply chain diversification. A senior finance ministry official expects these trends to support increased investment flows by 2024. Conversely, China recently reported its first quarterly FDI deficit during the July-September period, coinciding with a worldwide initiative to reduce reliance on Chinese-led supply chains. Policymakers emphasize that India may not be the sole alternative as FDI shifts from China, but signs suggest India's growing integration into global supply chains. Bibek Debroy, Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, said India's recent participation in global supply chains has been driven by efforts to create an FDI-friendly business environment and reduce post-COVID reliance on China. Former Chief Economic Adviser KV Subramanian sees India’s opportunity as global investors seek alternatives due to China's economic and demographic challenges. He stressed the need for continued structural reforms to capitalize on this window of opportunity, emphasizing that it may not last indefinitely. Subramanian pointed out that China's negative FDI reflects deeper structural and demographic challenges. While China previously benefited from a positive demographic dividend fueling high growth since the 1980s, it now faces an aging population and mounting financial sector difficulties, including significant bad loans and real estate sector issues characterized by oversupply and overinvestment. In contrast, India has implemented proactive measures to attract new investment, such as reducing the corporate tax rate for new manufacturing units to 15% and introducing production-linked incentive (PLI) schemes across multiple sectors. Despite these efforts, India's FDI equity inflows fell by 34% to $10.9 billion in the June quarter, which economists attribute to high interest rates and global economic uncertainty impacting global mergers and acquisitions. Nonetheless, economists maintain a positive medium-term outlook for India, with Rahul Bajoria, Managing Director at Barclays, noting that while FDI intentions are high, investment levels are being affected by elevated interest rates both in India and globally.
translated_content: இந்தியாவிற்கு வெளிநாட்டு நேரடி முதலீடு (FDI) மொத்தம் குறைந்து வருகிறது என்றாலும், சீனாவில் முதல் முறையாக FDI குறைபாடு ஏற்பட்டுள்ள நிலையில் கிரீன்பீல்ட் முதலீடுகளுக்கு அதிகம் ஆர்வம் இருப்பதால் நிபுணர்கள் நம்பிக்கையுடன் உள்ளனர். ஐநா வர்த்தக மற்றும் மேம்பாட்டு மாநாடு (UNCTAD), இந்தியாவின் முன்னேற்றங்களை சமீபத்தில் நிதியமைச்சகத்துடன் பகிர்ந்து கொண்டதாக ஈக்கனாமிக் டைம்ஸ் தெரிவித்துள்ளது. கிரீன்பீல்ட் FDI அறிவிப்புகளில் இந்தியா உலகளவில் முதல் மூன்று இடங்களில் உள்ளது; இது உலக சப்ளை சளையில் இனிவரும் வகைமாற்றத்திற்கு வாய்ப்பு அளிக்கிறது. 2024க்குள் முதலீடு அதிகரிக்கும் என்று நிதியமைச்சக ஒரு மூத்த அதிகாரி எதிர்பார்க்கிறார். இதற்கு எதிராக, சீனா கடந்த ஜூலை-செப்டம்பர் காலாண்டில் தனது முதலாவது காலாண்டு FDI பற்றாக்குறையை பதிவு செய்துள்ளது; இது சீனாவை மையமாக கொண்டுள்ள சப்ளை சளையில் இருந்து உலகம் விலகும் முயற்ச்சிகளுடன் ஏற்படுகிறது. இந்தியா மட்டும் மாற்றாக இருக்கப்போவதாக இல்லை என்றாலும், இந்தியா உலக சப்ளை சளையில் அதிகமாக ஒருங்கிணைகின்றது என்று கொள்கையியலாளர்கள் கூறுகின்றனர். பிரதமரின் பொருளாதார ஆலோசனை குழு தலைவர் பிபேக் டெப்ராய், இந்தியா சமீபத்தில் உலக சப்ளை சளையில் பங்குபெற்று வருவதற்குக் காரணம், FDIக்கு ஏற்ற வணிக சூழல் உருவாக்கும் முயற்சியும், கோவிட்குப் பின்னர் சீனாவைச் சார்ந்ததை குறைக்கும் திட்டங்களும் தான் என கூறினார். முன்னாள் முதன்மை பொருளாதார ஆலோசகர் கே.வி. சுப்ரமணியன், சீனாவின் பொருளாதார மற்றும் மக்கள் தொகை சவால்களால் முதலீட்டாளர்கள் மாற்று நாடுகளை நாடும் சூழலில் இந்தியாவுக்குப் பெரும் வாய்ப்பு உள்ளது என்று நினைக்கிறார். இந்த வாய்ப்பை பயனடைய தொடர்ச்சியாக கட்டமைப்பு சீர்திருத்தங்கள் செய்ய வேண்டும் என்றும், இந்த வாய்ப்பு நிரந்தரமில்லை என்றும் அவர் எச்சரித்தார். சுப்ரமணியன் சுட்டிக்காட்டியது: சீனாவின் FDI குறைபாடு அதன் ஆழ்ந்த கட்டமைப்பு மற்றும் ஜனகரீதியான சவால்களை பிரதிபலிக்கிறது. 1980களில் இருந்து சீனாவுக்கு மக்கள் தொகை பலன் இருந்தாலும், தற்போது வயதான மக்கள் மற்றும் நிதி துறையில் கடன் சுமை, ரியல் எஸ்டேட்டில் அதிக ஒதுக்கீடு, அதிக வீடுகள் போன்ற சிரமங்களை சந்திக்கிறது. இந்தியா இதற்கு மாறாக, புதிய முதலீடுகள் வரக்காரணமாக பல முனைப்புகளும் மேற்கொண்டும் வருகிறது; புதிய உற்பத்தி நிறுவனங்களுக்கு கார்ப்பரேட் வரியை 15% ஆக குறைத்து, பல துறைகளில் PLI திட்டங்களை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இதை அடுத்து, ஜூன் காலாண்டில் இந்தியாவின் FDI ஈக்விட்டி வரவு 34% குறைந்து $10.9 பில்லியனாக உள்ளது. இதற்கு உயர் வட்டி விகிதம் மற்றும் உலகளாவிய பொருளாதார மாறுபாடுகள் காரணம் என பொருளாதார நிபுணர்கள் தெரிவிக்கின்றனர். இருப்பினும், ராகுல் பஜோரியா (பார்க்ளேஸ்) என்னும் பொருளாதார நிபுணர் கூறுவது: FDI குறித்து ஆர்வம் அதிகமாக இருந்தாலும், நாட்டிலும் உலகிலும் உயர் வட்டி விகிதம் முதலீட்டை பாதிக்கிறது.

article_content: The spade-toothed beaked whale, regarded as the world's rarest whale and among the rarest mammals, has long been shrouded in mystery. Scientists had never seen a living specimen and possessed only a handful of skeletal remains to prove its existence. That changed in late 2010, when two dead whales washed ashore on Opape Beach in New Zealand. At first, researchers were unaware of the significance of their find. Anton van Helden, collection manager of marine mammals at the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa and co-author of a recent paper in 'Current Biology,' described the moment as feeling like 'finding the holy grail.' Rochelle Constantine, a co-author from the University of Auckland, along with colleague Kirsten Thompson, analyzed tissue samples from the whales. 'When we saw the results, we were stunned,' said Constantine. DNA analysis confirmed the whales were spade-toothed beaked whales, a species known previously from just three partial specimens (two found in New Zealand in 1872 and the 1950s, and a third from Robinson Crusoe Island off Chile in 1986). The spade-toothed beaked whale resembles a large, black, white, and gray dolphin with a long, pointed snout. Adults can grow to about 17 feet in length, and males bear prominent exposed teeth as their name suggests. The two whales—a female and a juvenile male—were initially misidentified as Gray's beaked whales and buried near their discovery site. In early 2012, scientists recovered the remains, completing the only full specimen in existence. Unfortunately, the head of the adult female had been lost to beach erosion. The discovery is a major breakthrough for cetacean research. Professor Ewan Fordyce of the University of Otago, who studies whale evolution and was not involved in the study, remarked that 'now we have an idea of the appearance and size of the species.' However, much about the spade-toothed beaked whale remains unknown, including its habits and lifestyle, as no live specimen has been observed. Researchers believe, based on similar species, that these whales are elusive, spend little time at the surface, dive to great depths (up to 2,000 meters), and likely feed on squid. 'This is the whale species we know least about in the world,' Constantine said. 'For the first time, we finally have a clearer picture of what it looks like.'
translated_content: உலகிலேயே மிகவும் அபூர்வமான திமிங்கல்களில் ஒன்றாக கருதப்படும் ஸ்பேடு-டூத் பீக்டு திமிங்கல் இதுவரை உயிருடன் காணப்படாதது. ஆராய்ச்சியாளர்கள் இதன் இருப்பை உறுதிப்படுத்துவதற்கான சில எலும்புகள் மட்டும் வைத்திருந்தனர். 2010 ஆம் ஆண்டு இறுதியில், நியூசிலாந்தின் ஓபாப் கடற்கரையில் இரண்டு இறந்த திமிங்கல்களின் உடல்கள் கரை ஒதுங்கின. இதில் ஆராய்ச்சியாளர்கள் இந்த கண்டுபிடிப்பின் முக்கியத்துவத்தைத் தெரியாமலிருந்தனர். மியூசியம் ஆஃப் நியூசிலாந்து டெ பப்பா தொங்கரேவாவின் கடல் உயிரின சேகரிப்பு மேலாளர் மற்றும் 'கரண்ட் பயோலஜி' இதழில் தன் ஆய்வுக்கட்டுரையை வெளியிட்ட ஆன்டன் வான் ஹெல்டன், இதை 'பவளசாவி கண்டுபிடித்தது' போன்ற உணர்ச்சியாக விவரிக்கிறார். ஆக்லாந்து பல்கலைக்கழகத்தைச் சேர்ந்த ரொசெல் கான்ஸ்டன்டைன் மற்றும் அவரது சக ஆய்வாளர் கிற்ஸ்டன் தாம்சன், உறுப்பு மாதிரிகளைக் கற்றாயில் முற்றும் அதிர்ச்சியடைந்தனர். DNA பரிசோதனை மூலம் இது ஸ்பேடு-டூத் பீக்டு திமிங்கல்போன்றது என உறுதி செய்யப்பட்டது. இதற்கு முன்பு 1872ம் ஆண்டு, 1950களில் நியூசிலாந்திலும், 1986-ல் சிலியின் Robinson Crusoe தீவில் முன்பே மூன்று பகுதி எலும்புகள் மட்டுமே இருந்தன. இவை கருப்பு, வெள்ளை மற்றும் சாம்பல் நிறத்தில் நீண்ட கூர்மையான மூக்குடன் காணப்படும் பெரிய டால்பினைப் போல் இருக்கும். வயது வந்த வரை 17 அடி உயரம் வரை வளரலாம், ஆண்களுக்கு வெளியே தெரியும் பெரிய பற்கள் காணப்படும். இந்த இரண்டு திமிங்கல்கள்—ஒரு பெண் மற்றும் ஒரு இளம் ஆண்—தவறாக கிரேஸ் பீக்டு திமிங்கல் என அடையாளம் காணப்பட்டு, அவை கிடைத்த இடத்தில் புதைக்கப்பட்டன. 2012-இல் விஞ்ஞானிகள் மீண்டும் அவற்றை மீட்டனர், உலகில் உள்ள ஒரே முழுமையான மாதிரியைப் பெற்றனர். ஆனால் பெரிய பெண் திமிங்கலின் தலை கடற்கரை அழைப்பு காரணமாக இல்லை. இந்த கண்டுபிடிப்பு தேந்துகளைக் குறித்த ஆராய்ச்சியில் பெரிய முன்னேற்றமாகும். ஒட்டாகோ பல்கலைக்கழக பேராசிரியர் ஈவன் போர்டைஸ், 'இனத்தின் தோற்றத்தையும் அளவையும் தற்போது தெரிந்துகொள்ள முடிகிறது' என்று தெரிவித்துள்ளார். இன்னும் இவை பற்றிய வாழ்க்கை முறையோ பழக்கங்களோ தெரியவில்லை, உயிருடன் காணப்படாத இனமானதால். மற்ற பீக்டு திமிங்கல்களைப் போல இவை கடலில் ஆழமாகத்தான் இருந்தும், மேற்பரப்பில் மிகக் குறைந்த நேரம் செலவழிக்கும் என்பதை ஆய்வாளர்கள் கருதி, 2,000 மீட்டர் ஆழத்திற்கு மூழ்கும். இவை மிக அதிகமான ஆழத்தில் மிதவும், ஸ்குவிட் போன்றவற்றை உணவாகக் கொள்வதாக கருதப்படுகிறது. 'இது உலகத்தில் நாம் மிகக் குறைவாக அறிந்த திமிங்கல் இனமாகும்,' என கான்ஸ்டன்டைன் கூறினார். 'முதல்முறையாக, இதன் தோற்றம் பற்றி தெளிவு கிடைத்துள்ளது.'

An inquest has revealed that Families SA considered the parenting skills of Chloe Valentine’s teenage mother, who used drugs, as 'good enough' despite clear evidence of neglect. Chloe was just four years old when she died from severe head injuries—39 injuries in total—in January 2012, after being forced to ride a motorbike and crashing repeatedly over a three-day period in her Adelaide backyard. The inquest heard that Chloe’s short life was marked by serious neglect and poor living conditions, yet she was never removed from her mother, Ashlee Polkinghorne’s, care.

On Wednesday, social worker Leanne Stewart testified that she believed Chloe, then only 18 months old, was receiving 'good enough' care in early 2009, even though there was substantial evidence of neglect and multiple child abuse notifications. Chloe’s teenage mother allowed her to be supervised by other teenagers for long periods, despite warnings from Ms Stewart that this was inappropriate. Family members, including Polkinghorne’s father, raised concerns about Chloe’s safety and expressed willingness to care for her if authorities decided to intervene.

Ms Stewart said she thought some complaints might have been exaggerated or made maliciously, due to ongoing family conflict. The inquest also heard that social workers were aware of Polkinghorne’s drug use and ongoing neglect from when Chloe was just 18 months old. Polkinghorne, herself still a teenager, struggled to keep a clean home and meet basic parenting responsibilities, Stewart added. Naomi Kereru, assisting the coroner, questioned Stewart’s justification for Polkinghorne’s actions, reminding her that her primary responsibility was to protect Chloe.

Ultimately, both Ashlee Polkinghorne, now 22, and her partner Benjamin McPartland, 28, were jailed for manslaughter by criminal neglect over Chloe’s death. The inquest into the tragic case is ongoing.

article_content: Wild orcas were gently rubbing their bellies on smooth stones in the shallow waters off Vancouver Island, Canada, captured in remarkable amateur footage by Chris Wilton, a builder working nearby. Just a few feet away, Wilton filmed a pod of orcas—also known as killer whales—at Bates Beach in Courtenay, British Columbia. 'I was at work putting a new roof on a home when we heard what sounded like orcas around the corner,' Chris said. 'We ran out front to see and were amazed by what was happening.' An adult and a juvenile orca were seen rubbing their bellies on the smooth stones in shallow water. Chris Wilton captured this footage of the orca pod at Bates Beach. 'There were four or five orcas swimming in and out of the beach, coming right up to shore within six feet of us.' Chris noted that while the posted video runs four minutes and twenty seconds, the actual display lasted about an hour. 'It was one of the most amazing things I have ever seen,' he added. The Orca Network shared his video on Facebook, including a quote from marine blogger Jackie Hildering (The Marine Detective): 'Absolutely remarkable footage of northern resident orcas displaying their culturally unique behavior of rubbing themselves on beaches like this.' Wilton confirmed that the display lasted about an hour and repeated how incredible the experience was. Jackie Hildering said this behavior is unique to northern resident orcas. She mentioned that, along with whale researchers Janie Wray and Christie McMillan, they believed these whales were from the A42 matriline, with the distinctive large male being A66, born in 1996. Observers watched in amazement, exclaiming, 'This is crazy,' 'Powerful,' and 'Holy moly.' Another person joked, 'I think they're trying to splash us.' The orcas swam away from shore before returning repeatedly to rub their undersides on the stones. Although this belly-rubbing behavior is famous among northern resident orcas, scientists aren’t entirely sure why they do it. One onlooker suggested, 'It probably feels like a nice massage.'

article_content: Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate Peter Obi has stated that Nigeria should not be experiencing poverty, blaming the country's current situation on poor planning and bad leadership. Obi emphasized the need to stop the embezzlement of public funds. Obi made these remarks at a colloquium and Hall of Fame event in honor of Labour Party National Chairman Julius Abure, held in Benin City and organized by the Edo Policy Round Table in conjunction with Mudiame University, Irrua, Edo State. In his goodwill message, Obi expressed that Nigeria is blessed with abundant natural resources and favorable conditions. He reiterated that poor planning and lack of effective leadership are the root causes of Nigeria’s problems. Obi praised Abure’s commitment to free and fair party primaries, noting that he values recognizing positive contributions in leadership. He admitted that while everyone has flaws, integrity matters and he strives not to knowingly do wrong. Drawing from his experience in both public and private sectors, Obi stated that Nigeria’s challenges stem from politicians failing to implement plans and often acting contrary to campaign promises once in office. He said: 'There is nothing wrong with Nigeria. The country has some of the best land, climate, resources, and people. If Nigeria is improved, so will Edo State. Those who have left will return when Edo prospers. However, what Nigeria lacks is good leadership.' Obi compared Nigeria's size to the three biggest economies in Europe—Germany, Britain, and France—saying their combined land mass is only about 20% larger than Nigeria's. He asserted that Nigeria’s GDP should be higher, but waste, overconsumption, and underproduction due to poor leadership are the main issues. Transforming Nigeria’s economy from consumption-based to production-focused would create jobs and reduce poverty. Obi urged Nigerians to stop people from stealing and wasting public funds, emphasizing collective responsibility and the importance of not celebrating such individuals. He called for unity and effort in rebuilding Nigeria to create a better future for coming generations, warning that otherwise, the country risks passing on further hardship. Guest speaker Dr. Yunusa Tanko noted Nigeria, at 63 years since independence, still seeks a new political order. He stated that ethnic, religious, and political factors have impeded democratic rule and national development. Tanko commended Abure for leading Labour Party to success, building on foundations from past leaders. In his address, Abure said the September 2, 2024 Edo governorship election offers citizens a chance to choose a selfless 'Shepherd Governor'—a leader ready to unite people, take risks, make sacrifices, and promote development. He asserted this governor should focus on wealth creation, poverty eradication, security, education, health, and infrastructure. Earlier, Prof. S. E. Eromosele of Mudiame University highlighted the severe poverty and hardship in Edo State. He called for people-oriented policies and greater public involvement in decision-making.

article_content: Emma Dalton, a 25-year-old from Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, made history by being the first person to complete the Wonder Cafe’s giant breakfast challenge. Shown on ITV's This Morning, Dalton ate a massive fry-up including four slices of toast, four eggs, six sausages, six pieces of bacon, six hash browns, four portions of black pudding, plum tomatoes, mushrooms, and baked beans. She finished the meal in just 21 minutes — less than half the 45-minute time limit. By completing the challenge, Dalton got her meal for free; those who fail must pay £20. The dish, containing about 5,000 calories, is known as one of the world’s largest fried breakfasts. Dalton started competitive eating about 13 weeks ago after taking on a challenge in Orlando, Florida. Since then, she has participated in numerous eating contests, such as finishing a three-pound burger and cake in Orlando, a 48-ounce burger with eight slices each of cheese and bacon in Southampton, an eight-pound burrito in Walsall, and an 80-ounce steak plus a three-foot-long hotdog. Although Dalton enjoys these competitions, she admits to gaining weight since starting out and describes experiencing ‘meat sweats’ and feeling hyper after big meals. She even craved chocolate after her huge breakfast challenge, saying the savory meal made her want something sweet. The Wonder Cafe also hosts the Wonder Burger Challenge, which requires eating a 36-ounce Aberdeen Angus beef burger topped with salad, onion rings, cheese, and bacon, along with coleslaw and chips, all within 30 minutes. Dalton says she doesn't feel unwell after the contests but sometimes finds it hard to sleep because of the amount of food consumed. Her achievement has drawn attention, solidifying her reputation in the competitive eating scene.

article_content:
It's tea time for a Mongolian family in their traditional ger, also known as a yurt. The close quarters of ger living help bring families together. If you're feeling disconnected from others, you might take a cue from Mongolians. According to a new Gallup report, 'The Global State of Social Connections', people in 142 countries were asked to evaluate their social connectedness—how emotionally close they feel to others, including family, friends, neighbors, coworkers, group members, and even strangers. Globally, seven out of ten people reported feeling 'very' or 'fairly' connected. But Mongolians were the most connected of all; 95% reported strong feelings of social connection, ranking above countries like Kosovo, Taiwan, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Both Mongolian men (95%) and women (94%) reported high social connection.

Curious about these results, the reporter reached out to Mongolians, who were not surprised to top the list. Traditionally, Mongolians live in gers, round felt tents suited for a nomadic lifestyle. Gers have specific customs, such as the way people enter (women to the east, men to the west), where to sit, and the door's orientation (typically facing south for sunlight). Inside, there are no interior walls, and families—sometimes large—sleep together on the floor with sheep wool mattresses, sharing meals cooked over a single stove burning coal, wood, or cow dung, explains wildlife disease specialist Enkhtuvshin Shiilegdamba.

Even in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia's bustling capital, ger neighborhoods remain. Navigating these neighborhoods can be challenging, as there are no street names or grid system. Instead, people rely on each other for directions, reinforcing social dependence. In rural areas, every family member has a chore, and even siblings often live in neighboring gers. This lifestyle fosters deep family bonds, which extend to neighbors and the community.

This sense of connection continues in urban lifestyles. Many city dwellers return to their hometowns during the summer to spend time with extended family. A 2023 study in the journal 'Buildings' found that Mongolian spiritual beliefs are tied to the ger's unique form, affecting values and behaviors. The ger's circular, domed shape blends religion and daily life, and the study observed higher satisfaction among ger dwellers compared to those in urban housing, linked to Mongolian appreciation for nature and freedom.

Gers support a close connection to nature, which also fosters social ties, notes band manager Tuga Namgur. 'To survive as nomads, we rely on each other. Family is everything,' Namgur says. He managed his brother's band, The Hu, based on these strong bonds, even while living in Chicago.

Mongolians aren't surprised by their country's high connectedness. When leaving home, ger dwellers don't set alarms; instead, they leave their ger unlocked so travelers can seek shelter and food—since in Mongolia's harsh climate this can be lifesaving.

Ultimately, Mongolia's deep social bonds are shaped by tradition, environment, and necessity, offering valuable insight at a time when many around the world seek greater connectedness.

Reporter Katya Cengel writes for Smithsonian Magazine and The New York Times Magazine, among others. Her latest book is 'Straitjackets and Lunch Money.'

மொங்கோலிய குடும்பம் அவர்களது பாரம்பரிய யுர்டில் (ger) தேநீரை சுவைத்து மகிழ்கிறது. இந்த ஓரிட குடிசை வாழ்வில் குடும்ப உறுப்பினர்கள் அனைவரும் மிக நெருக்கமாக இருக்கின்றனர். நீங்கள் ஒருவேளை பிறரிடமிருந்து வெகு தொலைவில் இருப்பதை உணர்கிறீர்களானால், மொங்கோலியர்களிடம் இருந்து சில பாடங்களை கற்றுக்கொள்ளலாம்.

'த குளோபல் ஸ்டேட் ஆஃப் சோஷியல் கனெக்ஷன்ஸ்' எனும் புதிய கல்லப் அறிக்கையில், 142 நாடுகளில் உள்ளவர்கள் அவர்களது சமூக இணைப்பை — குடும்பம், நண்பர்கள், அண்டைவர்கள், வேலைத்திற்பேர் மற்றும் அறிமுகமற்றவர்களையும்கூட உள்ளடக்கியவர்கள் குறித்த அவர்களின் மனநிலை குறித்து மதிப்பிடப்பட்டது. உலகளவில், பத்தில் ஏழுபேர் "மிகவும்" அல்லது "மிதமான முறையில்" இணைந்திருந்தனர் என்று தெரிவித்துள்ளனர். ஆனால் மொங்கோலியர்கள் அனைவருக்கும் மேம்பட்டதாகச் சுட்டிக்காட்டப்படுகிறார்கள்: 95% பேர் தங்களது சமூக இணைப்பு மிக வலிமையானது என்று கூறியுள்ளனர்; கோசோவோ, தைவான் மற்றும் போஸ்னியா உள்ளிட்ட நாடுகளையும் முந்திக் கொண்டுள்ளனர். ஆண்கள் (95%) மற்றும் பெண்கள் (94%) இருவரும் சமூக இணைப்பை அதிக அளவில் உணர்கிறார்கள்.

இந்த முடிகள் பற்றிய தகவலை அறிந்து செய்தியாளர் மொங்கோலியர்களிடம் தொடர்பு கொண்டார்; அவர்கள் இப்படிப் பட்ட தனித்துவத்துக்கு ஆச்சரியம் அல்ல என்று தெரிவித்தனர். பாரம்பரியமாய்ப் பார்த்தால், மொங்கோலியர்கள் வட்டம் மற்றும் மிதமான கூரை கொண்டடையுடைய felt கொண்டு செய்யப்பட்ட யுர்ட்களில் வாழ்கின்றனர். இவர்களுடைய வாழ்வியல் குறித்து எங்கேத்துவ்ஷின் ஷிலெக்டம்பா, விலங்கு நோய் நிபுணர் கூறுகிறார்: இங்கு பெண்கள் கிழக்குப் பக்கம், ஆண்கள் மேற்குப் பக்கம் நுழைவார்கள், கதவு பொதுவாக தெற்குப் பக்கம் அமையும் (சூரிய ஒளிக்காக), சுவர்கள் இல்லை, குடும்பம் முழுவதும் தரையில் மேப்பில்களில் சேரத் தூங்குகிறார்கள்; ஒரே அடுப்பில் (கோல், மரம், மாட்டொந்தை) சமையல் செய்கிறார்கள்.

உலான் பாதர் நகரிலும் இத்தகைய யுர்ட் பகுதிகள் உள்ளன; அங்கு தெருவுப் பெயர்கள், வழி அமைப்புகள் இல்லாததால், ஒருவருக்கும் ஒருவரை நாடி வழிகாட்டல்தான் முக்கியம். கிராமங்களில் ஒவ்வொரு உறுப்பினருக்கும் தனித் தொழில்கள் உள்ளன; சகோதரர்கள் அருகில் உள்ள வாரியங்களில் வாழ்கின்றனர். இது குடும்பத்திலும், அண்டைவர்களுடனும் நெருக்கத்தை உருவாக்குகிறது.

இது நகரம் வாழ்விலும் தொடர்கிறது. அங்குள்ள மக்கள் பலர் கோடையில் தங்கள் ஊர்களுக்கு திரும்பி, குடும்பத்தோடு நேரம் செலவிடுவார்கள். 2023ஆம் ஆண்டு 'பில்டிங்ஸ்' என்ற இணைய இதழின் ஆய்வில், மொங்கோலிய ஆன்மீகப் பாராட்டும், யுர்டின் வடிவமும் சம்மந்தப்பட்டுள்ளதை, மேலும் வட்ட, தூண் கூரையுடன் ஆன்மீகம் மற்றும் வாழ்வு ஒன்றாகச் சேர்ந்திருப்பதை கூறுகிறது. அருகிலுள்ள காடும் வெளிகளும் வாழ்க்கையில் அதிகமாக பொருந்துகிறது. யுர்டில் வாழும் மக்களின் திருப்தி, நகர வீடுகளில் வாழும் மக்களின் திருப்திக்கே முன் இடம் பிடித்துள்ளது.

"நாம் மறுமலர்ச்சி வாழ்கையில் ஒருவரையொருவர் நம்பிக் கொண்டே இருக்க வேண்டும்; குடும்பம் எங்கள் கலாச்சாரம்" என்று இசை குழு மேலாளர் டுகா நம்கூர் கூறுகிறார். அவர் தனது சகோதரன் பங்கேற்றுள்ள 'தி ஹு' இசைக் குழுவை, தானாக சிகாகோவில் வாழ்ந்தாலும் அதன் குடும்ப பிணைவை வைத்து நிர்வகித்துள்ளார்.

மொங்கோலியற்று மனிதர்களுக்கு Gallup கண்டறிந்த இடம் ஆச்சரியமல்ல. வீட்டை விட்டு வெளியே சென்ற போதும், அவர்கள் யுர்ட்டினை பூட்டமாட்டார்கள்; அங்கே வந்த விருந்தினர்கள் திறந்து உணவு எடுத்துக்கொள்ளலாம், உறங்கலாம் — ஏனெனில் கடும் வெப்ப நிலையில் இது உயிர் காப்பாற்றும்.

இவர்கள் வாழ்வியலும், பாரம்பரியமும், சூழ்நிலை தேவைகளும், உருக்குலைந்து வந்த சமூக இணைப்பும், உலகம் மேலும் நெருக்கத்தை நாடும் இக்காலத்தில் முக்கியமான பாடமாக இருக்கிறது.

செய்தியாளர் கட்டியா செங்கேல் Smithsonian Magazine மற்றும் New York Times Magazine-க்கு எழுதுகிறார்; அவர் எழுதிய சமீபத்திய புத்தகம் 'Straitjackets and Lunch Money.'

article_content: David Moyes has been dismissed as Manchester United manager following a disappointing season. Ryan Giggs was appointed interim manager after Moyes' sacking on Tuesday. Moyes, 51, was seen in Miami, Florida, with his wife Pamela, taking some time away after his departure. This was his first public appearance since leaving United’s Carrington training ground. Moyes, whose six-year contract was cut short by the club’s American owners, the Glazer family, reportedly agreed to a financial settlement worth around £7 million. The League Managers Association confirmed that a settlement agreement is being finalized but did not provide further details. Reports indicated that some Manchester United players mocked Moyes during his last months at Old Trafford, although he did not address this in his statement. In his message, Moyes thanked the club’s staff and fans for their support and wished the club success for the future. Sir Alex Ferguson, who had chosen Moyes as his successor, said he was upset by the way Moyes’ departure was handled. Giggs managed United in their match against Norwich City, while speculation continues that Louis van Gaal is likely to become the next permanent manager, potentially bringing Patrick Kluivert as his assistant.

article_content: A new study reveals that climate change and land use changes are causing a significant decline in insect pollinators for important tropical crops. As these problems intensify, coffee and chocolate lovers may soon pay higher prices for their favorites. Researchers examined data from thousands of insect species and locations. They discovered that when temperatures rise beyond normal levels and habitats of flowering plants shrink, pollinator numbers drop by 61%. This decline is more pronounced for pollinators—such as bees, flies, and moths—than for other insects. "We're already seeing climate change having a strong impact on pollinators," said Tim Newbold, an ecologist at University College London and co-author of the study. About 35% of the world's food crops and three-quarters of flowering plants depend on insect and animal pollinators, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture. Published in Science Advances, the study highlights that pollinator losses are worst in tropical regions, which have been less studied until now. Countries most at risk include China, India, Indonesia, Brazil, the Philippines, and sub-Saharan Africa, particularly concerning crops like cocoa and mangoes. Falling numbers of pollinators threaten yields of key tropical crops, such as coffee and cocoa, which rely on bees and flies for reproduction. Previous research has linked declining insect populations to climate change and habitat loss. The new study shows that these factors together have an even stronger negative impact, affecting both the plants and their pollinators. "Climate change is affecting both coffee plants and the pollinators they need. That's worrying for coffee lovers," Newbold remarked. Lead author Joe Millard of the Natural History Museum in London pointed out that while coffee and chocolate won’t disappear, they could become more expensive. University of Delaware entomologist Douglas Tallamy, who was not part of the study, commended the data but cautioned that the reasons for greater impacts on tropical pollinators are still uncertain and require further study. Researchers noted that habitat loss is the primary driver of pollinator decline, but climate change, disease, parasites, and pesticides also play crucial roles. Pollinators may be especially vulnerable in hotter conditions, though the precise reasons are still debated. Some speculate that insects with hairy bodies and legs, which help carry pollen, might be more sensitive to heat, but this idea remains unproven.

"Pollinators மீது காலநிலை மாற்றம் ஏற்கனவே மிகுந்த தாக்கம் செலுத்துகிறது," என ஆய்வின் இணை ஆசிரியர் மற்றும் University College London-இன் சூழலக நிபுணர் டிம் நியூபோல்ட் கூறுகிறார். உலகளவில் சுமார் 35% உணவு பயிர்கள் மற்றும் நான்கில் மூன்றில் மலர்கள் பூச்சி மற்றும் முல்லூங்கு Pollinators-இல் சார்ந்திருக்கின்றன என அமெரிக்க வேளாண்மை துறை கூறுகிறது. Pollinators குறைவாக்கம் குறித்து, முக்கியமான வெப்பமண்டல பயிர்கள், குறிப்பாக காபி மற்றும் கோகோ, தோன்றி வளர Pollinators-க்கு சார்ந்திருப்பதால் விளைச்சல் குறைக்கும் அபாயம் உள்ளது. முந்தைய ஆய்வுகள் பூச்சிகள் குறைவதேற்கான காரணங்கள் காலநிலை மாற்றம் மற்றும் வாழ்விடம் இழப்பு என்று கூறின. தற்போது ஆழமான தாக்கங்கள் இரண்டு காரணிகளும் ஒன்றாக இணைவதால் மேலும் மோசமாகும் என இப்புதிய ஆய்வு காட்டுகிறது. The quick delivery forced Stephanie's father to pull over on the roadside. As her parents spoke only Spanish, Stephanie communicated with a 911 operator and calmly translated the emergency instructions. Following the steps, she made sure her newborn sister was safe in her mother's arms and checked that the umbilical cord was not wrapped around the baby’s neck, all while remaining composed. Her steadfastness in a stressful moment reflects her ambition to become a nurse in the future.

article_content: Jimmy and Rosalynn Carter were the longest-married presidential couple, having married in 1946 when he was 21 and she was 18. Rosalynn Carter, the former First Lady of the United States and trusted adviser to Jimmy Carter during his presidency, has died at age 96. The Carter Center announced on Sunday that she died peacefully at her home in Plains, Georgia, surrounded by family, after living with dementia and experiencing months of declining health. In a statement, Jimmy Carter said, “Rosalynn was my equal partner in everything I ever accomplished. She gave me wise guidance and encouragement when I needed it. As long as Rosalynn was in the world, I always knew somebody loved and supported me.” After his presidential term ended in 1981, Carter enjoyed more post-White House years than any previous president, with Rosalynn playing an instrumental role during those years. She contributed significantly to the Carter Center and Habitat for Humanity. Initially seen as unassuming before coming to Washington in 1977, Rosalynn developed into an eloquent speaker, campaigner, and activist. Her passion for mental health advocacy extended far beyond her time as First Lady, driven by a belief in the importance of the cause. Before Jimmy Carter’s election in 1976, Rosalynn was not widely known outside Georgia, where Jimmy had been both a peanut farmer and governor. Carter served one four-year term as a Democrat, losing his 1980 re-election bid to Ronald Reagan, a Republican and former California governor and Hollywood actor. In Washington, the Carters were a close team, with Jimmy Carter referring to Rosalynn as “an extension of myself” and his closest adviser. She often attended Cabinet meetings and political strategy sessions as an observer. In a 1978 interview, Carter said he shared almost everything with his wife except top-secret information, noting her understanding of public sentiment. As First Lady, Rosalynn also undertook important official missions to Latin America and was involved in the campaign for ratification of the Equal Rights Amendment, which sought to guarantee equal treatment for women under the law. During the Iranian hostage crisis, when American diplomats were held captive in Tehran, Carter sought to resolve the situation rather than campaign for re-election. In support, Rosalynn spoke in 112 cities across 34 states during a 44-day tour, helping Carter defeat Ted Kennedy in the 1980 primaries, though he ultimately lost to Reagan in the general election. Rosalynn’s commitment to mental health started in the early 1970s, as she recognized the challenges faced by those with mental illness in Georgia. As First Lady of Georgia, she served on a governor’s commission focused on improving services for the mentally ill.

article_content: Cartoon characters, including Disney princesses like Ariel and Snow White, as well as TV favorites like Marge Simpson and Olive Oyl, have been reimagined as victims of domestic violence in a new series of striking artworks. The project was created by contemporary artist and activist AleXsandro Palombo to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, held annually on November 25th. These artworks show well-known female cartoon characters with visible injuries such as black eyes and bloodied noses, presenting a powerful image to highlight the issue of domestic abuse. Characters including Lois from Family Guy and Wilma Flintstone also appear, each holding a picture of their partner labeled 'coward,' emphasizing that domestic abuse is not heroic. The art collection, titled 'Coward,' aims to increase awareness about violence against women. The International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, organized by the United Nations, launches 16 days of activism that culminate on December 10th, Human Rights Day. According to the UN, 35% of women and girls globally experience physical or sexual violence in their lifetimes, with rates even higher in some countries. Palombo explained that the date, November 25th, was chosen to honor the Mirabal sisters, political activists from the Dominican Republic who were assassinated in 1960 under Rafael Trujillo's dictatorship. Palombo stated, 'Thousands of women are killed every year all over the world. Femicide is an unacceptable social issue. As a man, I feel ashamed of the behaviors of those who use violence against women. These individuals are not men but cowards. It's up to real men to stand up and fight against them.' The United Nations campaign also encourages the public to 'Orange YOUR Neighbourhood' by reaching out to local communities, lighting up landmarks in orange, displaying orange flags and ribbons, and organizing marches to raise awareness and discuss solutions to end violence against women.

'Orange YOUR Neighbourhood' என்ற இயக்கத்தில் மக்கள் அனைவரும் உள்ளூர் சமூகத்துடன் இணைந்து ஆரஞ்சு நிற ஒளி, கொடி, ரிப்பன் ஆகியவற்றை இடங்களில் நடத்தி விழிப்புணர்வு இயக்கங்கள் மற்றும் தீர்வுகள் குறித்து விவாதிக்குமாறு ஊக்குவிக்கின்றது.

article_content: Jee Young Lee, a visionary Korean artist, turns her small Seoul studio into fantastical, surreal set pieces for her long-running ‘Stage of Mind’ project. Since it began in 2007, Lee has been meticulously building each scene by hand, drawing inspiration from fairy tales, folklore, dreams, and her own life experiences. Unlike traditional photographers, she constructs every detail—acting as designer, sculptor, performer, and photographer—all within a compact studio measuring just 360 by 410 by 240 centimeters. Her photos burst with vibrant colors, bold patterns, and materials chosen to convey narratives from both Asian and Western heritage. Lee’s works reference Korean proverbs and legends, as well as famous Western stories and personal childhood memories. Every creation is intimately linked to her emotional and psychological journey, often exploring questions of identity and transformation. Among her recognized pieces is ‘I’ll Be Back,’ which visually adapts a Korean tale about children escaping a tiger with divine help. Here, Lee depicts a hand reaching out amid swirling blue fans, symbolizing danger and hope. ‘My Chemical Romance’ represents complex relationships with a tangled maze of pipes. ‘Broken Heart’ uses the Korean saying about breaking a stone with an egg to show resilience in adversity. In ‘The Last Supper,’ a nod to Da Vinci, rats race for a piece of cheese, reflecting competition for scarce resources. The work ‘Resurrection’ is inspired by the Korean novel Shim Cheong and John Everett Millais’s Ophelia, both telling stories of women facing loss and rebirth, which resonates with Lee’s own experiences. She also pulls from her childhood, as seen in ‘Panic Room’ and ‘Treasure Hunt’—the latter creating a lush, imaginative world shaped over three months. ‘Monsoon Season’ reflects on her studio flooding, capturing the chaos and the challenge of enduring hardship. Lee’s photographic style aligns her with postmodern artists who fashion their own realities, similar to Thomas Demand. For her, the process is about self-exploration—each piece a visual answer to personal questions about who she is and how she relates to her environment. A Hongik University graduate, Lee has received significant accolades, such as the Sovereign Art Prize 2012, establishing her as a leading name among new Korean artists.

Like many in the media and political spheres, I first learned via Twitter that Mitt Romney had chosen Paul Ryan as his vice-presidential running mate. The news broke between 11 p.m. and midnight on a Friday, quickly confirmed by multiple news outlets on Twitter—TV networks, newspapers, and wire services. Like many journalists, I stayed up late writing about the decision, filing my copy over the next three hours. The next morning, I was so tired I nearly slept through the actual announcement in Norfolk, Virginia.

It was nearly 12 hours after the story broke that I first switched on my TV. In today’s fast-moving world, it’s clear: cable TV is no longer where news breaks—it hasn’t been for years. Social media platforms have replaced cable news as the go-to for breaking updates, just as cable news once displaced afternoon newspapers.

This shift blurs the lines between reporters, sources, and the public. Experts often share analysis directly online rather than exclusively through journalists. For over a century, journalists bridged the gap between sources and audiences, but the Internet now connects producers and consumers more directly—be it products or information.

Cable TV still offers live global news coverage. During major events—like protests in Tahrir Square or California wildfires—people tune in. Yet such events are rare, and even this advantage may not last. With camera phones, anyone can capture newsworthy footage. Much of the video from Syria, for example, comes directly from locals and is distributed to networks willing to purchase or exchange it.

So what should cable news do in this environment? Three things:
1) Accept that viewers tune in for personalities, not just information. Unless there’s a compelling personality or reason, people won’t watch cable news.
2) Go upmarket. Out of 311 million Americans, just two to five million watch cable news at peak times. This audience is typically curious and well-informed, deserving of thoughtful content. The broader market for lightweight entertainment is already served elsewhere.
3) Go deep and long. Cable news has abundant airtime but often fills it with artificial urgency. Online, people use video to educate and engage—see TED Talks, Big Think, and documentaries like 'Inside Job.' Websites like SecondDraft.org offer video corrections of misleading news. Thoughtful, longer interviews, as seen on C-SPAN, reveal more than confrontational segments.

Adapting a legacy industry is hard, as discussed in 'Barbarians at the Gate.' But adaptation is necessary. These views represent my own—David Frum.

A Bangladeshi villager has her photograph and signature captured and stored in a vast digital database. As digital transformation swiftly reshapes societies worldwide, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) stands out as a crucial force. Operating across 170 countries, the UNDP plays a unique role at the intersection of technology, governance, and social welfare, leading digital initiatives that address challenges from poverty eradication to climate change.

At the energetic Web Summit in Lisbon, UNDP’s Chief Digital Officer, Robert Opp, discussed the complexities of leveraging digital technologies for social progress, especially in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. "The pandemic truly exposed both the weaknesses and strengths of every country’s digital infrastructure. As nations worked to maintain social distancing, establish COVID tracing, and support immunization efforts online, the need for robust digital systems became clear," Opp explained.

The UNDP responded to a surge in requests from countries seeking help to develop specific digital tools like health databases and vaccine tracking systems. In India, for example, the UNDP supported the rapid development of a nationwide COVID vaccine tracking system that eventually covered hundreds of millions, utilizing pre-existing digital infrastructure. However, many nations soon recognized the need for more comprehensive and long-term digital transformation strategies.

"Countries without national policies in this space reached out for support. We would share insights, resources, and experiences from other countries. Our framework, called inclusive digital transformation, means prioritizing citizens and ensuring everyone benefits from digital progress," said Opp.

He elaborated on the importance of 'digital public infrastructure'—building shared digital platforms and services for societal benefit. Comparing it to traditional infrastructure like roads, railways, and power grids, Opp emphasized that just as these structures powered economic growth, digital foundations can drive innovation and inclusion. He highlighted India's success in rolling out Aadhaar digital IDs and a robust digital payments platform, which together extended essential services to over a billion people and increased financial inclusion.

Achieving broad digital transformation requires more than infrastructure—it demands attention to factors such as internet access, digital literacy, and affordability. The UNDP’s approach is to advance connectivity and digital skills at the same time, not in sequence. In Bangladesh, this meant establishing thousands of digital access points in rural areas run by local entrepreneurs. Even those without personal connectivity could use these centers to access government services, such as passport applications.

Such initiatives demonstrate that bridging the digital divide and rolling out online services can occur together. Still, challenges persist. Technology often moves faster than policy, and AI’s potential to widen inequalities is a strong concern. “A major worry,” Opp noted, “is that countries with stronger AI capabilities will progress rapidly while others risk falling behind.”

To confront these disparities, UNDP supports local innovation through its 91 Accelerator Labs, though retaining tech talent remains a challenge as many seek opportunities abroad. Another significant issue is the lack of representative datasets from underrepresented regions, meaning AI systems might not serve all communities equally. “The internet is saturated with English-language content, mostly from North America and Europe. Regions like Sub-Saharan Africa or less wealthy areas are far less represented,” Opp observed.

Promoting open-source tools and data is one approach to redressing these inequalities—a digital commons to level the field globally. Ultimately, making AI’s benefits accessible to all requires cooperative action between public and private sectors to ensure no group is left behind. “We need an honest global conversation on harnessing AI for everyone’s benefit, not just a select few,” Opp urged.

ஒரு பங்களாதேஷ் கிராமவாசியின் புகைப்படமும் கையொப்பமும் ஒரு பெரிய டிஜிட்டல் தரவுத்தளத்தில் பதிவு செய்யப்படுகிறது. உலகம் முழுவதும் டிஜிட்டல் மாற்றம் societies-ஐ வேகமாக மாற்றிக்கொண்டிருக்கும் இந்த காலத்தில், ஐக்கிய நாடுகள் மேம்பாட்டு திட்டம் (UNDP) முக்கிய சக்தியாக விளங்குகிறது. 170 நாடுகளில் இயங்கும் இந்த அமைப்பு, தொழில்நுட்பம், நிர்வாகம் மற்றும் சமூக நலன் ஆகியவற்றின் சந்திப்பில் தனித்துவமான பங்கு வகிக்கிறது. ஏழ்மை நீக்கம் முதல் காலநிலை மாற்றம் வரை பல சவால்களுக்கு டிஜிட்டல் முயற்சிகளை நடத்துகிறது.

லிஸ்‌பனில் நடந்த Web Summit-ல், UNDP-வின் தலைமை டிஜிட்டல் அதிகாரி ராபர்ட் ஆப், சமீபத்திய COVID-19 பரவலுக்குப் பின் சமூக முன்னேற்றத்திற்கு டிஜிட்டலின் பங்களிப்பை விவாதித்தார். "இந்த பாண்டமிக் ஒவ்வொரு நாட்டின் டிஜிட்டல் கட்டமைப்பின் பலவீனங்களும் வலிமைகளும் வெளிச்சம் பார்க்க வைத்தது. சமூக இடைவெளிவை கையாள இனைவு, COVID தடுப்பு மற்றும் தடுப்பூசி ஆதரவுக்கான ஆன்லைன் முயற்சிகள் அதிகம் நடைபெற்றது – இதில் வலுவான டிஜிட்டல் அமைப்பு அவசியமென தெரிந்தது," என்றார் ஆப்.

UNDP பல நாடுகளிடம் குறுஞ்செய்திகள், சுகாதார தரவுத்தளங்கள், தடுப்பூசி கண்காணிப்புகள் ஆகியவை உருவாக்க உதவிப் பெற அதிக வினாக்களைப் பெற்றது. இந்தியாவில், UNDP ஏற்கனவே இருந்த டிஜிட்டல் அமைப்பை பயன்படுத்தி கோடிக்கணக்கான மக்களுக்கு தேசிய தடுப்பூசி கண்காணிப்பு அமைப்பை விரைவில் உருவாக்க உதவியது. இதைத் தவிர, பல நாடுகள் நீண்டகால மற்றும் விரிவான டிஜிட்டல் மாற்றத்தின் அவசியத்தை உணர்ந்தன.

"இந்த துறையில் தேசிய கொள்கை இல்லாத நாடுகள் எங்களிடம் உதவிக் கேட்டன. நாங்கள் அனுபவங்களும், ஆதாரங்களும், பிற நாட்டுகளின் அறிவையும் வழங்கினோம். நாங்கள் கொண்டு செல்லும் 'ஒற்றுமை மிக்க டிஜிட்டல் மாற்றம்' என்ற கட்டமைப்பு, பயனாளிகளுக்கு முன்னுரிமை அளித்து, எல்லோருக்கும் பயனடைய வைத்தல் என்பதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டது," என்றார் ஆப்.

'டிஜிட்டல் பொது உட்கட்டமைப்பு' என்னும் கருத்தை அவர் விளக்கினார் – சமூக நலனுக்காக மையம் கொண்டுள்ள பகிரப்பட்ட டிஜிட்டல் பிளாட்பார்ம் மற்றும் சேவைகள். பழைய கட்டமைப்புகள் (வழிகள், ரயில்வே, மின் விநியோகம்) பொருளாதாரம் வளர்ச்சிக்கு உதவியது போலவே, டிஜிட்டல் அடித்தளங்கள் புதுமை மற்றும் உள்ளடக்கம் தரும் என்றார். இந்தியாவின் ஆதார் மற்றும் பரவலான டிஜிட்டல் பேமென்ட் திட்டங்களின் வெற்றி இதற்கு எடுத்துக்காட்டாகும்.

இந்த மாதிரிக் கூட்டு முயற்சிகள், டிஜிட்டல் பாகுபாடையும் ஆன்லைன் சேவைகளையும் ஒரே நேரத்தில் விரிவுபடுத்த முடியும் என்பதைக் காட்டுகிறது. ஆனால் சவால்கள் இன்னும் இருக்கின்றன. தொழில்நுட்பம் நடைபெற்றூங்கும் வேகம் கொள்கையை விட அதிகம்; ஏ.ஐ. ஏற்றத்தாழ்வை பெருக்கக்கூடும் என்று ஆப் கவலை தெரிவித்தார்.

இந்த சமச்சீர் கூடிய சமுதாயத்திற்காக UNDP அதன் 91 ஆக்கீராசர் ஆய்வகங்களை நடத்துகிறது; குறிப்பாக உள்ளூர் திறமையை நிலைநிறுத்துவது இன்னும் கடினம், ஏனெனில் பலர் வெளிநாட்டை நாடுகிறார்கள். ஒரு முக்கிய பிரச்சினை – குறைந்தபட்சமான பகுதிகளில் தரவுகள் குறைவு. இணையம் பெரும்பாலும் ஆங்கில உள்ளடக்கத்தால் நிரம்பியுள்ளது, குறிப்பாக வட அமெரிக்காவும் ஐரோப்பாவும். சில பகுதி நாடுகள் (sub-Saharan Africa போல) இதில் போதிய பங்காற்றவில்லை என்று ஆப் கூறினார்.

திறந்த மூலத்தரவு மற்றும் கருவிகளை ஊக்குவிப்பது இந்த சமத்தை ஏற்படுத்தும் ஒரு வழி – உலகளாவிய தளத்தில் சமத்துவத்தை ஏற்படுத்துகிறது. இறுதியாக, அனைத்து மக்களும் ஏ.ஐ.யின் பங்குதொடரும் வகையில், பொது மற்றும் தனியார் துறைகள் இணைந்து செயல்பட வேண்டும். "ஏ.ஐ. பயன்பாட்டை அனைவருக்கும் பயன்படுத்தும்படி சத்தியமான உரையாடல் தேவை," என்றார் ஆப்.
